        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.243.17">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17.<span class="headnote">Border state registry fee.</span></h2>
          <p>The initial application fee for border state registration is $50. Any subsequent notice of employment change to remain or be reinstated on the registry is $50.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.243.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/1/9/#laws.5.7.0">1Sp2011 c 9 art 5 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.148.25"><b>148.25</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/242/#laws.0.14.0">1945 c 242 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.251">
        <h1 class="shn">148.251 NURSING PROGRAM.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.251.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Initial approval.</span></h2>
          <p>An institution desiring to conduct a nursing program shall apply to the board and submit evidence that:</p>
          <p>(1) It is prepared to provide a program of theory and practice in advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing that meets the program approval standards adopted by the board. Instruction and required experience may be obtained in one or more institutions or agencies outside the applying institution as long as the nursing program retains accountability for all clinical and nonclinical teaching.</p>
          <p>(2) It is prepared to meet other standards established by law and by the board.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.251.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/194/#laws.0.22.0">1989 c 194 s 22</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.251.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Continuing approval.</span></h2>
          <p>From time to time as deemed necessary by the board, it shall be the duty of the board, through its representatives, to survey all nursing programs in the state. If the results of the survey show that a nursing program meets all board rules, the board shall continue approval of the nursing program.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.251.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Loss of approval.</span></h2>
          <p>If the board determines that an approved nursing program is not maintaining the standards required by the statutes and board rules, notice thereof in writing specifying the defect shall be given to the program. If a program fails to correct these conditions to the satisfaction of the board within a reasonable time, approval of the program shall be revoked and the program shall be removed from the list of approved nursing programs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.251.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Reinstatement of approval.</span></h2>
          <p>The board shall reinstate approval of a nursing program upon submission of satisfactory evidence that its program of theory and practice meets the standards required by statutes and board rules.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.251.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Advanced standing.</span></h2>
          <p>Associate degree nursing programs approved or seeking to be approved by the board shall provide for advanced standing for licensed practical nurses in recognition of their nursing education and experience.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.251.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/242/#laws.0.9.0">1945 c 242 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1961/0/56/#laws.0.2.0">1961 c 56 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/360/#laws.0.8.0">1975 c 360 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/94/#laws.0.7.0">1981 c 94 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/194/#laws.0.11.0">1989 c 194 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/235/#laws.0.28.0">2014 c 235 s 28</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.148.26"><b>148.26</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/242/#laws.0.14.0">1945 c 242 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.261">
        <h1 class="shn">148.261 GROUNDS FOR DISCIPLINARY ACTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.261.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Grounds listed.</span></h2>
          <p>The board may deny, revoke, suspend, limit, or condition the license and registration of any person to practice advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.285">148.285</a>, or to otherwise discipline a licensee or applicant as described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.262">148.262</a>. The following are grounds for disciplinary action:</p>
          <p>(1) Failure to demonstrate the qualifications or satisfy the requirements for a license contained in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.285">148.285</a> or rules of the board. In the case of a person applying for a license, the burden of proof is upon the applicant to demonstrate the qualifications or satisfaction of the requirements.</p>
          <p>(2) Employing fraud or deceit in procuring or attempting to procure a permit, license, or registration certificate to practice advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing or attempting to subvert the licensing examination process. Conduct that subverts or attempts to subvert the licensing examination process includes, but is not limited to:</p>
          <p>(i) conduct that violates the security of the examination materials, such as removing examination materials from the examination room or having unauthorized possession of any portion of a future, current, or previously administered licensing examination;</p>
          <p>(ii) conduct that violates the standard of test administration, such as communicating with another examinee during administration of the examination, copying another examinee's answers, permitting another examinee to copy one's answers, or possessing unauthorized materials; or</p>
          <p>(iii) impersonating an examinee or permitting an impersonator to take the examination on one's own behalf.</p>
          <p>(3) Conviction of a felony or gross misdemeanor reasonably related to the practice of professional, advanced practice registered, or practical nursing. Conviction as used in this subdivision includes a conviction of an offense that if committed in this state would be considered a felony or gross misdemeanor without regard to its designation elsewhere, or a criminal proceeding where a finding or verdict of guilt is made or returned but the adjudication of guilt is either withheld or not entered.</p>
          <p>(4) Revocation, suspension, limitation, conditioning, or other disciplinary action against the person's professional or practical nursing license or advanced practice registered nursing credential, in another state, territory, or country; failure to report to the board that charges regarding the person's nursing license or other credential are pending in another state, territory, or country; or having been refused a license or other credential by another state, territory, or country.</p>
          <p>(5) Failure to or inability to perform professional or practical nursing as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171#stat.148.171.14">148.171, subdivision 14</a> or 15, with reasonable skill and safety, including failure of a registered nurse to supervise or a licensed practical nurse to monitor adequately the performance of acts by any person working at the nurse's direction.</p>
          <p>(6) Engaging in unprofessional conduct, including, but not limited to, a departure from or failure to conform to board rules of professional or practical nursing practice that interpret the statutory definition of professional or practical nursing as well as provide criteria for violations of the statutes, or, if no rule exists, to the minimal standards of acceptable and prevailing professional or practical nursing practice, or any nursing practice that may create unnecessary danger to a patient's life, health, or safety. Actual injury to a patient need not be established under this clause.</p>
          <p>(7) Failure of an advanced practice registered nurse to practice with reasonable skill and safety or departure from or failure to conform to standards of acceptable and prevailing advanced practice registered nursing.</p>
          <p>(8) Delegating or accepting the delegation of a nursing function or a prescribed health care function when the delegation or acceptance could reasonably be expected to result in unsafe or ineffective patient care.</p>
          <p>(9) Actual or potential inability to practice nursing with reasonable skill and safety to patients by reason of illness, use of alcohol, drugs, chemicals, or any other material, or as a result of any mental or physical condition.</p>
          <p>(10) Adjudication as mentally incompetent, mentally ill, a chemically dependent person, or a person dangerous to the public by a court of competent jurisdiction, within or without this state.</p>
          <p>(11) Engaging in any unethical conduct, including, but not limited to, conduct likely to deceive, defraud, or harm the public, or demonstrating a willful or careless disregard for the health, welfare, or safety of a patient. Actual injury need not be established under this clause.</p>
          <p>(12) Engaging in conduct with a patient that is sexual or may reasonably be interpreted by the patient as sexual, or in any verbal behavior that is seductive or sexually demeaning to a patient, or engaging in sexual exploitation of a patient or former patient.</p>
          <p>(13) Obtaining money, property, or services from a patient, other than reasonable fees for services provided to the patient, through the use of undue influence, harassment, duress, deception, or fraud.</p>
          <p>(14) Revealing a privileged communication from or relating to a patient except when otherwise required or permitted by law.</p>
          <p>(15) Engaging in abusive or fraudulent billing practices, including violations of federal Medicare and Medicaid laws or state medical assistance laws.</p>
          <p>(16) Improper management of patient records, including failure to maintain adequate patient records, to comply with a patient's request made pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291">144.291</a> to 144.298, or to furnish a patient record or report required by law.</p>
          <p>(17) Knowingly aiding, assisting, advising, or allowing an unlicensed person to engage in the unlawful practice of advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing.</p>
          <p>(18) Violating a rule adopted by the board, an order of the board, or a state or federal law relating to the practice of advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing, or a state or federal narcotics or controlled substance law.</p>
          <p>(19) Knowingly providing false or misleading information that is directly related to the care of that patient unless done for an accepted therapeutic purpose such as the administration of a placebo.</p>
          <p>(20) Aiding suicide or aiding attempted suicide in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.215">609.215</a> as established by any of the following:</p>
          <p>(i) a copy of the record of criminal conviction or plea of guilty for a felony in violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.215#stat.609.215.1">609.215, subdivision 1</a> or 2;</p>
          <p>(ii) a copy of the record of a judgment of contempt of court for violating an injunction issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.215#stat.609.215.4">609.215, subdivision 4</a>;</p>
          <p>(iii) a copy of the record of a judgment assessing damages under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.215#stat.609.215.5">609.215, subdivision 5</a>; or</p>
          <p>(iv) a finding by the board that the person violated section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.215#stat.609.215.1">609.215, subdivision 1</a> or 2. The board shall investigate any complaint of a violation of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.215#stat.609.215.1">609.215, subdivision 1 </a>or 2.</p>
          <p>(21) Practicing outside the scope of practice authorized by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171#stat.148.171.5">148.171, subdivision 5</a>, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, or 21.</p>
          <p>(22) Making a false statement or knowingly providing false information to the board, failing to make reports as required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.263">148.263</a>, or failing to cooperate with an investigation of the board as required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.265">148.265</a>.</p>
          <p>(23) Engaging in false, fraudulent, deceptive, or misleading advertising.</p>
          <p>(24) Failure to inform the board of the person's certification or recertification status as a certified registered nurse anesthetist, certified nurse-midwife, certified nurse practitioner, or certified clinical nurse specialist.</p>
          <p>(25) Engaging in clinical nurse specialist practice, nurse-midwife practice, nurse practitioner practice, or registered nurse anesthetist practice without a license and current certification or recertification by a national nurse certification organization acceptable to the board.</p>
          <p>(26) Failing to report employment to the board as required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.211#stat.148.211.2a">148.211, subdivision 2a</a>, or knowingly aiding, assisting, advising, or allowing a person to fail to report as required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.211#stat.148.211.2a">148.211, subdivision 2a</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.261.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Conviction of a felony-level criminal sexual offense.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided in paragraph (e), the board may not grant or renew a license to practice nursing to any person who has been convicted on or after August 1, 2014, of any of the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.342#stat.609.342.1">609.342, subdivision 1</a> or 1a, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.343#stat.609.343.1">609.343, subdivision 1</a> or 1a, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.344#stat.609.344.1">609.344, subdivision 1</a>, or subdivision 1a, clauses (c) to (i), or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.345#stat.609.345.1">609.345, subdivision 1</a>, or subdivision 1a, clauses (c) to (i), or a similar statute in another jurisdiction.</p>
          <p>(b) A license to practice nursing is automatically revoked if the licensee is convicted of an offense listed in paragraph (a).</p>
          <p>(c) A license to practice nursing that has been denied or revoked under this subdivision is not subject to chapter 364.</p>
          <p>(d) For purposes of this subdivision, "conviction" means a plea of guilty, a verdict of guilty by a jury, or a finding of guilty by the court, unless the court stays imposition or execution of the sentence and final disposition of the case is accomplished at a nonfelony level.</p>
          <p>(e) The board may establish criteria whereby an individual convicted of an offense listed in paragraph (a) may become licensed provided that the criteria:</p>
          <p>(1) utilize a rebuttable presumption that the applicant is not suitable for licensing;</p>
          <p>(2) provide a standard for overcoming the presumption; and</p>
          <p>(3) require that a minimum of ten years has elapsed since the applicant's sentence was discharged.</p>
          <p>The board shall not consider an application under this paragraph if the board determines that the victim involved in the offense was a patient or a client of the applicant at the time of the offense.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.261.1b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.<span class="headnote">Reproductive health care services.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this subdivision, "reproductive health care services" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/147.091">147.091, subdivision </a>1c.</p>
          <p>(b) Notwithstanding subdivision 1, clause (3) or (4), the board shall not refuse to grant a license to an applicant for licensure or impose disciplinary action against a nurse solely on one or more of the following grounds:</p>
          <p>(1) the applicant or nurse provided or assisted in the provision of reproductive health care services in a manner that is lawful in this state and that is within the applicable scope of practice;</p>
          <p>(2) the applicant or nurse was convicted in another jurisdiction of a felony resulting from conduct specified in clause (1); or</p>
          <p>(3) the applicant or nurse was subject to disciplinary action in another jurisdiction or was refused a license to practice advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing in another jurisdiction resulting from conduct specified in clause (1).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.261.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/222/#laws.0.209.0">1976 c 222 s 209</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.261.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/194/#laws.0.22.0">1989 c 194 s 22</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.261.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Evidence.</span></h2>
          <p>In disciplinary actions alleging a violation of subdivision 1, clause (3) or (4), or subdivision 1a, a copy of the judgment or proceeding under the seal of the court administrator or of the administrative agency that entered the same shall be admissible into evidence without further authentication and shall constitute prima facie evidence of the violation concerned.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.261.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Examination; access to medical data.</span></h2>
          <p>The board may take the following actions if it has probable cause to believe that grounds for disciplinary action exist under subdivision 1, clause (9) or (10):</p>
          <p>(a) It may direct the applicant or nurse to submit to a mental or physical examination or substance use disorder evaluation. For the purpose of this subdivision, when a nurse licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.285">148.285</a> is directed in writing by the board to submit to a mental or physical examination or substance use disorder evaluation, that person is considered to have consented and to have waived all objections to admissibility on the grounds of privilege. Failure of the applicant or nurse to submit to an examination when directed constitutes an admission of the allegations against the applicant or nurse, unless the failure was due to circumstances beyond the person's control, and the board may enter a default and final order without taking testimony or allowing evidence to be presented. A nurse affected under this paragraph shall, at reasonable intervals, be given an opportunity to demonstrate that the competent practice of professional, advanced practice registered, or practical nursing can be resumed with reasonable skill and safety to patients. Neither the record of proceedings nor the orders entered by the board in a proceeding under this paragraph, may be used against a nurse in any other proceeding.</p>
          <p>(b) It may, notwithstanding sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.384">13.384</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.651">144.651</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/595.02">595.02</a>, or any other law limiting access to medical or other health data, obtain medical data and health records relating to a registered nurse, advanced practice registered nurse, licensed practical nurse, or applicant for a license without that person's consent. The medical data may be requested from a provider, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291#stat.144.291.2">144.291, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (i), an insurance company, or a government agency, including the Department of Human Services. A provider, insurance company, or government agency shall comply with any written request of the board under this subdivision and is not liable in any action for damages for releasing the data requested by the board if the data are released pursuant to a written request under this subdivision unless the information is false and the provider giving the information knew, or had reason to believe, the information was false. Information obtained under this subdivision is classified as private data on individuals as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02">13.02</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.261.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/242/#laws.0.10.0">1945 c 242 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/360/#laws.0.9.0">1975 c 360 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/222/#laws.0.55.0">1976 c 222 s 55</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/194/#laws.0.12.0">1989 c 194 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/464/#laws.1.56.0">1992 c 464 art 1 s 56</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/559/#laws.1.4.0">1992 c 559 art 1 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/577/#laws.0.3.0">1992 c 577 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/88/#laws.0.5.0">1993 c 88 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/172/#laws.0.6.0">1999 c 172 s 6</a>,7,18; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/227/#laws.0.22.0">1999 c 227 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/272/#laws.0.2.0">2002 c 272 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.10.15.0">2007 c 147 art 10 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/278/#laws.2.11.0">2012 c 278 art 2 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/235/#laws.0.29.0">2014 c 235 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.4.8.0">2014 c 291 art 4 s 8</a>,9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/83/#laws.2.9.0">2020 c 83 art 2 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/11/#laws.4.31.0">1Sp2021 c 11 art 4 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/98/#laws.4.51.0">2022 c 98 art 4 s 51</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/31/#laws.0.4.0">2023 c 31 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.4.77.0">2023 c 70 art 4 s 77</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.262">
        <h1 class="shn">148.262 FORMS OF DISCIPLINARY ACTION; AUTOMATIC SUSPENSION; TEMPORARY SUSPENSION; REISSUANCE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.262.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Forms of disciplinary action.</span></h2>
          <p>When the board finds that grounds for disciplinary action exist under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.261#stat.148.261.1">148.261, subdivision 1</a>, it may take one or more of the following actions:</p>
          <p>(1) deny the license, registration, or registration renewal;</p>
          <p>(2) revoke the license;</p>
          <p>(3) suspend the license;</p>
          <p>(4) impose limitations on the nurse's practice of advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing including, but not limited to, limitation of scope of practice or the requirement of practice under supervision;</p>
          <p>(5) impose conditions on the retention of the license including, but not limited to, the imposition of retraining or rehabilitation requirements or the conditioning of continued practice on demonstration of knowledge or skills by appropriate examination, monitoring, or other review;</p>
          <p>(6) impose a civil penalty not exceeding $10,000 for each separate violation, the amount of the civil penalty to be fixed as to deprive the nurse of any economic advantage gained by reason of the violation charged, to reimburse the board for the cost of counsel, investigation, and proceeding, and to discourage repeated violations;</p>
          <p>(7) order the nurse to provide unremunerated service;</p>
          <p>(8) censure or reprimand the nurse; or</p>
          <p>(9) any other action justified by the facts in the case.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.262.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Automatic suspension.</span></h2>
          <p>Unless the board orders otherwise, a license to practice advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing is automatically suspended if:</p>
          <p>(1) a guardian of a nurse is appointed by order of a court under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/524.5-101">524.5-101 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/524.5-502">524.5-502</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) the nurse is committed by order of a court under chapter 253B; or</p>
          <p>(3) the nurse is determined to be mentally incompetent, mentally ill, chemically dependent, or a person dangerous to the public by a court of competent jurisdiction within or without this state.</p>
          <p>The license remains suspended until the nurse is restored to capacity by a court and, upon petition by the nurse, the suspension is terminated by the board after a hearing or upon agreement between the board and the nurse.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.262.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Temporary suspension of license.</span></h2>
          <p>In addition to any other remedy provided by law, the board may, through its designated board member under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.10#stat.214.10.2">214.10, subdivision 2</a>, temporarily suspend the license of a nurse without a hearing if the board finds that there is probable cause to believe the nurse has violated a statute or rule the board is empowered to enforce and continued practice by the nurse would create a serious risk of harm to others. The suspension shall take effect upon written notice to the nurse, served by first-class mail, specifying the statute or rule violated. The suspension shall remain in effect until the board issues a temporary stay of suspension or a final order in the matter after a hearing or upon agreement between the board and the nurse. At the time it issues the suspension notice, the board shall schedule a disciplinary hearing to be held under the Administrative Procedure Act. The nurse shall be provided with at least 20 days' notice of any hearing held under this subdivision. The hearing shall be scheduled to begin no later than 30 days after the issuance of the suspension order.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.262.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Reissuance.</span></h2>
          <p>The board may reinstate and reissue a license or registration certificate to practice advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing, but as a condition may impose any disciplinary or corrective measure that it might originally have imposed. Any person whose license or registration has been revoked, suspended, or limited may have the license reinstated and a new registration issued when, in the discretion of the board, the action is warranted, provided that the person shall be required by the board to pay the costs of the proceedings resulting in the revocation, suspension, or limitation of the license or registration certificate and reinstatement of the license or registration certificate, and to pay the fee for the current registration period. The cost of proceedings shall include, but not be limited to, the cost paid by the board to the Office of Administrative Hearings and the Office of the Attorney General for legal and investigative services, the costs of a court reporter and witnesses, reproduction of records, board staff time, travel, and expenses, and board members' per diem reimbursements, travel costs, and expenses.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.262.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/194/#laws.0.13.0">1989 c 194 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/1/1/#laws.2.8.0">1Sp1994 c 1 art 2 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/172/#laws.0.8.0">1999 c 172 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/146/#laws.3.47.0">2004 c 146 art 3 s 47</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/235/#laws.0.30.0">2014 c 235 s 30</a>-32</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.263">
        <h1 class="shn">148.263 REPORTING OBLIGATIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.263.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Permission to report.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who has knowledge of any conduct constituting grounds for discipline under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.285">148.285</a> may report the alleged violation to the board.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.263.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Institutions.</span></h2>
          <p>The chief nursing executive or chief administrative officer of any hospital, clinic, prepaid medical plan, or other health care institution or organization located in this state shall report to the board any action taken by the institution or organization or any of its administrators or committees to revoke, suspend, limit, or condition a nurse's privilege to practice in the institution, or as part of the organization, any denial of privileges, any dismissal from employment, or any other disciplinary action. The institution or organization shall also report the resignation of any nurse before the conclusion of any disciplinary proceeding, or before commencement of formal charges, but after the nurse had knowledge that formal charges were contemplated or in preparation. The reporting described by this subdivision is required only if the action pertains to grounds for disciplinary action under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.261">148.261</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.263.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Licensed professionals.</span></h2>
          <p>A person licensed by a health-related licensing board as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.01#stat.214.01.2">214.01, subdivision 2</a>, shall report to the board personal knowledge of any conduct the person reasonably believes constitutes grounds for disciplinary action under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.285">148.285</a> by any nurse including conduct indicating that the nurse may be incompetent, may have engaged in unprofessional or unethical conduct, or may be mentally or physically unable to engage safely in the practice of professional, advanced practice registered, or practical nursing.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.263.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Insurers.</span></h2>
          <p>Four times each year, by the first day of February, May, August, and November, each insurer authorized to sell insurance described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/60A.06#stat.60A.06.1">60A.06, subdivision 1</a>, clause (13), and providing professional liability insurance to registered nurses, advanced practice registered nurses, or licensed practical nurses shall submit to the board a report concerning any nurse against whom a malpractice award has been made or who has been a party to a settlement. The report must contain at least the following information:</p>
          <p>(1) the total number of settlements or awards;</p>
          <p>(2) the date settlement or award was made;</p>
          <p>(3) the allegations contained in the claim or complaint leading to the settlement or award;</p>
          <p>(4) the dollar amount of each malpractice settlement or award and whether that amount was paid as a result of a settlement or of an award; and</p>
          <p>(5) the name and address of the practice of the nurse against whom an award was made or with whom a settlement was made.</p>
          <p>An insurer shall also report to the board any information it possesses that tends to substantiate a charge that a nurse may have engaged in conduct violating sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.285">148.285</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.263.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Courts.</span></h2>
          <p>The court administrator of district court or another court of competent jurisdiction shall report to the board any judgment or other determination of the court that adjudges or includes a finding that a nurse is a person who is mentally ill, mentally incompetent, chemically dependent, dangerous to the public, guilty of a felony or gross misdemeanor, guilty of a violation of federal or state narcotics laws or controlled substances act, guilty of operating a motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance, or guilty of an abuse or fraud under Medicare or Medicaid, appoints a guardian of the nurse under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/524.5-101">524.5-101</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/524.5-502">524.5-502</a>, or commits a nurse under chapter 253B.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.263.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Deadlines; forms.</span></h2>
          <p>Reports required by subdivisions 2 to 5 must be submitted no later than 30 days after the occurrence of the reportable event or transaction. The board may provide forms for the submission of reports required by this section, may require that the reports be submitted on the forms provided, and may adopt rules necessary to assure prompt and accurate reporting. The board shall review all reports, including those submitted after the deadline.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.263.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Failure to report.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">On or after August 1, 2012, any person, institution, insurer, or organization that fails to report as required under subdivisions 2 to 5 shall be subject to civil penalties for failing to report as required by law.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.263.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/194/#laws.0.14.0">1989 c 194 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/1/1/#laws.2.9.0">1Sp1994 c 1 art 2 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/172/#laws.0.9.0">1999 c 172 s 9</a>,10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/221/#laws.0.2.0">2002 c 221 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/146/#laws.3.47.0">2004 c 146 art 3 s 47</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/278/#laws.2.12.0">2012 c 278 art 2 s 12</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.264">
        <h1 class="shn">148.264 IMMUNITY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.264.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Reporting.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person, health care facility, business, or organization is immune from civil liability or criminal prosecution for submitting in good faith a report to the board under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.263">148.263</a> or for otherwise reporting in good faith to the board violations or alleged violations of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.285">148.285</a>. All such reports are investigative data as defined in chapter 13.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.264.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Investigation.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Members of the board and persons employed by the board or engaged in the investigation of violations and in the preparation and management of charges of violations of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.285">148.285</a> on behalf of the board or persons participating in the investigation or testifying regarding charges of violations are immune from civil liability and criminal prosecution for any actions, transactions, or publications in the execution of, or relating to, their duties under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.285">148.285</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) Members of the board and persons employed by the board or engaged in maintaining records and making reports regarding adverse health care events are immune from civil liability and criminal prosecution for any actions, transactions, or publications in the execution of or relating to their duties under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.267">148.267</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.264.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/194/#laws.0.15.0">1989 c 194 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/186/#laws.0.7.0">2004 c 186 s 7</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.265">
        <h1 class="shn">148.265 NURSE COOPERATION.</h1>
        <p>A nurse who is the subject of an investigation by or on behalf of the board shall cooperate fully with the investigation. Cooperation includes responding fully and promptly to any question raised by or on behalf of the board relating to the subject of the investigation and providing copies of patient or other records in the nurse's possession, as reasonably requested by the board, to assist the board in its investigation and to appear at conferences and hearings scheduled by the board. The board shall pay for copies requested. If the board does not have a written consent from a patient permitting access to the patient's records, the nurse shall delete any data in the record that identify the patient before providing it to the board. The board shall maintain any records obtained pursuant to this section as investigative data under chapter 13. The nurse shall not be excused from giving testimony or producing any documents, books, records, or correspondence on the grounds of self-incrimination, but the testimony or evidence may not be used against the nurse in any criminal case.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.265.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/194/#laws.0.16.0">1989 c 194 s 16</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.266">
        <h1 class="shn">148.266 DISCIPLINARY RECORD ON JUDICIAL REVIEW.</h1>
        <p>Upon judicial review of any board disciplinary action taken under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.285">148.285</a>, the reviewing court shall seal the administrative record, except for the board's final decision, and shall not make the administrative record available to the public.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.266.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/194/#laws.0.17.0">1989 c 194 s 17</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.267">
        <h1 class="shn">148.267 REPORTS TO COMMISSIONER OF HEALTH.</h1>
        <p>(a) The board shall maintain a record of an event that comes to the board's attention that, in the judgment of the board or a committee of the board, qualifies as an adverse health care event under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7065">144.7065</a>.</p>
        <p>(b) Within 30 days of making a determination under paragraph (a) that an event qualifies as an adverse health care event, the board shall forward to the commissioner of health a report of the event, including the facility involved, the date of the event, and information known to the board regarding the event. The report shall not include any identifying information for any of the health care professionals, facility employees, or patients involved.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.267.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/186/#laws.0.8.0">2004 c 186 s 8</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.148.27"><b>148.27</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/242/#laws.0.14.0">1945 c 242 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.271">
        <h1 class="shn">148.271 EXEMPTIONS.</h1>
        <p>The provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.285">148.285</a> shall not prohibit:</p>
        <p>(1) The furnishing of nursing assistance in an emergency.</p>
        <p>(2) The practice of advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing by any legally qualified advanced practice, registered, or licensed practical nurse of another state who is employed by the United States government or any bureau, division, or agency thereof while in the discharge of official duties.</p>
        <p>(3) The practice of any profession or occupation licensed by the state, other than advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing, by any person duly licensed to practice the profession or occupation, or the performance by a person of any acts properly coming within the scope of the profession, occupation, or license.</p>
        <p>(4) The provision of a nursing or nursing-related service by an unlicensed assistive person who has been delegated or assigned the specific function and is supervised by a registered nurse or monitored by a licensed practical nurse.</p>
        <p>(5) The care of the sick with or without compensation when done in a nursing home covered by the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.09#stat.144A.09.1">144A.09, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
        <p>(6) Professional nursing practice or advanced practice registered nursing practice by a registered nurse or practical nursing practice by a licensed practical nurse licensed in another state or territory who is in Minnesota as a student enrolled in a formal, structured course of study, such as a course leading to a higher degree, certification in a nursing specialty, or to enhance skills in a clinical field, while the student is practicing in the course.</p>
        <p>(7) Professional or practical nursing practice by a student practicing under the supervision of an instructor while the student is enrolled in a nursing program approved by the board under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.251">148.251</a>.</p>
        <p>(8) Advanced practice registered nursing as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171, subdivisions 5, 10, 11, 13, and 21</a>, by a registered nurse who is licensed and currently registered in Minnesota or another United States jurisdiction and who is enrolled as a student in a formal graduate education program leading to eligibility for certification and licensure as an advanced practice registered nurse.</p>
        <p>(9) Professional nursing practice or advanced practice registered nursing practice by a registered nurse or advanced practice registered nurse licensed in another state, territory, or jurisdiction who is in Minnesota temporarily:</p>
        <p>(i) providing continuing or in-service education;</p>
        <p>(ii) serving as a guest lecturer;</p>
        <p>(iii) presenting at a conference; or</p>
        <p>(iv) teaching didactic content via distance education to a student located in Minnesota who is enrolled in a formal, structured course of study, such as a course leading to a higher degree or certification in a nursing specialty.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.271.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/242/#laws.0.11.0">1945 c 242 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/140/#laws.0.2.0">1959 c 140 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/360/#laws.0.10.0">1975 c 360 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/256/#laws.0.1.0">1977 c 256 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/94/#laws.0.8.0">1981 c 94 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/194/#laws.0.18.0">1989 c 194 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/172/#laws.0.11.0">1999 c 172 s 11</a>,18; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/31/#laws.0.10.0">2013 c 31 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/235/#laws.0.33.0">2014 c 235 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/125/#laws.0.9.0">2016 c 125 s 9</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.148.272"><b>148.272</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/194/#laws.0.22.0">1989 c 194 s 22</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.148.28"><b>148.28</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/242/#laws.0.14.0">1945 c 242 s 14</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.281">
        <h1 class="shn">148.281 VIOLATIONS; PENALTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.281.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Violations described.</span></h2>
          <p>It shall be unlawful for any person, corporation, firm, or association, to:</p>
          <p>(1) sell or fraudulently obtain or furnish any nursing diploma, license or record, or aid or abet therein;</p>
          <p>(2) practice advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing or practice as a public health nurse under cover of any diploma, permit, license, registration certificate, advanced practice credential, or record illegally or fraudulently obtained or signed or issued unlawfully or under fraudulent representation;</p>
          <p>(3) practice advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing unless the person has been issued a temporary permit under the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.212">148.212</a> or is duly licensed and currently registered to do so under the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.285">148.285</a>;</p>
          <p>(4) use the professional title nurse unless duly licensed to practice advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing under the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.285">148.285</a>, except as authorized by the board by rule;</p>
          <p>(5) use any abbreviation or other designation tending to imply licensure as an advanced practice registered nurse, a registered nurse, or a licensed practical nurse unless duly licensed and currently registered so to practice advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing under the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.285">148.285</a> except as authorized by the board by rule;</p>
          <p>(6) use any title, abbreviation, or other designation tending to imply certification as a certified registered nurse as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171#stat.148.171.22">148.171, subdivision 22</a>, unless duly certified by a national nurse certification organization;</p>
          <p>(7) use any abbreviation or other designation tending to imply registration as a public health nurse unless duly registered by the board;</p>
          <p>(8) practice advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing in a manner prohibited by the board in any limitation of a license or registration issued under the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.285">148.285</a>;</p>
          <p>(9) practice advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing during the time a license or current registration issued under the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.285">148.285</a> shall be suspended or revoked;</p>
          <p>(10) conduct a nursing program for the education of persons to become advanced practice registered nurses, registered nurses, or licensed practical nurses unless the program has been approved by the board; and</p>
          <p>(11) knowingly employ persons in the practice of advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing who have not been issued a current permit, license, or registration certificate to practice as a nurse in this state.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.281.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/194/#laws.0.22.0">1989 c 194 s 22</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.281.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person, corporation, or association violating any provisions of subdivision 1 shall be guilty of a gross misdemeanor, and shall be punished according to law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.281.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Penalty; advanced practice registered nurses.</span></h2>
          <p>In addition to subdivision 2, an advanced practice registered nurse who practices advanced practice registered nursing without a current license and certification or recertification shall pay a penalty fee of $200 for the first month or part of a month and an additional $100 for each subsequent month or parts of months of practice. The amount of the penalty fee shall be calculated from the first day the advanced practice registered nurse practiced without a current advanced practice registered nurse license and certification to the last day of practice without a current license and certification, or from the first day the advanced practice registered nurse practiced without a current license and certification on file with the board until the day the current license and certification is filed with the board.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.281.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/242/#laws.0.12.0">1945 c 242 s 12</a>,13; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/140/#laws.0.4.0">1959 c 140 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/360/#laws.0.11.0">1975 c 360 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/256/#laws.0.2.0">1977 c 256 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/194/#laws.0.19.0">1989 c 194 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/172/#laws.0.12.0">1999 c 172 s 12</a>,18; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/87/#laws.0.6.0">2003 c 87 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/235/#laws.0.34.0">2014 c 235 s 34</a>,35</p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.148.282"><b>148.282</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/360/#laws.0.25.0">1975 c 360 s 25</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.283">
        <h1 class="shn">148.283 UNAUTHORIZED PRACTICE OF PROFESSIONAL, ADVANCED PRACTICE REGISTERED, AND PRACTICAL NURSING.</h1>
        <p>The practice of advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing by any person who has not been licensed to practice advanced practice, professional, or practical nursing under the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.171">148.171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.285">148.285</a>, or whose license has been suspended or revoked, or whose registration or national credential has expired, is hereby declared to be inimical to the public health and welfare and to constitute a public nuisance. Upon a complaint being made by the board or any prosecuting officer, and upon a proper showing of the facts, the district court of the county where such practice occurred may enjoin such acts and practice. Such injunction proceeding shall be in addition to, and not in lieu of, all other penalties and remedies provided by law.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.283.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/140/#laws.0.6.0">1959 c 140 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/194/#laws.0.20.0">1989 c 194 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/172/#laws.0.13.0">1999 c 172 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/235/#laws.0.36.0">2014 c 235 s 36</a></p>
      </div>

      <div class="section" id="stat.148.285">
        <h1 class="shn">148.285 TRANSFER OF ASSETS.</h1>
        <p>All money, property, and property rights belonging to and under the control of the board of examiners, are hereby transferred and appropriated to the control and use of the board hereunder and the purpose provided herein.</p>
      </div>

      <h1 class="fgh">SPEECH-LANGUAGE PATHOLOGISTS<br>AND AUDIOLOGISTS</h1>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.148.511"><b>148.511</b> MS 1971 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/62/#laws.0.4.0">1974 c 62 s 4</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.511">
        <h1 class="shn">148.511 SCOPE.</h1>
        <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a> apply to persons who are applicants for licensure, who use protected titles, who represent that they are licensed, or who engage in the practice of speech-language pathology or audiology or practice as a speech-language pathology assistant. Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a> do not apply to school personnel licensed by the Professional Educator Licensing and Standards Board and practicing within the scope of their school license under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/8710.6000">8710.6000</a>, or the paraprofessionals who assist these individuals.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.511.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/363/#laws.0.1.0">1996 c 363 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/7/#laws.0.34.0">2001 c 7 s 34</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/87/#laws.0.7.0">2003 c 87 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/279/#laws.1.1.0">2004 c 279 art 1 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/147/#laws.7.19.0">2005 c 147 art 7 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/5/#laws.12.22.0">1Sp2017 c 5 art 12 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.25.2.0">2024 c 127 art 25 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>The amendment to this section by Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 2, is effective July 1, 2025. Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 2, the effective date.</p>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.512">
        <h1 class="shn">148.512 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purpose of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>, the following terms have the meanings given to them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Accredited educational institution.</span></h2>
          <p>"Accredited educational institution" means a university or college that offers speech-language pathology or audiology graduate degrees and that is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology, a body recognized by the United States Department of Education, or an equivalent as determined by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Advisory council.</span></h2>
          <p>"Advisory council" means the Minnesota Speech-Language Pathologist and Audiologist Advisory Council established under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.13#stat.214.13.4">214.13, subdivision 4</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Applicant.</span></h2>
          <p>"Applicant" means a person who applies to the commissioner for licensure or licensure renewal.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Continuing education sponsor.</span></h2>
          <p>"Continuing education sponsor" means an organization that offers a learning experience designed to promote continuing competency in the procedures and techniques of the practice of speech-language pathology or audiology and whose activities meet the criteria in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5193#stat.148.5193.2">148.5193, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Audiologist.</span></h2>
          <p>"Audiologist" means a natural person who engages in the practice of audiology, meets the qualifications required by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>, and is licensed by the commissioner under a general, clinical fellowship, doctoral externship, or temporary license. Audiologist also means a natural person using any descriptive word with the title audiologist.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>"Commissioner" means the commissioner of health or a designee.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Contact hour.</span></h2>
          <p>"Contact hour" means an instructional session of 60 consecutive minutes, excluding coffee breaks, registration, meals without a speaker, and social activities.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Continuing education.</span></h2>
          <p>"Continuing education" is a planned learning experience in speech-language pathology or audiology not including the basic educational program leading to a degree if the education is used by the licensee for credit to achieve a baccalaureate or master's degree in speech-language pathology or audiology.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Credential.</span></h2>
          <p>"Credential" means a license, permit, certification, registration, or other evidence of qualification or authorization to engage in the practice of speech-language pathology or audiology issued by any authority.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.10a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10a.<span class="headnote">Hearing aid.</span></h2>
          <p>"Hearing aid" means a prescribed aid, or any of its parts, worn in the ear canal and designed to or represented as being able to aid human hearing. "Hearing aid" includes the aid's parts, attachments, or accessories, including, but not limited to, ear molds and behind the ear (BTE) devices with or without an ear mold. Batteries and cords are not parts, attachments, or accessories of a hearing aid. Surgically implanted hearing aids, and assistive listening devices not worn within the ear canal, are not hearing aids.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.10b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10b.<span class="headnote">Hearing aid dispensing.</span></h2>
          <p>"Hearing aid dispensing" means making ear mold impressions, prescribing a hearing aid, assisting the consumer in prescription aid selection, or testing human hearing in connection with these activities regardless of whether the person conducting these activities has a monetary interest in the dispensing of prescription hearing aids to the consumer. Hearing aid dispensing does not include selling over-the-counter hearing aids.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.10c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10c.<span class="headnote">Over-the-counter hearing aid or OTC hearing aid.</span></h2>
          <p>"Over-the-counter hearing aid" or "OTC hearing aid" has the meaning given to that term in Code of Federal Regulations, title 21, section 800.30(b).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/87/#laws.0.53.0">2003 c 87 s 53</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Practice of audiology.</span></h2>
          <p>The "practice of audiology" means:</p>
          <p>(1) identification, assessment, and interpretation, diagnosis, rehabilitation, and prevention of hearing disorders;</p>
          <p>(2) conservation of the auditory system function; development and implementation of hearing conservation programs;</p>
          <p>(3) measurement, assessment, and interpretation of auditory and vestibular function;</p>
          <p>(4) selecting, fitting, and dispensing of assistive listening devices, alerting and amplification devices, and systems for personal and public use, including hearing aids and devices, and providing training in their use;</p>
          <p>(5) aural habilitation and rehabilitation and related counseling for individuals who are deaf, deafblind, and hard-of-hearing and their families;</p>
          <p>(6) screening of speech, language, voice, or fluency for the purposes of audiologic evaluation or identification of possible communication disorders; or</p>
          <p>(7) supervision of the functions in clauses (1) to (6).</p>
          <p>The practice of audiology does not include the practice of medicine and surgery, or osteopathic medicine and surgery, or medical diagnosis that is commonly performed by a physician.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Practice of speech-language pathology.</span></h2>
          <p>The "practice of speech-language pathology" means:</p>
          <p>(1) identification, assessment, and interpretation, diagnosis, habilitation, rehabilitation, treatment and prevention of disorders of speech, articulation, fluency, voice, and language;</p>
          <p>(2) identification, assessment, and interpretation, diagnosis, habilitation, and rehabilitation of disorders of oral-pharyngeal function and related disorders;</p>
          <p>(3) identification, assessment, and interpretation, diagnosis, habilitation, and rehabilitation of communication disorders associated with cognition;</p>
          <p>(4) assessing, selecting, and developing augmentative and alternative communication systems and providing training in their use;</p>
          <p>(5) aural habilitation and rehabilitation and related counseling for individuals who are deaf, deafblind, and hard-of-hearing and their families;</p>
          <p>(6) enhancing speech-language proficiency and communication effectiveness;</p>
          <p>(7) screening individuals for hearing loss or middle ear pathology for the purposes of speech-language evaluation or for the identification of possible hearing disorders; or</p>
          <p>(8) supervision of the functions in clauses (1) to (7).</p>
          <p>The practice of speech-language pathology does not include the practice of medicine and surgery, or osteopathic medicine and surgery, or medical diagnosis that is commonly performed by a physician.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.13a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13a.<span class="headnote">Prescription hearing aid.</span></h2>
          <p>"Prescription hearing aid" means a hearing aid requiring a prescription from a certified hearing aid dispenser or licensed audiologist that is not an OTC hearing aid.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">License or licensed.</span></h2>
          <p>"License" or "licensed" means the act or status of a person who meets the requirements of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.15">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">Licensee.</span></h2>
          <p>"Licensee" means an individual who meets the requirements of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.16">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.<span class="headnote">Licensure.</span></h2>
          <p>"Licensure" is the system of regulation defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.001#stat.214.001.3">214.001, subdivision 3</a>, clause (3), and is the process specified in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.17">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17.<span class="headnote">Speech-language pathologist.</span></h2>
          <p>"Speech-language pathologist" means a person who practices speech-language pathology, meets the qualifications under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>, and is licensed by the commissioner. Speech-language pathologist also means a natural person using, as an occupational title, a term identified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.513">148.513</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.17a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17a.<span class="headnote">Speech-language pathology assistant.</span></h2>
          <p>"Speech-language pathology assistant" means a person who meets the qualifications under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5181">148.5181</a> and provides speech-language pathology services under the supervision of a licensed speech-language pathologist in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5192">148.5192</a>.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.18">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 18.<span class="headnote">Supervisee.</span></h2>
          <p>"Supervisee" means a person who, under the direction or evaluation of a supervisor, is:</p>
          <p>(1) engaging in the supervised practice of speech-language pathology or audiology;</p>
          <p>(2) performing a function of supervised clinical training as a student of speech-language pathology or audiology; or</p>
          <p>(3) performing a function of supervised postgraduate or doctoral clinical experience in speech-language pathology or audiology.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.19">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 19.<span class="headnote">Supervision.</span></h2>
          <p>"Supervision" means the direct or indirect evaluation or direction of:</p>
          <p>(1) a practitioner of speech-language pathology or audiology;</p>
          <p>(2) a person performing a function of supervised clinical training as a student of speech-language pathology or audiology;</p>
          <p>(3) a person performing a function of supervised postgraduate clinical experience in speech-language pathology or audiology; or</p>
          <p>(4) a speech-language pathology assistant in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5192">148.5192</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.512.20">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 20.<span class="headnote">Supervisor.</span></h2>
          <p>"Supervisor" means a person who has the authority to direct or evaluate a supervisee and who:</p>
          <p>(1) is a licensed speech-language pathologist or audiologist under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.515">148.515</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.516">148.516</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.517">148.517</a>; or</p>
          <p>(2) when the commissioner determines that supervision by a licensed speech-language pathologist or audiologist as required in clause (1) is unobtainable, and in other situations considered appropriate by the commissioner, is a person practicing speech-language pathology or audiology who holds a current certificate of clinical competence from the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association or board certification in audiology by the American Board of Audiology.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.512.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/363/#laws.0.2.0">1996 c 363 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/460/#laws.0.22.0">2000 c 460 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/87/#laws.0.8.0">2003 c 87 s 8</a>-20; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/279/#laws.1.2.0">2004 c 279 art 1 s 2</a>-6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/147/#laws.7.1.0">2005 c 147 art 7 s 1</a>-3,19; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/189/#laws.0.5.0">2008 c 189 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/157/#laws.1.3.0">2009 c 157 art 1 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/62/#laws.0.7.0">2013 c 62 s 7</a>,8; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/0/40/#laws.1.35.0">2017 c 40 art 1 s 35</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.3.36.0">2023 c 70 art 3 s 36</a>-39; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.25.3.0">2024 c 127 art 25 s 3</a></p>
      </div>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>The amendment to subdivision 17a by Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 3, is effective July 1, 2025. Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 3, the effective date.</p>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.513">
        <h1 class="shn">148.513 LICENSURE; PROTECTED TITLES AND RESTRICTIONS ON USE; EXEMPTIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.513.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Unlicensed practice prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>A person must not engage in the practice of speech-language pathology or audiology or practice as a speech-language pathology assistant unless the person is licensed as a speech-language pathologist, an audiologist, or a speech-language pathology assistant under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>. For purposes of this subdivision, a speech-language pathology assistant's duties are limited to the duties described in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5192#stat.148.5192.2">148.5192, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.513.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Protected titles and restrictions on use; speech-language pathologists and audiologists.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Notwithstanding paragraph (c), the use of the following terms or initials which represent the following terms, alone or in combination with any word or words, by any person to form an occupational title is prohibited unless that person is licensed as a speech-language pathologist or audiologist under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>:</p>
          <p>(1) speech-language;</p>
          <p>(2) speech-language pathologist, S, SP, or SLP;</p>
          <p>(3) speech pathologist;</p>
          <p>(4) language pathologist;</p>
          <p>(5) audiologist, A, or AUD;</p>
          <p>(6) speech therapist;</p>
          <p>(7) speech clinician;</p>
          <p>(8) speech correctionist;</p>
          <p>(9) language therapist;</p>
          <p>(10) voice therapist;</p>
          <p>(11) voice pathologist;</p>
          <p>(12) logopedist;</p>
          <p>(13) communicologist;</p>
          <p>(14) aphasiologist;</p>
          <p>(15) phoniatrist;</p>
          <p>(16) audiometrist;</p>
          <p>(17) audioprosthologist;</p>
          <p>(18) hearing therapist;</p>
          <p>(19) hearing clinician; or</p>
          <p>(20) hearing aid audiologist.</p>
          <p>(b) Use of the term "Minnesota licensed" in conjunction with the titles protected under paragraph (a) by any person is prohibited unless that person is licensed as a speech-language pathologist or audiologist under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) A speech-language pathology assistant practicing under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a> must not represent, indicate, or imply to the public that the assistant is a licensed speech-language pathologist and shall only utilize the titles provided in subdivision 2b.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.513.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Hearing aid dispensers.</span></h2>
          <p>An audiologist must not hold out as a licensed hearing aid dispenser.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.513.2b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2b.<span class="headnote">Protected titles and restrictions on use; speech-language pathology assistant.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The use of the following terms or initials which represent the following terms, alone or in combination with any word or words, by any person to form an occupational title is prohibited unless that person is licensed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5181">148.5181</a>:</p>
          <p>(1) speech-language pathology assistant;</p>
          <p>(2) SLP assistant; or</p>
          <p>(3) SLP asst.</p>
