        <p>(J) If no written notice of intent to attend the public hearing by interested parties is received, the commission may proceed with promulgation of the proposed rule without a public hearing.</p>
        <p>(K) The commission shall, by majority vote of all members, take final action on the proposed rule and shall determine the effective date of the rule, if any, based on the rulemaking record and the full text of the rule.</p>
        <p>(L) Upon determination that an emergency exists, the commission may consider and adopt an emergency rule without prior notice, opportunity for comment, or hearing; provided that the usual rulemaking procedures provided in the compact and in this Article shall be retroactively applied to the rule as soon as reasonably possible, in no event later than 90 days after the effective date of the rule. For the purposes of this provision, an emergency rule is one that must be adopted immediately in order to:</p>
        <p>(1) meet an imminent threat to public health, safety, or welfare;</p>
        <p>(2) prevent a loss of commission or member state funds; or</p>
        <p>(3) meet a deadline for the promulgation of an administrative rule that is established by federal law or rule.</p>
        <p>(M) The commission or an authorized committee of the commission may direct revisions to a previously adopted rule or amendment for purposes of correcting typographical errors, errors in format, errors in consistency, or grammatical errors. Public notice of any revisions shall be posted on the website of the commission. The revision shall be subject to challenge by any person for a period of 30 days after posting. The revision may be challenged only on grounds that the revision results in a material change to a rule. A challenge shall be made in writing and delivered to the chair of the commission prior to the end of the notice period. If no challenge is made, the revision shall take effect without further action. If the revision is challenged, the revision may not take effect without the approval of the commission.</p>
        <p class="ce">ARTICLE X</p>
        <p class="ce">OVERSIGHT, DISPUTE RESOLUTION, AND ENFORCEMENT</p>
        <p>(A) Dispute Resolution:</p>
        <p>(1) Upon request by a member state, the commission shall attempt to resolve disputes related to the compact that arise among member states and between member and nonmember states.</p>
        <p>(2) The commission shall promulgate a rule providing for both mediation and binding dispute resolution for such disputes as appropriate.</p>
        <p>(B) Enforcement:</p>
        <p>(1) The commission, in the reasonable exercise of its discretion, shall enforce the provisions and rules of this compact.</p>
        <p>(2) By majority vote, the commission may initiate legal action in the United States District Court for the District of Columbia or the federal district where the commission has its principal offices against a member state in default to enforce compliance with the provisions of the compact and its promulgated rules and bylaws. The relief sought may include both injunctive relief and damages. In the event judicial enforcement is necessary, the prevailing member shall be awarded all costs of litigation, including reasonable attorney's fees.</p>
        <p>(3) The remedies herein shall not be the exclusive remedies of the commission. The commission may pursue any other remedies available under federal or state law.</p>
        <p class="ce">ARTICLE XI</p>
        <p class="ce">DATE OF IMPLEMENTATION OF THE INTERSTATE COMMISSION FOR AUDIOLOGY AND SPEECH-LANGUAGE PATHOLOGY PRACTICE AND ASSOCIATED RULES, WITHDRAWAL, AND AMENDMENT</p>
        <p>(A) The compact shall come into effect on the date on which the compact statute is enacted into law in the tenth member state. The provisions, which become effective at that time, shall be limited to the powers granted to the commission relating to assembly and the promulgation of rules. Thereafter, the commission shall meet and exercise rulemaking powers necessary to the implementation and administration of the compact.</p>
        <p>(B) Any state that joins the compact subsequent to the commission's initial adoption of the rules shall be subject to the rules as they exist on the date on which the compact becomes law in that state. Any rule that has been previously adopted by the commission shall have the full force and effect of law on the day the compact becomes law in that state.</p>
        <p>(C) Any member state may withdraw from this compact by enacting a statute repealing the same.</p>
        <p>(1) A member state's withdrawal shall not take effect until six months after enactment of the repealing statute.</p>
        <p>(2) Withdrawal shall not affect the continuing requirement of the withdrawing state's audiology or speech-language pathology licensing board to comply with the investigative and adverse action reporting requirements of this compact prior to the effective date of withdrawal.</p>
        <p>(D) Nothing contained in this compact shall be construed to invalidate or prevent any audiology or speech-language pathology licensure agreement or other cooperative arrangement between a member state and a nonmember state that does not conflict with the provisions of this compact.</p>
        <p>(E) This compact may be amended by the member states. No amendment to this compact shall become effective and binding upon any member state until it is enacted into the laws of all member states.</p>
        <p class="ce">ARTICLE XII</p>
        <p class="ce">CONSTRUCTION AND SEVERABILITY</p>
        <p>This compact shall be liberally construed so as to effectuate the purposes thereof. The provisions of this compact shall be severable and if any phrase, clause, sentence, or provision of this compact is declared to be contrary to the constitution of any member state or of the United States or the applicability thereof to any government, agency, person, or circumstance is held invalid, the validity of the remainder of this compact and the applicability thereof to any government, agency, person, or circumstance shall not be affected thereby. If this compact shall be held contrary to the constitution of any member state, the compact shall remain in full force and effect as to the remaining member states and in full force and effect as to the member state affected as to all severable matters.</p>
        <p class="ce">ARTICLE XIII</p>
        <p class="ce">BINDING EFFECT OF COMPACT AND OTHER LAWS</p>
        <p>(A) Nothing herein prevents the enforcement of any other law of a member state that is not inconsistent with the compact.</p>
        <p>(B) All laws in a member state in conflict with the compact are superseded to the extent of the conflict.</p>
        <p>(C) All lawful actions of the commission, including all rules and bylaws promulgated by the commission, are binding upon the member states.</p>
        <p>(D) All agreements between the commission and the member states are binding in accordance with their terms.</p>
        <p>(E) In the event any provision of the compact exceeds the constitutional limits imposed on the legislature of any member state, the provision shall be ineffective to the extent of the conflict with the constitutional provision in question in that member state.</p>
      </div>

			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.30.1.0">2024 c 127 art 30 s 1</a>

      <div class="section" id="stat.148.5186">
        <h1 class="shn">148.5186 APPLICATION OF AUDIOLOGY AND SPEECH-LANGUAGE PATHOLOGY INTERSTATE COMPACT TO EXISTING LAWS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5186.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Rulemaking.</span></h2>
          <p>Rules developed by the Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology Compact Commission under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5185">148.5185</a> are not subject to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.05">14.05 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.389">14.389</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5186.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Background studies.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health is authorized to require an audiologist or speech-language pathologist licensed in Minnesota as the home state to submit to a criminal history background check under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.0572">144.0572</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.5186.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.30.2.0">2024 c 127 art 30 s 2</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.519">
        <h1 class="shn">148.519 LICENSURE PROCEDURES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.519.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Applications for licensure; speech-language pathologists and audiologists.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An applicant for licensure as a speech-language pathologist or audiologist must:</p>
          <p>(1) submit a completed application for licensure on forms provided by the commissioner. The application must include the applicant's name, certification number under chapter 153A, if applicable, business address and telephone number, or home address and telephone number if the applicant practices speech-language pathology or audiology out of the home, and a description of the applicant's education, training, and experience, including previous work history for the five years immediately preceding the date of application. The commissioner may ask the applicant to provide additional information necessary to clarify information submitted in the application; and</p>
          <p>(2) submit documentation of the certificate of clinical competence issued by the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association, board certification by the American Board of Audiology, or satisfy the following requirements:</p>
          <p>(i) submit a transcript showing the completion of a master's or doctoral degree or its equivalent meeting the requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.515#stat.148.515.2">148.515, subdivision 2</a>;</p>
          <p>(ii) submit documentation of the required hours of supervised clinical training;</p>
          <p>(iii) submit documentation of the postgraduate clinical or doctoral clinical experience meeting the requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.515#stat.148.515.4">148.515, subdivision 4</a>; and</p>
          <p>(iv) submit documentation of receiving a qualifying score on an examination meeting the requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.515#stat.148.515.6">148.515, subdivision 6</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) In addition, an applicant must:</p>
          <p>(1) sign a statement that the information in the application is true and correct to the best of the applicant's knowledge and belief;</p>
          <p>(2) submit with the application all fees required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5194">148.5194</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) sign a waiver authorizing the commissioner to obtain access to the applicant's records in this or any other state in which the applicant has engaged in the practice of speech-language pathology or audiology; and</p>
          <p>(4) consent to a fingerprint-based criminal history background check as required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.0572">144.0572</a>, pay all required fees, and cooperate with all requests for information. An applicant must complete a new criminal history background check if more than one year has elapsed since the applicant last applied for a license.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.519.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Applications for licensure; speech-language pathology assistants.</span></h2>
          <p>An applicant for licensure as a speech-language pathology assistant must:</p>
          <p>(1) submit a completed application on forms provided by the commissioner. The application must include the applicant's name, business address and telephone number, home address and telephone number, and a description of the applicant's education, training, and experience, including previous work history for the five years immediately preceding the application date. The commissioner may ask the applicant to provide additional information needed to clarify information submitted in the application;</p>
          <p>(2) submit a transcript showing the completion of the requirements set forth in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5181">148.5181</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) submit a signed statement that the information in the application is true and correct to the best of the applicant's knowledge and belief;</p>
          <p>(4) submit all fees required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5194">148.5194</a>;</p>
          <p>(5) submit a signed waiver authorizing the commissioner to obtain access to the applicant's records in this or any other state in which the applicant has worked as a speech-language pathology assistant; and</p>
          <p>(6) consent to a fingerprint-based criminal history background check as required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.0572">144.0572</a>, pay all required fees, and cooperate with all requests for information. An applicant must complete a new criminal history background check if more than one year has lapsed since the applicant last applied for a license.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.519.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Action on applications for licensure.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner shall act on an application for licensure according to paragraphs (b) to (e).</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioner shall determine if the applicant meets the requirements for licensure. The commissioner or advisory council may investigate information provided by an applicant to determine whether the information is accurate and complete.</p>
          <p>(c) The commissioner shall not issue a license to an applicant who refuses to consent to a background study within 90 days after submission of an application or fails to submit fingerprints to the Department of Human Services. Any fees paid by the applicant to the Department of Health shall be forfeited if the applicant refuses to consent to the background study.</p>
          <p>(d) The commissioner shall notify an applicant, via certified mail, of action taken on the application and of the grounds for denying licensure if licensure is denied.</p>
          <p>(e) An applicant denied licensure may make a written request to the commissioner, within 30 days of the date of notification to the applicant, for reconsideration of the denial. Individuals requesting reconsideration may submit information that the applicant wants considered in the reconsideration. After reconsideration of the commissioner's determination to deny licensure, the commissioner shall determine whether the original determination should be affirmed or modified. An applicant may make only one request in any one biennial license period for reconsideration of the commissioner's determination to deny licensure.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.519.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Change of name, employment, and addresses.</span></h2>
          <p>A licensee who changes addresses must inform the commissioner, in writing, of the change of name, employment, or address within 30 days. A change in name must be accompanied by a copy of a marriage certificate or court order. All notices or other correspondence mailed to or served on a licensee by the commissioner at the licensee's address on file with the commissioner shall be considered as having been received by the licensee.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.519.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/363/#laws.0.9.0">1996 c 363 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/87/#laws.0.29.0">2003 c 87 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/189/#laws.0.10.0">2008 c 189 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/158/#laws.1.67.0">2016 c 158 art 1 s 67</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.10.113.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 10 s 113</a>,114; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.25.12.0">2024 c 127 art 25 s 12</a>,13</p>
      </div>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>The amendments to subdivision 1 by Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 12, are effective July 1, 2025. Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 12, the effective date.</p>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>Subdivision 1a, as added by Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 13, is effective July 1, 2025. Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 13, the effective date.</p>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.5191">
        <h1 class="shn">148.5191 LICENSURE RENEWAL.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5191.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Renewal requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>To renew licensure, an applicant for license renewal as a speech-language pathologist or audiologist must:</p>
          <p>(1) biennially complete a renewal application on a form provided by the commissioner and submit the biennial renewal fee;</p>
          <p>(2) meet the continuing education requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5193">148.5193</a> and submit evidence of attending continuing education courses, as required in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5193#stat.148.5193.6">148.5193, subdivision 6</a>; and</p>
          <p>(3) submit additional information if requested by the commissioner to clarify information presented in the renewal application. The information must be submitted within 30 days after the commissioner's request.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5191.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Renewal requirements; speech-language pathology assistant.</span></h2>
          <p>To renew licensure, an applicant for license renewal as a speech-language pathology assistant must:</p>
          <p>(1) biennially complete a renewal application on a form provided by the commissioner and submit the biennial renewal fee;</p>
          <p>(2) meet the continuing education requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5193">148.5193</a>, subdivision 1a, and submit evidence of attending continuing education courses, as required in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5193#stat.148.5193.1a">148.5193, subdivision 1a</a>; and</p>
          <p>(3) submit additional information if requested by the commissioner to clarify information presented in the renewal application. The information must be submitted within 30 days after the commissioner's request.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5191.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Late fee.</span></h2>
          <p>An application submitted after the renewal deadline date must be accompanied by a late fee as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5194#stat.148.5194.4">148.5194, subdivision 4</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5191.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Licensure renewal notice.</span></h2>
          <p>Licensure renewal is on a biennial basis. At least 60 days before the licensure expiration date, the commissioner shall send out a renewal notice to the licensee's last known address. The notice shall include a renewal application and notice of fees required for renewal. If the licensee does not receive the renewal notice, the licensee is still required to meet the deadline for renewal to qualify for continuous licensure status.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5191.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Renewal deadline.</span></h2>
          <p>Each license, including a temporary license provided under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5161">148.5161</a>, must state an expiration date. An application for licensure renewal must be received by the Department of Health or postmarked at least 30 days before the expiration date. If the postmark is illegible, the application shall be considered timely if received at least 21 days before the expiration date.</p>
          <p>When the commissioner establishes the renewal schedule for an applicant, licensee, or temporary licensee, if the period before the expiration date is less than two years, the fee shall be prorated.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.5191.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/363/#laws.0.10.0">1996 c 363 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/317/#laws.0.5.0">1998 c 317 s 5</a>-7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/87/#laws.0.30.0">2003 c 87 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.25.14.0">2024 c 127 art 25 s 14</a>,15</p>
      </div>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>The amendment to subdivision 1 by Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 14, is effective July 1, 2025. Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 14, the effective date.</p>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>Subdivision 1a, as added by Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 15, is effective July 1, 2025. Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 15, the effective date.</p>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.5192">
        <h1 class="shn">148.5192 SPEECH-LANGUAGE PATHOLOGY ASSISTANTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5192.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Delegation requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>A licensed speech-language pathologist may delegate duties to a licensed speech-language pathology assistant in accordance with this section following an initial introduction to a client with the speech-language pathologist and speech-language pathology assistant present.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5192.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Delegated duties; prohibitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A speech-language pathology assistant may perform only those duties delegated by a licensed speech-language pathologist and must be limited to duties within the training and experience of the speech-language pathology assistant.</p>
          <p>(b) Duties may include the following as delegated by the supervising speech-language pathologist:</p>
          <p>(1) assist with speech language and hearing screenings;</p>
          <p>(2) implement documented treatment plans or protocols developed by the supervising speech-language pathologist;</p>
          <p>(3) document client performance, including writing progress notes;</p>
          <p>(4) assist with assessments of clients;</p>
          <p>(5) assist with preparing materials and scheduling activities as directed;</p>
          <p>(6) perform checks and maintenance of equipment;</p>
          <p>(7) support the supervising speech-language pathologist in research projects, in-service training, and public relations programs; and</p>
          <p>(8) collect data for quality improvement.</p>
          <p>(c) A speech-language pathology assistant may not:</p>
          <p>(1) perform standardized or nonstandardized diagnostic tests, perform formal or informal evaluations, or interpret test results;</p>
          <p>(2) demonstrate strategies included in the feeding and swallowing plan developed by the speech-language pathologist or share such information with students, patients, clients, families, staff, and caregivers;</p>
          <p>(3) participate in parent conferences, case conferences, or interdisciplinary team meetings without approval from the speech-language pathologist or misrepresent themselves as a speech-language pathologist at such a conference or meeting. The speech-language pathologist and speech-language pathology assistant are required to meet prior to the parent conferences, case conferences, or interdisciplinary team meetings to determine the information to be shared;</p>
          <p>(4) provide client or family counseling or consult with the client or the family regarding the client status or service;</p>
          <p>(5) write, develop, or modify a client's individualized treatment plan or individualized education program;</p>
          <p>(6) select clients for service;</p>
          <p>(7) discharge clients from service;</p>
          <p>(8) disclose information to other team members without permission from the supervising speech-language pathologist; or</p>
          <p>(9) make referrals for additional services.</p>
          <p>(d) A speech-language pathology assistant must only sign documents, including treatment plans, education plans, reimbursement forms, or reports, when cosigned by the supervising speech-language pathologist. The speech-language pathology assistant must sign or initial all treatment notes written by the assistant, which must then also be cosigned by the supervising speech-language pathologist.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5192.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Supervision requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A supervising speech-language pathologist shall authorize and accept full responsibility for the performance, practice, and activity of a speech-language pathology assistant. The amount and type of supervision required must be based on the skills and experience of the speech-language pathology assistant. A minimum of one hour every 30 days of consultative supervision time must be documented for each speech-language pathology assistant.</p>
          <p>(b) A supervising speech-language pathologist must:</p>
          <p>(1) be licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) hold a certificate of clinical competence from the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association or its equivalent as approved by the commissioner; and</p>
          <p>(3) have completed at least ten hours of continuing education in supervision.</p>
          <p>(c) Once every 60 days, the supervising speech-language pathologist must treat or cotreat with the speech-language pathology assistant each client on the speech-language pathology assistant's caseload.</p>
          <p>(d) For purposes of this section, "direct supervision" means observation and guidance by the supervising speech-language pathologist during the performance of a delegated duty that occurs either on-site and in-view or through the use of real-time, two-way interactive audio and visual communication. The supervision requirements described in this section are minimum requirements. Additional supervision requirements may be imposed at the discretion of the supervising speech-language pathologist.</p>
          <p>(e) A supervising speech-language pathologist must be available to communicate with a speech-language pathology assistant at any time the assistant is in direct contact with a client.</p>
          <p>(f) A supervising speech-language pathologist must document activities performed by the assistant that are directly supervised by the supervising speech-language pathologist. At a minimum, the documentation must include:</p>
          <p>(1) information regarding the quality of the speech-language pathology assistant's performance of the delegated duties; and</p>
          <p>(2) verification that any delegated clinical activity was limited to duties authorized to be performed by the speech-language pathology assistant under this section.</p>
          <p>(g) A supervising speech-language pathologist must review and cosign all informal treatment notes signed or initialed by the speech-language pathology assistant.</p>
          <p>(h) A full-time, speech-language pathologist may supervise no more than two full-time, speech-language pathology assistants or the equivalent of two full-time assistants.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5192.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Notification.</span></h2>
          <p>Any agency or clinic that intends to utilize the services of a speech-language pathology assistant must provide written notification to the client or, if the client is younger than 18 years old, to the client's parent or guardian before a speech-language pathology assistant may perform any of the duties described in this section.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.5192.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/279/#laws.1.14.0">2004 c 279 art 1 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/147/#laws.7.19.0">2005 c 147 art 7 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.25.16.0">2024 c 127 art 25 s 16</a>-18</p>
      </div>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>The amendments to subdivisions 1 to 3 by Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, sections 16 to 18, are effective July 1, 2025. Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, sections 16 to 18, the effective dates.</p>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.5193">
        <h1 class="shn">148.5193 CONTINUING EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5193.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Number of contact hours required; speech-language pathologists and audiologists.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An applicant for licensure renewal as a speech-language pathologist or audiologist must meet the requirements for continuing education stipulated by the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association or the American Board of Audiology, or satisfy the requirements described in paragraphs (b) to (e).</p>
          <p>(b) Within one month following expiration of a license, an applicant for licensure renewal as either a speech-language pathologist or an audiologist must provide evidence to the commissioner of a minimum of 30 contact hours of continuing education obtained within the two years immediately preceding licensure expiration. A minimum of 20 contact hours of continuing education must be directly related to the licensee's area of licensure. Ten contact hours of continuing education may be in areas generally related to the licensee's area of licensure. Licensees who are issued licenses for a period of less than two years shall prorate the number of contact hours required for licensure renewal based on the number of months licensed during the biennial licensure period. Licensees shall receive contact hours for continuing education activities only for the biennial licensure period in which the continuing education activity was performed.</p>
          <p>(c) An applicant for licensure renewal as both a speech-language pathologist and an audiologist must attest to and document completion of a minimum of 36 contact hours of continuing education offered by a continuing education sponsor within the two years immediately preceding licensure renewal. A minimum of 15 contact hours must be received in the area of speech-language pathology and a minimum of 15 contact hours must be received in the area of audiology. Six contact hours of continuing education may be in areas generally related to the licensee's areas of licensure. Licensees who are issued licenses for a period of less than two years shall prorate the number of contact hours required for licensure renewal based on the number of months licensed during the biennial licensure period. Licensees shall receive contact hours for continuing education activities only for the biennial licensure period in which the continuing education activity was performed.</p>
          <p>(d) If the licensee is licensed by the Professional Educator Licensing and Standards Board:</p>
          <p>(1) activities that are approved in the categories of Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/8710.7200">8710.7200</a>, subpart 3, items A and B, and that relate to speech-language pathology, shall be considered:</p>
          <p>(i) offered by a sponsor of continuing education; and</p>
          <p>(ii) directly related to speech-language pathology;</p>
          <p>(2) activities that are approved in the categories of Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/8710.7200">8710.7200</a>, subpart 3, shall be considered:</p>
          <p>(i) offered by a sponsor of continuing education; and</p>
          <p>(ii) generally related to speech-language pathology; and</p>
          <p>(3) one clock hour as defined in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/8710.7200">8710.7200</a>, subpart 1, is equivalent to 1.0 contact hours of continuing education.</p>
          <p>(e) Contact hours may not be accumulated in advance and transferred to a future continuing education period.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5193.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Continuing education; speech-language pathology assistants.</span></h2>
          <p>An applicant for licensure renewal as a speech-language pathology assistant must meet the requirements for continuing education established by the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association and submit evidence of attending continuing education courses. A licensee must receive contact hours for continuing education activities only for the biennial licensure period in which the continuing education activity was completed. Continuing education contact hours obtained in one licensure period must not be transferred to a future licensure period.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5193.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Continuing education provided by sponsors.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner will accept continuing education provided by sponsors if the continuing education activity meets the following standards:</p>
          <p>(1) constitutes an organized program of learning;</p>
          <p>(2) reasonably expects to advance the knowledge and skills of the speech-language pathologist or audiologist;</p>
          <p>(3) pertains to subjects that relate to the practice of speech-language pathology or audiology;</p>
          <p>(4) is conducted by individuals who have education, training, and experience by reason of which said individuals should be considered experts concerning the subject matter of the activity; and</p>
          <p>(5) is presented by a sponsor who has a mechanism to verify participation and maintains attendance records for four years.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5193.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/460/#laws.0.66.0">2000 c 460 s 66</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5193.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Earning continuing education contact hours through contact hour equivalents.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A licensee who teaches continuing education courses or presents or publishes for educational purposes may obtain contact hour equivalents according to paragraphs (b) to (d).</p>
          <p>(b) The sponsor of the course must meet the requirements of subdivision 2.</p>
          <p>(c) A licensee may not obtain more than six contact hours in any two-year continuing education period by teaching continuing education courses.</p>
          <p>(d) A licensee may obtain two contact hours for each hour spent teaching a course. Contact hours may be claimed only once for teaching the same course in any two-year continuing education period.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5193.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/460/#laws.0.66.0">2000 c 460 s 66</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5193.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Records of attendance.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A licensee must maintain for four years records of attending the continuing education contact hours required for licensure renewal.</p>
          <p>(b) An applicant for licensure renewal must submit documentation demonstrating compliance with continuing education requirements of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association or the American Board of Audiology or an equivalent, or the following information on a form provided by the commissioner: the sponsoring organization, the dates of the course, the course name, the number of contact hours completed, and the name and signature of the licensee.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5193.6a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6a.<span class="headnote">Auditing continuing education reports.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner may audit a percentage of the continuing education reports based on random selection. A licensee shall maintain all documentation required by this section for two years after the last day of the biennial licensure period in which the contact hours were earned.</p>
          <p>(b) All renewal applications that are received after the expiration date may be subject to a continuing education report audit.</p>
          <p>(c) Any licensee against whom a complaint is filed may be subject to a continuing education report audit.</p>
          <p>(d) The licensee shall make the following information available to the commissioner for auditing purposes:</p>
          <p>(1) a copy of the completed continuing education report form for the continuing education reporting period that is the subject of the audit including all supporting documentation required by subdivision 5;</p>
          <p>(2) a description of the continuing education activity prepared by the presenter or sponsor that includes the course title or subject matter, date, place, number of program contact hours, presenters, and sponsors;</p>
          <p>(3) documentation of self-study programs by materials prepared by the presenter or sponsor that includes the course title, course description, name of sponsor or author, and the number of hours required to complete the program;</p>
          <p>(4) documentation of university, college, or vocational school courses by a course syllabus, listing in a course bulletin, or equivalent documentation that includes the course title, instructor's name, course dates, number of contact hours, and course content, objectives, or goals; and</p>
          <p>(5) verification of attendance by:</p>
          <p>(i) a signature of the presenter or a designee at the continuing education activity on the continuing education report form or a certificate of attendance with the course name, course date, and licensee's name;</p>
          <p>(ii) a summary or outline of the educational content of an audio or video educational activity to verify the licensee's participation in the activity if a designee is not available to sign the continuing education report form;</p>
          <p>(iii) verification of self-study programs by a certificate of completion or other documentation indicating that the individual has demonstrated knowledge and has successfully completed the program; or</p>
          <p>(iv) verification of attendance at a university, college, or vocational course by an official transcript.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5193.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Verification of continuing education reports.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may request a licensee or continuing education sponsor to verify the continuing education to which the licensee attested. Documentation may come directly from the licensee, the continuing education sponsor, or from a national accrediting or certifying organization which maintains the records.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5193.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Waiver of continuing education requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may grant a waiver of the requirements of this section in cases where the requirements would impose an undue burden on the licensee. A licensee must request in writing a waiver of the requirements of this section. The request for a waiver must cite this section, the reasons for requesting the waiver, the period of time the licensee wishes to have the continuing education requirement waived, and the alternative measures that will be taken if a waiver is granted. The commissioner shall set forth, in writing, the reasons for granting or denying the waiver. Waivers granted by the commissioner shall specify in writing the time limitation and required alternative measures to be taken by the licensee.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.5193.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/363/#laws.0.11.0">1996 c 363 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/460/#laws.0.26.0">2000 c 460 s 26</a>-30; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/87/#laws.0.31.0">2003 c 87 s 31</a>-36; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/279/#laws.1.15.0">2004 c 279 art 1 s 15</a>,16; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/267/#laws.2.8.0">2006 c 267 art 2 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/157/#laws.1.4.0">2009 c 157 art 1 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/274/#laws.0.2.0">2010 c 274 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/5/#laws.12.22.0">1Sp2017 c 5 art 12 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.25.19.0">2024 c 127 art 25 s 19</a>,20</p>
      </div>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>The amendment to subdivision 1 by Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 19, is effective July 1, 2025. Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 19, the effective date. </p>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>Subdivision 1a, as added by Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 20, is effective July 1, 2025. Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 20, the effective date.</p>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.5194">
        <h1 class="shn">148.5194 FEES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5194.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Fee proration.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall prorate the licensure fee for clinical fellowship, doctoral externship, temporary, and first time licensees according to the number of months that have elapsed between the date the license is issued and the date the license expires or must be renewed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5191#stat.148.5191.4">148.5191, subdivision 4</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5194.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Speech-language pathologist licensure fees.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The fee for initial licensure for a speech-language pathologist is $210.50.</p>
          <p>(b) The fee for clinical fellowship licensure, doctoral externship, temporary license, or renewal for a speech-language pathologist is $200.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5194.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote"> Licensure fees for dual licensure as a speech-language pathologist and audiologist.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The fee for initial dual licensure as a speech-language pathologist and audiologist is $523.</p>
          <p>(b) The fee for clinical fellowship licensure, doctoral externship, temporary license, or renewal for dual licensure as a speech-language pathologist and audiologist is $510.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5194.3a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.7.89.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 7 s 89</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5194.3b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3b.<span class="headnote">Speech-language pathology assistant licensure fees.</span></h2>
          <p>The fee for initial licensure as a speech-language pathology assistant is $493. The fee for licensure renewal for a speech-language pathology assistant is $493.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5194.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Penalty fee for late renewals.</span></h2>
          <p>The penalty fee for late submission of a renewal application is $60.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5194.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Use of fees.</span></h2>
          <p>All fees are nonrefundable. The commissioner shall only use fees collected under this section for the purposes of administering this chapter. The legislature must not transfer money generated by these fees from the state government special revenue fund to the general fund.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5194.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Verification of credential.</span></h2>
          <p>The fee for written verification of credentialed status is $25.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5194.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Audiologist biennial licensure fee.</span></h2>
          <p>The licensure fee for initial applicants is $523. The biennial licensure fee for audiologists for clinical fellowship, doctoral externship, temporary, and renewal licenses is $510.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5194.7a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7a.<span class="headnote">Surcharge.</span></h2>
          <p>Speech-language pathologists who were licensed prior to January 1, 2018, shall pay a onetime surcharge of $10.50 to renew when their license first expires after January 1, 2020. Audiologists who were licensed before January 1, 2018, shall pay a onetime surcharge of $13 to renew when their license first expires after January 1, 2020. The surcharge shall cover the commissioner's costs associated with criminal background checks.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5194.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Penalty fees.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The penalty fee for practicing speech-language pathology or audiology, practicing as a speech-language pathology assistant, or using protected titles without a current license after the credential has expired and before it is renewed is the amount of the license renewal fee for any part of the first month, plus the license renewal fee for any part of any subsequent month up to 36 months.</p>
          <p>(b) The penalty fee for applicants who engage in the unauthorized practice of speech-language pathology or audiology, practice as a speech-language pathology assistant, or use of protected titles before being issued a license is the amount of the license application fee for any part of the first month, plus the license application fee for any part of any subsequent month up to 36 months. This paragraph does not apply to applicants not qualifying for a license who engage in the unauthorized practice of speech-language pathology or audiology or in the unauthorized practice as a speech-language pathology assistant.</p>
          <p>(c) The penalty fee for practicing speech-language pathology or audiology and failing to submit a continuing education report by the due date with the correct number or type of hours in the correct time period is $100 plus $20 for each missing clock hour. The penalty fee for a licensed speech-language pathology assistant who fails to submit a continuing education report by the due date with the correct number or type of hours in the correct time period is $100 plus $20 for each missing clock hour. "Missing" means not obtained between the effective and expiration dates of the certificate, the one-month period following the certificate expiration date, or the 30 days following notice of a penalty fee for failing to report all continuing education hours. The licensee must obtain the missing number of continuing education hours by the next reporting due date.</p>
          <p>(d) Civil penalties and discipline incurred by licensees prior to August 1, 2005, for conduct described in paragraph (a), (b), or (c) shall be recorded as nondisciplinary penalty fees. For conduct described in paragraph (a) or (b) occurring after August 1, 2005, and exceeding six months, payment of a penalty fee does not preclude any disciplinary action reasonably justified by the individual case.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.5194.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/363/#laws.0.12.0">1996 c 363 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/317/#laws.0.8.0">1998 c 317 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/245/#laws.2.34.0">1999 c 245 art 2 s 34</a>-37; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/87/#laws.0.37.0">2003 c 87 s 37</a>-39; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.7.48.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 7 s 48</a>-51; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/147/#laws.7.6.0">2005 c 147 art 7 s 6</a>; art 9 s 1; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/189/#laws.0.11.0">2008 c 189 s 11</a>,12; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/157/#laws.1.5.0">2009 c 157 art 1 s 5</a>-7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/278/#laws.2.13.0">2012 c 278 art 2 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.10.115.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 10 s 115</a>-119; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/83/#laws.1.37.0">2020 c 83 art 1 s 37</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.25.21.0">2024 c 127 art 25 s 21</a>,22</p>
      </div>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>Subdivision 3b, as added by Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 21, is effective July 1, 2025. Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 21, the effective date. </p>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>The amendments to subdivision 8 by Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 22, are effective July 1, 2025. Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 22, the effective date.</p>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.5195">
        <h1 class="shn">148.5195 INVESTIGATION PROCESS AND GROUNDS FOR DISCIPLINARY ACTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5195.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Investigations of complaints.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner or advisory council may initiate an investigation upon receiving a signed complaint or other signed written communication that alleges or implies that an individual has violated sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>. According to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.13#stat.214.13.6">214.13, subdivision 6</a>, in the receipt, investigation, and hearing of a complaint that alleges or implies an individual has violated sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>, the commissioner shall follow the procedures in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.10">214.10</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5195.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Rights of applicants and licensees.</span></h2>
          <p>The rights of an applicant denied licensure are stated in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.519#stat.148.519.2">148.519, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (e). A licensee shall not be subjected to disciplinary action under this section without first having an opportunity for a contested case hearing under chapter 14.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5195.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Grounds for disciplinary action by commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may take any of the disciplinary actions listed in subdivision 4 on proof that the individual has:</p>
          <p>(1) intentionally submitted false or misleading information to the commissioner or the advisory council;</p>
          <p>(2) failed, within 30 days, to provide information in response to a written request by the commissioner or advisory council;</p>
          <p>(3) performed services of a speech-language pathologist, audiologist, or speech-language pathology assistant in an incompetent or negligent manner;</p>
          <p>(4) violated sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>;</p>
          <p>(5) failed to perform services with reasonable judgment, skill, or safety due to the use of alcohol or drugs, or other physical or mental impairment;</p>
          <p>(6) violated any state or federal law, rule, or regulation, and the violation is a felony or misdemeanor, an essential element of which is dishonesty, or which relates directly or indirectly to the practice of speech-language pathology or audiology or to the practice of a speech-language pathology assistant. Conviction for violating any state or federal law which relates to speech-language pathology, audiology, or the practice of a speech-language pathology assistant is necessarily considered to constitute a violation, except as provided in chapter 364;</p>
          <p>(7) aided or abetted another person in violating any provision of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>;</p>
          <p>(8) been or is being disciplined by another jurisdiction, if any of the grounds for the discipline is the same or substantially equivalent to those under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>;</p>
          <p>(9) not cooperated with the commissioner or advisory council in an investigation conducted according to subdivision 1;</p>
          <p>(10) advertised in a manner that is false or misleading;</p>
          <p>(11) engaged in conduct likely to deceive, defraud, or harm the public; or demonstrated a willful or careless disregard for the health, welfare, or safety of a client;</p>
          <p>(12) failed to disclose to the consumer any fee splitting or any promise to pay a portion of a fee to any other professional other than a fee for services rendered by the other professional to the client;</p>
          <p>(13) engaged in abusive or fraudulent billing practices, including violations of federal Medicare and Medicaid laws, Food and Drug Administration regulations, or state medical assistance laws;</p>
          <p>(14) obtained money, property, or services from a consumer through the use of undue influence, high pressure sales tactics, harassment, duress, deception, or fraud;</p>
          <p>(15) performed services for a client who had no possibility of benefiting from the services;</p>
          <p>(16) failed to refer a client for medical evaluation or to other health care professionals when appropriate or when a client indicated symptoms associated with diseases that could be medically or surgically treated;</p>
          <p>(17) had the certification required by chapter 153A denied, suspended, or revoked according to chapter 153A;</p>
          <p>(18) used the term doctor of audiology, doctor of speech-language pathology, AuD, or SLPD without having obtained the degree from an institution accredited by the North Central Association of Colleges and Secondary Schools, the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology, the United States Department of Education, or an equivalent;</p>
          <p>(19) failed to comply with the requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5192">148.5192</a> regarding supervision of speech-language pathology assistants; or</p>
          <p>(20) if the individual is an audiologist or certified prescription hearing aid dispenser:</p>
          <p>(i) prescribed to a consumer or potential consumer the use of a prescription hearing aid, unless the prescription from a physician, an audiologist, or a certified dispenser is in writing, is based on an audiogram that is delivered to the consumer or potential consumer when the prescription is made, and bears the following information in all capital letters of 12-point or larger boldface type: "THIS PRESCRIPTION MAY BE FILLED BY, AND PRESCRIPTION HEARING AIDS MAY BE PURCHASED FROM, THE LICENSED AUDIOLOGIST OR CERTIFIED DISPENSER OF YOUR CHOICE";</p>
          <p>(ii) failed to give a copy of the audiogram, upon which the prescription is based, to the consumer when the consumer requests a copy;</p>
          <p>(iii) failed to provide the consumer rights brochure required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5197#stat.148.5197.3">148.5197, subdivision 3</a>;</p>
          <p>(iv) failed to comply with restrictions on sales of prescription hearing aids in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5197#stat.148.5197.3">148.5197, subdivision 3</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>;</p>
          <p>(v) failed to return a consumer's prescription hearing aid used as a trade-in or for a discount in the price of a new prescription hearing aid when requested by the consumer upon cancellation of the purchase agreement;</p>
          <p>(vi) failed to follow Food and Drug Administration or Federal Trade Commission regulations relating to dispensing prescription hearing aids;</p>
          <p>(vii) failed to dispense a prescription hearing aid in a competent manner or without appropriate training;</p>
          <p>(viii) delegated prescription hearing aid dispensing authority to a person not authorized to dispense a prescription hearing aid under this chapter or chapter 153A;</p>
          <p>(ix) failed to comply with the requirements of an employer or supervisor of a prescription hearing aid dispenser trainee;</p>
          <p>(x) violated a state or federal court order or judgment, including a conciliation court judgment, relating to the activities of the individual's prescription hearing aid dispensing; or</p>
          <p>(xi) failed to include on the audiogram the practitioner's printed name, credential type, credential number, signature, and date.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5195.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Disciplinary actions.</span></h2>
          <p>If the commissioner finds that an individual should be disciplined according to subdivision 3, the commissioner may take any one or more of the following actions:</p>
          <p>(1) refuse to grant or renew licensure;</p>
          <p>(2) suspend licensure for a period not exceeding one year;</p>
          <p>(3) revoke licensure;</p>
          <p>(4) take any reasonable lesser action against an individual upon proof that the individual has violated sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>; or</p>
          <p>(5) impose, for each violation, a civil penalty not exceeding $10,000 that deprives the licensee of any economic advantage gained by the violation and that reimburses the Department of Health for costs of the investigation and proceedings resulting in disciplinary action, including the amount paid for services of the administrative hearings, the amount paid for services of the Office of the Attorney General, attorney fees, court reporters, witnesses, reproduction of records, advisory council members' per diem compensation, department staff time, and expenses incurred by advisory council members and department staff.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5195.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Consequences of disciplinary actions.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon the suspension or revocation of licensure, the speech-language pathologist or audiologist, or speech-language pathology assistant, shall cease to practice speech-language pathology or audiology, or practice as a speech-language pathology assistant; to use titles protected under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>; and to represent to the public that the speech-language pathologist or audiologist, or speech-language pathology assistant, is licensed by the commissioner.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5195.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Reinstatement requirements after disciplinary action.</span></h2>
          <p>A speech-language pathologist or audiologist, or speech-language pathology assistant, who has had licensure suspended may petition on forms provided by the commissioner for reinstatement following the period of suspension specified by the commissioner. The requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5191">148.5191</a> for renewing licensure must be met before licensure may be reinstated.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5195.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Authority to contract.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall contract with the health professionals services program as authorized by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.31">214.31</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.37">214.37</a> to provide these services to practitioners under this chapter. The health professionals services program does not affect the commissioner's authority to discipline violations of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.5195.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/363/#laws.0.13.0">1996 c 363 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/317/#laws.0.9.0">1998 c 317 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/87/#laws.0.41.0">2003 c 87 s 41</a>-45; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/279/#laws.1.17.0">2004 c 279 art 1 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/147/#laws.7.7.0">2005 c 147 art 7 s 7</a>,19; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/267/#laws.2.9.0">2006 c 267 art 2 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/189/#laws.0.13.0">2008 c 189 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/274/#laws.0.3.0">2010 c 274 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.10.120.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 10 s 120</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.3.43.0">2023 c 70 art 3 s 43</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.25.23.0">2024 c 127 art 25 s 23</a>-25</p>
      </div>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>The amendments to subdivisions 3, 5, and 6 by Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, sections 23, 24, and 25, are effective July 1, 2025. Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, sections 23, 24, and 25, the effective dates.</p>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.5196">
        <h1 class="shn">148.5196 SPEECH-LANGUAGE PATHOLOGIST AND AUDIOLOGIST ADVISORY COUNCIL.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5196.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Membership.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall appoint 13 persons to a Speech-Language Pathologist and Audiologist Advisory Council. The 13 persons must include:</p>
          <p>(1) three public members, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.02">214.02</a>. Two of the public members shall be either persons receiving services of a speech-language pathologist or audiologist, or family members of or caregivers to such persons, and at least one of the public members shall be either a hearing aid user or an advocate of one;</p>
          <p>(2) three speech-language pathologists licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>, one of whom is currently and has been, for the five years immediately preceding the appointment, engaged in the practice of speech-language pathology in Minnesota and each of whom is employed in a different employment setting including, but not limited to, private practice, hospitals, rehabilitation settings, educational settings, and government agencies;</p>
          <p>(3) one speech-language pathologist licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>, who is currently and has been, for the five years immediately preceding the appointment, employed by a Minnesota public school district or a Minnesota public school district consortium that is authorized by Minnesota Statutes and who is licensed in speech-language pathology by the Professional Educator Licensing and Standards Board;</p>
          <p>(4) three audiologists licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>, two of whom are currently and have been, for the five years immediately preceding the appointment, engaged in the practice of audiology and the dispensing of prescription hearing aids in Minnesota and each of whom is employed in a different employment setting including, but not limited to, private practice, hospitals, rehabilitation settings, educational settings, industry, and government agencies;</p>
          <p>(5) one nonaudiologist prescription hearing aid dispenser recommended by a professional association representing prescription hearing aid dispensers;</p>
          <p>(6) one physician licensed under chapter 147 and certified by the American Board of Otolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery; and</p>
          <p>(7) one speech-language pathology assistant licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5196.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Organization.</span></h2>
          <p>The advisory council shall be organized and administered under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/15.059">15.059</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5196.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Duties.</span></h2>
          <p>The advisory council shall:</p>
          <p>(1) advise the commissioner regarding speech-language pathologist and audiologist licensure standards;</p>
          <p>(2) advise the commissioner regarding the delegation of duties to, the licensure standards for, and the training required for speech-language pathology assistants;</p>
          <p>(3) advise the commissioner on enforcement of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5198">148.5198</a>;</p>
          <p>(4) provide for distribution of information regarding speech-language pathologist, audiologist, and speech-language pathology assistant licensure standards;</p>
          <p>(5) review applications and make recommendations to the commissioner on granting or denying licensure or licensure renewal;</p>
          <p>(6) review reports of investigations relating to individuals and make recommendations to the commissioner as to whether licensure should be denied or disciplinary action taken against the individual;</p>
          <p>(7) advise the commissioner regarding approval of continuing education activities provided by sponsors using the criteria in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.5193#stat.148.5193.2">148.5193, subdivision 2</a>; and</p>
          <p>(8) perform other duties authorized for advisory councils under chapter 214, or as directed by the commissioner.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.5196.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/363/#laws.0.14.0">1996 c 363 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/460/#laws.0.31.0">2000 c 460 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/87/#laws.0.46.0">2003 c 87 s 46</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/279/#laws.1.18.0">2004 c 279 art 1 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/147/#laws.7.8.0">2005 c 147 art 7 s 8</a>,19; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/5/#laws.12.22.0">1Sp2017 c 5 art 12 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.3.44.0">2023 c 70 art 3 s 44</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.25.26.0">2024 c 127 art 25 s 26</a>,27</p>
      </div>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>The amendments to subdivisions 1 and 3 by Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, sections 26 and 27, are effective July 1, 2025. Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, sections 26 and 27, the effective dates.</p>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.5197">
        <h1 class="shn">148.5197 HEARING AID DISPENSING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5197.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Content of contracts.</span></h2>
          <p>Oral statements made by an audiologist or certified dispenser regarding the provision of warranties, refunds, and service on the prescription hearing aid or aids dispensed must be written on, and become part of, the contract of sale, specify the item or items covered, and indicate the person or business entity obligated to provide the warranty, refund, or service.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5197.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Required use of license number.</span></h2>
          <p>The audiologist's license number or certified dispenser's certificate number must appear on all contracts, bills of sale, and receipts used in the sale of prescription hearing aids.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5197.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Consumer rights information.</span></h2>
          <p>An audiologist or certified dispenser shall, at the time of the prescription, give a consumer rights brochure, prepared by the commissioner and containing information about legal requirements pertaining to dispensing of prescription hearing aids, to each potential consumer of a prescription hearing aid. The brochure must contain information about the consumer information center described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/153A.18">153A.18</a>. A contract for a prescription hearing aid must note the receipt of the brochure by the consumer, along with the consumer's signature or initials.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5197.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Liability for contracts.</span></h2>
          <p>Owners of entities in the business of dispensing prescription hearing aids, employers of audiologists or persons who dispense prescription hearing aids, supervisors of trainees or audiology students, and hearing aid dispensers conducting the transaction at issue are liable for satisfying all terms of contracts, written or oral, made by their agents, employees, assignees, affiliates, or trainees, including terms relating to products, repairs, warranties, service, and refunds. The commissioner may enforce the terms of prescription hearing aid contracts against the principal, employer, supervisor, or dispenser who conducted the transaction and may impose any remedy provided for in this chapter.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.5197.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/147/#laws.7.9.0">2005 c 147 art 7 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.3.45.0">2023 c 70 art 3 s 45</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.5198">
        <h1 class="shn">148.5198 RESTRICTION ON SALE OF PRESCRIPTION HEARING AIDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5198.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">45-calendar-day guarantee and buyer right to cancel.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An audiologist or certified dispenser dispensing a prescription hearing aid in this state must comply with paragraphs (b) and (c).</p>
          <p>(b) The audiologist or certified dispenser must provide the buyer with a 45-calendar-day written money-back guarantee. The guarantee must permit the buyer to cancel the purchase for any reason within 45 calendar days after receiving the prescription hearing aid by giving or mailing written notice of cancellation to the audiologist or certified dispenser. If the buyer mails the notice of cancellation, the 45-calendar-day period is counted using the postmark date, to the date of receipt by the audiologist or certified dispenser. If the prescription hearing aid must be repaired, remade, or adjusted during the 45-calendar-day money-back guarantee period, the running of the 45-calendar-day period is suspended one day for each 24-hour period that the prescription hearing aid is not in the buyer's possession. A repaired, remade, or adjusted prescription hearing aid must be claimed by the buyer within three business days after notification of availability, after which time the running of the 45-calendar-day period resumes. The guarantee must entitle the buyer, upon cancellation, to receive a refund of payment within 30 days of return of the prescription hearing aid to the audiologist or certified dispenser. The audiologist or certified dispenser may retain as a cancellation fee no more than $250 of the buyer's total purchase price of the prescription hearing aid.</p>
          <p>(c) The audiologist or certified dispenser shall provide the buyer with a contract written in plain English, that contains uniform language and provisions that meet the requirements under the Plain Language Contract Act, sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325G.29">325G.29</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325G.36">325G.36</a>. The contract must include, but is not limited to, the following: in immediate proximity to the space reserved for the signature of the buyer, or on the first page if there is no space reserved for the signature of the buyer, a clear and conspicuous disclosure of the following specific statement in all capital letters of no less than 12-point boldface type: "MINNESOTA STATE LAW GIVES THE BUYER THE RIGHT TO CANCEL THIS PURCHASE FOR ANY REASON AT ANY TIME PRIOR TO MIDNIGHT OF THE 45TH CALENDAR DAY AFTER RECEIPT OF THE PRESCRIPTION HEARING AID(S). THIS CANCELLATION MUST BE IN WRITING AND MUST BE GIVEN OR MAILED TO THE AUDIOLOGIST OR CERTIFIED DISPENSER. IF THE BUYER DECIDES TO RETURN THE PRESCRIPTION HEARING AID(S) WITHIN THIS 45-CALENDAR-DAY PERIOD, THE BUYER WILL RECEIVE A REFUND OF THE TOTAL PURCHASE PRICE OF THE AID(S) FROM WHICH THE AUDIOLOGIST OR CERTIFIED DISPENSER MAY RETAIN AS A CANCELLATION FEE NO MORE THAN $250."</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5198.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Itemized repair bill.</span></h2>
          <p>Any audiologist, certified dispenser, or company who agrees to repair a prescription hearing aid must provide the owner of the prescription hearing aid, or the owner's representative, with a bill that describes the repair and services rendered. The bill must also include the repairing audiologist's, certified dispenser's, or company's name, address, and telephone number.</p>
          <p>This subdivision does not apply to an audiologist, certified dispenser, or company that repairs a prescription hearing aid pursuant to an express warranty covering the entire prescription hearing aid and the warranty covers the entire cost, both parts and labor, of the repair.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5198.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Repair warranty.</span></h2>
