          <p>Any guarantee of prescription hearing aid repairs must be in writing and delivered to the owner of the prescription hearing aid, or the owner's representative, stating the repairing audiologist's, certified dispenser's, or company's name, address, telephone number, length of guarantee, model, and serial number of the prescription hearing aid and all other terms and conditions of the guarantee.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5198.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>A person found to have violated this section is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5198.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Additional.</span></h2>
          <p>In addition to the penalty provided in subdivision 4, a person found to have violated this section is subject to the penalties and remedies provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325F.69#stat.325F.69.1">325F.69, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.5198.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Estimates.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon the request of the owner of a prescription hearing aid or the owner's representative for a written estimate and prior to the commencement of repairs, a repairing audiologist, certified dispenser, or company shall provide the customer with a written estimate of the price of repairs. If a repairing audiologist, certified dispenser, or company provides a written estimate of the price of repairs, it must not charge more than the total price stated in the estimate for the repairs. If the repairing audiologist, certified dispenser, or company after commencing repairs determines that additional work is necessary to accomplish repairs that are the subject of a written estimate and if the repairing audiologist, certified dispenser, or company did not unreasonably fail to disclose the possible need for the additional work when the estimate was made, the repairing audiologist, certified dispenser, or company may charge more than the estimate for the repairs if the repairing audiologist, certified dispenser, or company immediately provides the owner or owner's representative a revised written estimate pursuant to this section and receives authorization to continue with the repairs. If continuation of the repairs is not authorized, the repairing audiologist, certified dispenser, or company shall return the prescription hearing aid as close as possible to its former condition and shall release the prescription hearing aid to the owner or owner's representative upon payment of charges for repairs actually performed and not in excess of the original estimate.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.5198.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/147/#laws.7.10.0">2005 c 147 art 7 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.3.46.0">2023 c 70 art 3 s 46</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">OPTOMETRISTS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.52">
        <h1 class="shn">148.52 BOARD OF OPTOMETRY.</h1>
        <p>The Board of Optometry shall consist of two public members as defined by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.02">214.02</a> and five Minnesota licensed optometrists appointed by the governor. Membership terms, compensation of members, removal of members, the filling of membership vacancies, and fiscal year and reporting requirements shall be as provided in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.07">214.07</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.09">214.09</a>.</p>
        <p>The provision of staff, administrative services and office space; the review and processing of complaints; the setting of board fees; and other provisions relating to board operations shall be as provided in chapter 214.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.52.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/35">5785</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1915/0/127/#laws.0.1.0">1915 c 127 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1925/0/239/#laws.0.1.0">1925 c 239 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1929/0/420/#laws.0.1.0">1929 c 420 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/62/#laws.0.1.0">1973 c 62 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/638/#laws.0.20.0">1973 c 638 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/136/#laws.0.16.0">1975 c 136 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/222/#laws.0.61.0">1976 c 222 s 61</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/239/#laws.0.56.0">1976 c 239 s 56</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/199/#laws.1.42.0">1991 c 199 art 1 s 42</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.1.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.53">
        <h1 class="shn">148.53 POWERS OF BOARD.</h1>
        <p>The state Board of Optometry shall have the power to make any rules and to do any and all things not inconsistent with law which it may deem necessary or expedient for the effective enforcement of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.52">148.52</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.62">148.62</a> or for the full and efficient performance of its duties thereunder.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.53.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/35">5786</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1915/0/127/#laws.0.2.0">1915 c 127 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1925/0/239/#laws.0.2.0">1925 c 239 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1929/0/420/#laws.0.2.0">1929 c 420 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.54">
        <h1 class="shn">148.54 BOARD; SEAL.</h1>
        <p>The Board of Optometry shall elect from among its members a president, vice president, and secretary and may adopt a seal.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.54.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/35">5787</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1915/0/127/#laws.0.3.0">1915 c 127 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1925/0/239/#laws.0.3.0">1925 c 239 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1949/0/267/#laws.0.1.0">1949 c 267 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/136/#laws.0.17.0">1975 c 136 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/222/#laws.0.62.0">1976 c 222 s 62</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.2.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.148.55"><b>148.55</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/222/#laws.0.209.0">1976 c 222 s 209</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.56">
        <h1 class="shn">148.56 OPTOMETRISTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.56.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Optometry defined.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Any person shall be deemed to be practicing optometry within the meaning of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.52">148.52</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.62">148.62</a> who shall in any way:</p>
          <p>(1) advertise as an optometrist;</p>
          <p>(2) employ any means, including the use of autorefractors or other automated testing devices, for the measurement of the powers of vision or the adaptation of lenses or prisms for the aid thereof;</p>
          <p>(3) possess testing appliances for the purpose of the measurement of the powers of vision;</p>
          <p>(4) diagnose any disease, optical deficiency or deformity, or visual or muscular anomaly of the visual system consisting of the human eye and its accessory or subordinate anatomical parts;</p>
          <p>(5) prescribe lenses, including plano or cosmetic contact lenses, or prisms for the correction or the relief of same;</p>
          <p>(6) employ or prescribe ocular exercises, orthoptics, or habilitative and rehabilitative therapeutic vision care; or</p>
          <p>(7) prescribe or administer legend drugs to aid in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, prevention, treatment, or management of disease, deficiency, deformity, or abnormality of the human eye and adnexa included in the curricula of accredited schools or colleges of optometry, and as limited by Minnesota statute and adopted rules by the Board of Optometry, or who holds oneself out as being able to do so.</p>
          <p>(b) In the course of treatment, nothing in this section shall allow:</p>
          <p>(1) legend drugs to be administered intravenously, intramuscularly, or by injection, except for treatment of anaphylaxis;</p>
          <p>(2) invasive surgery including, but not limited to, surgery using lasers;</p>
          <p>(3) Schedule II and III oral legend drugs and oral steroids to be administered or prescribed;</p>
          <p>(4) oral antivirals to be prescribed or administered for more than ten days; or</p>
          <p>(5) oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitors to be prescribed or administered for more than seven days.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.56.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Unlawful practices.</span></h2>
          <p>It shall be unlawful for any person who is not licensed as an optometrist in this state to:</p>
          <p>(1) perform any of the actions contained in subdivision 1;</p>
          <p>(2) fit, sell, or dispose of, or to take, receive, or solicit any order for the fitting, sale, or disposition of, any spectacles, eye glasses, or lenses for the correction of vision in any place within the state other than an established place of business where spectacles, eye glasses, or lenses are commonly sold and dealt in; or</p>
          <p>(3) sell or dispose of, at retail, any spectacles, eye glasses, or lenses for the correction of vision in any established place of business or elsewhere in this state except under the supervision, direction, and authority of a duly licensed optometrist who holds a certificate under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.52">148.52</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.62">148.62</a>, and is in charge of and in personal attendance at the booth, counter, or place where such articles are sold or disposed of.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.56.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Unregulated sales.</span></h2>
          <p>Nothing in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.52">148.52</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.62">148.62</a> shall be construed to apply to the sale of toy glasses, goggles consisting of plano-white or plano-colored lenses or ordinary colored glasses or to the replacement of duplications of broken lenses, nor to sales upon prescription from persons legally authorized by the laws of this state to examine eyes and prescribe glasses therefor, nor shall it apply to regularly licensed physicians and surgeons. Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.52">148.52</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.62">148.62</a> also do not apply to the sale of spectacles, used for reading and containing only simple lenses having a plus power of up to and including <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/3.25">3.25</a>, if no attempt is made to test the eyes. The term "simple lenses" does not include bifocals. The seller shall prominently display a sign on the counter or rack or other display device where the spectacles are offered for sale that reads as follows: "If you have experienced a vision loss, the selection of these glasses should not take the place of an eye exam."</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.56.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">License required.</span></h2>
          <p>It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the practice of optometry without first procuring a license from the state Board of Optometry.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.56.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Scope of practice exemption.</span></h2>
          <p>Nothing in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.52">148.52</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.62">148.62</a> shall prohibit the practice of a licensed or registered health care provider in Minnesota who is operating within the provider's scope of practice under Minnesota law.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.56.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/35">5789</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1915/0/127/#laws.0.5.0">1915 c 127 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1925/0/239/#laws.0.5.0">1925 c 239 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1929/0/420/#laws.0.3.0">1929 c 420 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/301/#laws.0.146.0">1983 c 301 s 146</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/125/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 125 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/262/#laws.0.1.0">2008 c 262 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/129/#laws.0.1.0">2013 c 129 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/55/#laws.1.40.0">2022 c 55 art 1 s 40</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.57">
        <h1 class="shn">148.57 LICENSE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.57.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Examination.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person not authorized to practice optometry in the state and desiring to do so shall apply to the state Board of Optometry by filling out and swearing to an application for a license granted by the board and accompanied by a fee established by the board, not to exceed the amount specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.59">148.59</a>. With the submission of the application form, the candidate shall prove that the candidate:</p>
          <p>(1) is of good moral character;</p>
          <p>(2) has obtained a clinical doctorate degree from a board-approved school or college of optometry, or is currently enrolled in the final year of study at such an institution; and</p>
          <p>(3) has passed all parts of an examination.</p>
          <p>(b) The examination shall include both a written portion and a clinical practical portion and shall thoroughly test the fitness of the candidate to practice in this state. In regard to the written and clinical practical examinations, the board may:</p>
          <p>(1) prepare, administer, and grade the examination itself;</p>
          <p>(2) recognize and approve in whole or in part an examination prepared, administered and graded by a national board of examiners in optometry; or</p>
          <p>(3) administer a recognized and approved examination prepared and graded by or under the direction of a national board of examiners in optometry.</p>
          <p>(c) The board shall issue a license to each applicant who satisfactorily passes the examinations and fulfills the other requirements stated in this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.57.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Endorsement.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An optometrist who holds a current license from another state, and who has practiced in that state not less than three years immediately preceding application, may apply for licensure in Minnesota by filling out and swearing to an application for license by endorsement furnished by the board. The completed application with all required documentation shall be filed at the board office along with a fee established by the board, not to exceed the amount specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.59">148.59</a>. The application fee shall be for the use of the board and in no case shall be refunded.</p>
          <p>(b) To verify that the applicant possesses the knowledge and ability essential to the practice of optometry in this state, the applicant must provide evidence of:</p>
          <p>(1) having obtained a clinical doctorate degree from a board-approved school or college of optometry;</p>
          <p>(2) successful completion of both written and practical examinations for licensure in the applicant's original state of licensure that thoroughly tested the fitness of the applicant to practice;</p>
          <p>(3) successful completion of an examination of Minnesota state optometry laws;</p>
          <p>(4) compliance with the requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.575">148.575</a>;</p>
          <p>(5) compliance with all continuing education required for license renewal in every state in which the applicant currently holds an active license to practice; and</p>
          <p>(6) being in good standing with every state board from which a license has been issued.</p>
          <p>(c) Documentation from a national certification system or program, approved by the board, which supports any of the listed requirements, may be used as evidence. The applicant may then be issued a license if the requirements for licensure in the other state are deemed by the board to be equivalent to those of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.52">148.52</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.62">148.62</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.57.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.34.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.57.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.34.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.57.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Change of address.</span></h2>
          <p>A person regulated by the board shall maintain a current name and address with the board and shall notify the board in writing within 30 days of any change in name or address. If a name change only is requested, the regulated person must request revised credentials and return the current credentials to the board. The board may require the regulated person to substantiate the name change by submitting official documentation from a court of law or agency authorized under law to receive and officially record a name change. If an address change only is requested, no request for revised credentials is required. If the regulated person's current credentials have been lost, stolen, or destroyed, the person shall provide a written explanation to the board.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.57.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Expedited and temporary licensing for former and current members of the military.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Applicants seeking licensure according to this subdivision must be:</p>
          <p>(1) an active duty military member;</p>
          <p>(2) the spouse of an active duty military member; or</p>
          <p>(3) a veteran who has left service in the two years preceding the date of license application, and has confirmation of an honorable or general discharge status.</p>
          <p>(b) A qualified applicant under this subdivision must provide evidence of:</p>
          <p>(1) a current valid license, certificate, or permit in another state without history of disciplinary action by a regulatory authority in the other state; and</p>
          <p>(2) a current criminal background study without a criminal conviction that is determined by the board to adversely affect the applicant's ability to become licensed.</p>
          <p>(c) A temporary license issued under this subdivision is effective for six months from the initial temporary licensure date.</p>
          <p>(d) During the temporary license period, the individual shall complete the licensed optometrist application for licensure.</p>
          <p>(e) In order to remain licensed after the expiration of the temporary license, an individual must meet the requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.57">148.57, subdivisions 1</a> and 2.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.57.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/35">5790</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1915/0/127/#laws.0.6.0">1915 c 127 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1925/0/239/#laws.0.6.0">1925 c 239 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1929/0/420/#laws.0.4.0">1929 c 420 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1949/0/267/#laws.0.3.0">1949 c 267 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/381/#laws.0.2.0">1967 c 381 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/62/#laws.0.2.0">1973 c 62 s 2</a>-4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/222/#laws.0.63.0">1976 c 222 s 63</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/516/#laws.0.1.0">1978 c 516 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/388/#laws.0.5.0">1982 c 388 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/247/#laws.0.25.0">1985 c 247 s 25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/419/#laws.0.1.0">1992 c 419 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/121/#laws.0.3.0">1993 c 121 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/413/#laws.0.1.0">2000 c 413 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/262/#laws.0.2.0">2008 c 262 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.3.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 3</a>-5; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/77/#laws.2.18.0">2015 c 77 art 2 s 18</a></p>
      </div>

      <div class="sr_by_subd" id="stat.148.573">

        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.573.1">

          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.34.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 34</a>]</p>

      <div class="section" id="stat.148.574">
        <h1 class="shn">148.574 PROHIBITIONS RELATING TO LEGEND DRUGS.</h1>
        <p class="in">Notwithstanding sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/151.37">151.37</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/152.12">152.12</a>, an optometrist is prohibited from dispensing legend drugs at retail, unless the legend drug is within the scope designated in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.56#stat.148.56.1">148.56, subdivision 1</a>, and is administered to the eye through an ophthalmic good as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145.711#stat.145.711.4">145.711, subdivision 4</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.574.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/388/#laws.0.4.0">1982 c 388 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/121/#laws.0.5.0">1993 c 121 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/62/#laws.0.2.0">2003 c 62 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/262/#laws.0.5.0">2008 c 262 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.6.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 6</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.575">
        <h1 class="shn">148.575 CERTIFICATE REQUIRED FOR USE OF LEGEND DRUGS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.575.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.34.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.575.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Requirements defined.</span></h2>
          <p> A licensed optometrist shall comply with the following requirements for the use of legend drugs:</p>
          <p>(1) successful completion of at least 100 hours of study in the examination, diagnosis, and treatment of conditions of the human eye with legend drugs;</p>
          <p>(2) successful completion of two years of supervised clinical experience in differential diagnosis of eye disease or disorders as part of optometric training or one year of that experience and ten years of actual clinical experience as a licensed optometrist; and</p>
          <p>(3) successful completion of a nationally standardized examination approved or administered by the board on the subject of treatment and management of ocular disease.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.575.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.34.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.575.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Accreditation of courses.</span></h2>
          <p>The Board of Optometry may approve courses of study in general or ocular pharmacology and examination, diagnosis, and treatment of conditions of the human eye only if they are taught by an institution that meets the following criteria:</p>
          <p>(1) the institution has facilities for both didactic and clinical instruction in pharmacology and ocular disease treatment;</p>
          <p>(2) the institution certifies to the Board of Optometry that the course of instruction is comparable in content to courses of instruction required by other health-related licensing boards whose license holders or registrants are permitted to administer pharmaceutical agents in their professional practice for either diagnostic or therapeutic purposes or both; and</p>
          <p>(3) the institution is accredited by a regional or professional accrediting organization recognized by the Council for Higher Education Accreditation or its successor agency.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.575.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.34.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.575.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.34.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 34</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.575.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/121/#laws.0.6.0">1993 c 121 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/62/#laws.0.3.0">2003 c 62 s 3</a>,4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/262/#laws.0.6.0">2008 c 262 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.7.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 7</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.148.576"><b>148.576</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.34.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 34</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.577">
        <h1 class="shn">148.577 STANDARD OF CARE.</h1>
        <p>A licensed optometrist is held to the same standard of care in the use of those legend drugs as physicians licensed by the state of Minnesota.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.577.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/121/#laws.0.8.0">1993 c 121 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/62/#laws.0.6.0">2003 c 62 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.8.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 8</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.148.578"><b>148.578</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/7/#laws.2.67.0">1997 c 7 art 2 s 67</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.148.58"><b>148.58</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/222/#laws.0.209.0">1976 c 222 s 209</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.59">
        <h1 class="shn">148.59 LICENSE RENEWAL; LICENSE AND REGISTRATION FEES.</h1>
        <p>A licensed optometrist shall pay to the state Board of Optometry a fee as set by the board in order to renew a license as provided by board rule. No fees shall be refunded. Fees may not exceed the following amounts but may be adjusted lower by board direction and are for the exclusive use of the board:</p>
        <p>(1) optometry licensure application, $160;</p>
        <p>(2) optometry annual licensure renewal, $200;</p>
        <p>(3) optometry late penalty fee, $75;</p>
        <p>(4) annual license renewal card, $10;</p>
        <p>(5) continuing education provider application, $45;</p>
        <p>(6) emeritus registration, $10;</p>
        <p>(7) endorsement/reciprocity application, $160;</p>
        <p>(8) replacement of initial license, $12;</p>
        <p>(9) license verification, $50;</p>
        <p>(10) state jurisprudence examination, $75;</p>
        <p>(11) optometric education continuing education data bank registration, $25; and</p>
        <p>(12) miscellaneous labels and data retrieval, $50.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.59.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/35">5792</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1915/0/127/#laws.0.8.0">1915 c 127 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1925/0/239/#laws.0.8.0">1925 c 239 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1949/0/267/#laws.0.4.0">1949 c 267 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/378/#laws.0.1.0">1959 c 378 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/381/#laws.0.4.0">1967 c 381 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/62/#laws.0.6.0">1973 c 62 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/222/#laws.0.64.0">1976 c 222 s 64</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.9.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.10.7.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 10 s 7</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.595">
        <h1 class="shn">148.595 TEMPORARY MILITARY PERMIT; FEE.</h1>
        <p>The Board of Optometry shall establish a temporary permit in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/197.4552">197.4552</a>. The fee for the temporary military permit is $250.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.595.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/312/#laws.4.10.0">2014 c 312 art 4 s 10</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.60">
        <h1 class="shn">148.60 EXPENSES.</h1>
        <p>The expenses of administering sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.52">148.52</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.62">148.62</a> shall be paid from appropriations made to the Board of Optometry.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.60.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/35">5793</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1915/0/127/#laws.0.9.0">1915 c 127 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1925/0/239/#laws.0.9.0">1925 c 239 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1955/0/847/#laws.0.14.0">1955 c 847 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/638/#laws.0.21.0">1973 c 638 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/136/#laws.0.19.0">1975 c 136 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/222/#laws.0.65.0">1976 c 222 s 65</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.603">
        <h1 class="shn">148.603 GROUNDS FOR DISCIPLINARY ACTION.</h1>
        <p>The board may refuse to grant a license or may impose disciplinary action as described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.607">148.607</a> against any optometrist for the following:</p>
        <p>(1) failure to demonstrate the qualifications or satisfy the requirements for a license contained in this chapter or in rules of the board. The burden of proof shall be on the applicant to demonstrate the qualifications or the satisfaction of the requirements;</p>
        <p>(2) obtaining a license by fraud or cheating, or attempting to subvert the licensing examination process. Conduct which subverts or attempts to subvert the licensing examination process includes, but is not limited to: (i) conduct which violates the security of the examination materials, such as removing examination materials from the examination room or having unauthorized possession of any portion of a future, current, or previously administered licensing examination; (ii) conduct which violates the standard of test administration, such as communicating with another examinee during administration of the examination, copying another examinee's answers, permitting another examinee to copy one's answers, or possessing unauthorized materials; or (iii) impersonating an examinee or permitting an impersonator to take the examination on one's own behalf;</p>
        <p>(3) conviction, during the previous five years, of a felony or gross misdemeanor, reasonably related to the practice of optometry. Conviction as used in this section shall include a conviction of an offense which if committed in this state would be deemed a felony or gross misdemeanor without regard to its designation elsewhere, or a criminal proceeding where a finding or verdict of guilt is made or returned but the adjudication of guilt is either withheld or not entered thereon;</p>
        <p>(4) revocation, suspension, restriction, limitation, or other disciplinary action against the person's optometry license in another state or jurisdiction, failure to report to the board that charges regarding the person's license have been brought in another state or jurisdiction, or having been refused a license by any other state or jurisdiction;</p>
        <p>(5) advertising which is false or misleading, which violates any rule of the board, or which claims without substantiation the positive cure of any disease;</p>
        <p>(6) violating a rule adopted by the board or an order of the board, a state or federal law, which relates to the practice of optometry, or a state or federal narcotics or controlled substance law;</p>
        <p>(7) engaging in any unethical conduct; conduct likely to deceive, defraud, or harm the public, or demonstrating a willful or careless disregard for the health, welfare, or safety of a patient; or practice of optometry which is professionally incompetent, in that it may create unnecessary danger to any patient's life, health, or safety, which in any of the cases, proof of actual injury need not be established;</p>
        <p>(8) failure to supervise an optometrist's assistant or failure to supervise an optometrist under any agreement with the board;</p>
        <p>(9) aiding or abetting an unlicensed person in the practice of optometry, except that it is not a violation of this section for an optometrist to employ, supervise, or delegate functions to a qualified person who may or may not be required to obtain a license or registration to provide health services if that person is practicing within the scope of that person's license or registration or delegated authority;</p>
        <p>(10) adjudication as mentally incompetent, mentally ill, or developmentally disabled, or as a chemically dependent person, a person dangerous to the public, a sexually dangerous person, or a person who has a sexual psychopathic personality by a court of competent jurisdiction, within or without this state. Such adjudication shall automatically suspend a license for the duration of the license unless the board orders otherwise;</p>
        <p>(11) engaging in unprofessional conduct which includes any departure from or the failure to conform to the minimal standards of acceptable and prevailing practice in which case actual injury to a patient need not be established;</p>
        <p>(12) inability to practice optometry with reasonable skill and safety to patients by reason of illness, use of alcohol, drugs, narcotics, chemicals, or any other type of material or as a result of any mental or physical condition, including deterioration through the aging process or loss of motor skills;</p>
        <p>(13) revealing a privileged communication from or relating to a patient except when otherwise required or permitted by law;</p>
        <p>(14) improper management of medical records, including failure to maintain adequate medical records, to comply with a patient's request made pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291">144.291</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.298">144.298</a> or to furnish a medical record or report required by law;</p>
        <p>(15) fee splitting, including without limitation:</p>
        <p>(i) paying, offering to pay, receiving, or agreeing to receive a commission, rebate, or remuneration, directly or indirectly, primarily for the referral of patients or the prescription of drugs or devices; and</p>
        <p>(ii) dividing fees with another optometrist, other health care provider, or a professional corporation, unless the division is in proportion to the services provided and the responsibility assumed by each professional and the optometrist has disclosed the terms of the division;</p>
        <p>(16) engaging in abusive or fraudulent billing practices, including violations of the federal Medicare and Medicaid laws or state medical assistance laws;</p>
        <p>(17) becoming addicted or habituated to a drug or intoxicant;</p>
        <p>(18) prescribing a drug or device for other than accepted therapeutic or experimental or investigative purposes authorized by the state or a federal agency;</p>
        <p>(19) engaging in conduct with a patient which is sexual or may reasonably be interpreted by the patient as sexual, or in any verbal behavior which is seductive or sexually demeaning to a patient;</p>
        <p>(20) failure to make reports as required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.604">148.604</a> or to cooperate with an investigation of the board as required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.606">148.606</a>;</p>
        <p>(21) knowingly providing false or misleading information that is directly related to the care of a patient; and</p>
        <p>(22) practice of a board-regulated profession under lapsed or nonrenewed credentials.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.603.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/413/#laws.0.2.0">2000 c 413 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/66/#laws.0.3.0">2003 c 66 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.10.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 10</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.604">
        <h1 class="shn">148.604 REPORTING OBLIGATIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.604.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Permission to report.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who has knowledge of any conduct constituting grounds for discipline under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.52">148.52</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.62">148.62</a> may report the violation to the board.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.604.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Institutions.</span></h2>
          <p>Any hospital, clinic, prepaid medical plan, or other health care institution or organization located in this state shall report to the board any action taken by the institution or organization or any of its administrators or medical or other committees to revoke, suspend, restrict, or condition an optometrist's privilege to practice or treat patients in the institution, or as part of the organization, any denial of privileges, or any other disciplinary action. The institution or organization shall also report the resignation of any optometrist prior to the conclusion of any disciplinary proceeding, or prior to the commencement of formal charges but after the optometrist had knowledge that formal charges were contemplated or in preparation. Each report made under this subdivision must state the nature of the action taken, state in detail the reasons for the action, and identify the specific patient medical records upon which the action was based. No report shall be required of an optometrist voluntarily limiting the practice of the optometrist at a hospital provided that the optometrist notifies all hospitals where the optometrist has privileges of the voluntary limitation and the reasons for it.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.604.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Licensed professionals.</span></h2>
          <p>A licensed optometrist shall report to the board personal knowledge of any conduct by any optometrist which the person reasonably believes constitutes grounds for disciplinary action under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.52">148.52</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.62">148.62</a>, including any conduct indicating that the person may be incompetent, may have engaged in unprofessional conduct, or may be physically unable to safely engage in the practice of optometry.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.604.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Self-reporting.</span></h2>
          <p>An optometrist shall report to the board any personal action which would require that a report be filed with the board by any person, health care facility, business, or organization pursuant to subdivisions 2 and 3.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.604.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Deadlines; forms; rulemaking.</span></h2>
          <p>Reports required by subdivisions 2 to 4 must be submitted not later than 30 days after the occurrence of the reportable event or transaction. The board may provide forms for the submission of reports required by this section, may require that reports be submitted on the forms provided, and may adopt rules necessary to ensure prompt and accurate reporting.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.604.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Subpoenas.</span></h2>
          <p>The board may issue subpoenas for the production of any reports required by subdivisions 2 to 4 or any related documents.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.604.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.11.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 11</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.605">
        <h1 class="shn">148.605 IMMUNITY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.605.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Reporting.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person, health care facility, business, or organization is immune from civil liability or criminal prosecution for submitting a report to the board pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.604">148.604</a> or for otherwise reporting to the board violations or alleged violations of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.603">148.603</a>, if they are acting in good faith and in the exercise of reasonable care.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.605.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Investigation; indemnification.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Members of the board, persons employed by the board, and consultants retained by the board for the purpose of investigation of violations, the preparation of charges, and management of board orders on behalf of the board are immune from civil liability and criminal prosecution for any actions, transactions, or publications in the execution of, or relating to, their duties under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.52">148.52</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.62">148.62</a>, if they are acting in good faith and in the exercise of reasonable care.</p>
          <p>(b) Members of the board and persons employed by the board or engaged in maintaining records and making reports regarding adverse health care events are immune from civil liability and criminal prosecution for any actions, transactions, or publications in the execution of, or relating to, their duties under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.52">148.52</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.62">148.62</a>, if they are acting in good faith and in the exercise of reasonable care.</p>
          <p>(c) For purposes of this section, a member of the board or a consultant described in paragraph (a) is considered a state employee under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/3.736#stat.3.736.9">3.736, subdivision 9</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.605.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.12.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 12</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.606">
        <h1 class="shn">148.606 OPTOMETRIST COOPERATION.</h1>
        <p>An optometrist who is the subject of an investigation by or on behalf of the board shall cooperate fully with the investigation. Cooperation includes responding fully and promptly to any question raised by or on behalf of the board relating to the subject of the investigation and providing copies of patient medical records, as reasonably requested by the board, to assist the board in its investigation. If the board does not have written consent from a patient permitting access to the patient's records, the optometrist shall delete any data in the record which identifies the patient before providing it to the board. The board shall maintain any records obtained pursuant to this section as investigative data pursuant to chapter 13.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.606.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.13.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 13</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.607">
        <h1 class="shn">148.607 DISCIPLINARY ACTIONS.</h1>
        <p>When the board finds that a licensed optometrist under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.57">148.57</a> has violated a provision or provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.52">148.52</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.62">148.62</a>, it may do one or more of the following:</p>
        <p>(1) revoke the license;</p>
        <p>(2) suspend the license;</p>
        <p>(3) impose limitations or conditions on the optometrist's practice of optometry, including the limitation of scope of practice to designated field specialties; the imposition of retraining or rehabilitation requirements; the requirement of practice under supervision; or the conditioning of continued practice on demonstration of knowledge or skills by appropriate examination or other review of skill and competence;</p>
        <p>(4) impose a civil penalty not exceeding $10,000 for each separate violation, the amount of the civil penalty to be fixed so as to deprive the optometrist of any economic advantage gained by reason of the violation charged or to reimburse the board for the cost of the investigation and proceeding; and</p>
        <p>(5) censure or reprimand the licensed optometrist.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.607.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.10.14.0">2015 c 71 art 10 s 14</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.61">
        <h1 class="shn">148.61 PENALTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.61.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/242/#laws.0.14.0">1945 c 242 s 14</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.61.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511#stat.148.511.1">148.511, subdivision 1</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.61.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.101">148.101</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.61.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.511">148.511, subd 2</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.61.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Every person not licensed by the board pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.57">148.57</a> who practices optometry in this state shall be guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.61.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/35">5794</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1915/0/127/#laws.0.10.0">1915 c 127 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1925/0/239/#laws.0.10.0">1925 c 239 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/413/#laws.0.3.0">2000 c 413 s 3</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.62">
        <h1 class="shn">148.62 APPLICATION.</h1>
        <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.52">148.52</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.62">148.62</a> shall not be construed as forbidding any person licensed to practice any profession in this state from engaging in such profession as it may now be defined by law.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.62.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/35">5796-1</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1925/0/239/#laws.0.13.0">1925 c 239 s 13</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">DIETITIANS AND NUTRITIONISTS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.621">
        <h1 class="shn">148.621 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.621.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Applicability.</span></h2>
          <p>The definitions in this section apply to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.621.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Accredited college or university.</span></h2>
          <p>"Accredited college or university" means a college or university accredited by the regional accrediting agencies recognized by the Council on Postsecondary Accreditation, and the United States Department of Education at the time the degree was conferred.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.621.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Association.</span></h2>
          <p>"Association" means the American Dietetic Association.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.621.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Board.</span></h2>
          <p>"Board" means the Board of Dietetics and Nutrition Practice.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.621.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Commission.</span></h2>
          <p>"Commission" means the Commission on Dietetic Registration that is a member of the National Commission on Health Certifying Agencies, which national commission establishes national standards of competence for individuals participating in the health care delivery system.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.621.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>"Commissioner" means the commissioner of health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.621.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Dietitian.</span></h2>
          <p>"Dietitian" means an individual who engages in dietetics or nutrition practice and uses the title dietitian.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.621.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Nutritionist.</span></h2>
          <p>"Nutritionist" means an individual who engages in dietetics or nutrition practice and uses the title nutritionist.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.621.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Dietetics or nutrition practice.</span></h2>
          <p>"Dietetics or nutrition practice" means the integration and application of scientific principles of food, nutrition, biochemistry, physiology, food management, and behavioral and social sciences to achieve and maintain human health through the provision of nutrition care services.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.621.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Nutrition care services.</span></h2>
          <p>"Nutrition care services" means:</p>
          <p>(1) assessment of the nutritional needs of individuals or groups;</p>
          <p>(2) establishment of priorities, goals, and objectives to meet nutritional needs;</p>
          <p>(3) provision of nutrition counseling for both normal and therapeutic needs;</p>
          <p>(4) development, implementation, and management of nutrition care services; or</p>
          <p>(5) evaluation, adjustment, and maintenance of appropriate standards of quality in nutrition care.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.621.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Nutritional assessment.</span></h2>
          <p>"Nutritional assessment" means the evaluation of the nutritional needs of individuals or groups based on appropriate biochemical, anthropometric, physical, and dietary data to determine nutrient needs and recommend appropriate nutritional intake.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.621.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Nutrition counseling.</span></h2>
          <p>"Nutrition counseling" means advising and assisting individuals or groups on appropriate nutritional intake by integrating information from the nutritional assessment with information on food and other sources of nutrients and meal preparation consistent with cultural background and socioeconomic status.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.621.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Person.</span></h2>
          <p>"Person" means an individual, corporation, partnership, or other legal entity.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.621.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/613/#laws.0.2.0">1994 c 613 s 2</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.622">
        <h1 class="shn">148.622 BOARD OF DIETETICS AND NUTRITION PRACTICE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.622.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Creation.</span></h2>
          <p>The Board of Dietetics and Nutrition Practice consists of seven members appointed by the governor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.622.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Membership.</span></h2>
          <p>Members of the board must have been residents of the state of Minnesota for two years immediately preceding appointment and must represent various geographic areas of the state and various employment settings, as required by this section. Two members must be dietitians registered with the commission with at least three years of dietetics practice in Minnesota. Two members must be nutritionists with at least three years of nutrition practice in Minnesota. The professional members first appointed need not be licensed under this chapter for appointment to their first terms on the board, but must possess the qualifications necessary for licensure under this chapter. Three other members must be public members as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.02">214.02</a>. Two of the public members must be consumers of nutrition care services or caregivers of those utilizing such services.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.622.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Membership terms; officers; quorum; expenses.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Members must be appointed for staggered terms of four years, with terms beginning August 1 of each year. The terms of the initial board members must be determined by lot as follows: one member must be appointed for a term that expires August 1, 2000; two members must be appointed for terms that expire August 1, 1998; two members must be appointed for terms that expire August 1, 1997; and two members must be appointed for terms that expire August 1, 1995. Members of the board serve until the expiration of the term to which they have been appointed or until their successors have qualified. A person may not be appointed to serve more than two consecutive terms.</p>
          <p>(b) The board shall organize annually and select a chair and vice-chair.</p>
          <p>(c) Four members of the board, including two professional members and two public members, constitute a quorum to do business.</p>
          <p>(d) The board shall hold at least two regular meetings each year. Additional meetings may be held at the call of the chair or at the written request of any three members of the board. At least 14 days' written advance notice of the board meeting is required.</p>
          <p>(e) Board members receive compensation for their services in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/15.0575">15.0575</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.622.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/613/#laws.0.3.0">1994 c 613 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/192/#laws.0.26.0">1997 c 192 s 26</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.623">
        <h1 class="shn">148.623 DUTIES OF THE BOARD.</h1>
        <p>The board shall:</p>
        <p>(1) adopt rules necessary to administer and enforce sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a>;</p>
        <p>(2) administer, coordinate, and enforce sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a>;</p>
        <p>(3) evaluate the qualifications of applicants;</p>
        <p>(4) issue subpoenas, examine witnesses, and administer oaths;</p>
        <p>(5) conduct hearings and keep records and minutes necessary to the orderly administration of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a>;</p>
        <p>(6) investigate persons engaging in practices that violate sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a>; and</p>
        <p>(7) adopt rules under chapter 14 prescribing a code of ethics for licensees.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.623.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/613/#laws.0.4.0">1994 c 613 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.624">
        <h1 class="shn">148.624 LICENSURE; RENEWAL.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.624.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Dietetics.</span></h2>
          <p>The board shall issue a license as a dietitian to a person who files a completed application, pays all required fees, and certifies and furnishes evidence satisfactory to the board that the applicant:</p>
          <p>(1) meets the following qualifications:</p>
          <p>(i) has received a baccalaureate or postgraduate degree from a United States regionally accredited college or university with a major in dietetics, human nutrition, nutrition education, food and nutrition, or food services management;</p>
          <p>(ii) has completed a documented supervised preprofessional practice experience component in dietetic practice of not less than 900 hours under the supervision of a registered dietitian, a state licensed nutrition professional, or an individual with a doctoral degree conferred by a United States regionally accredited college or university with a major course of study in human nutrition, nutrition education, food and nutrition, dietetics, or food systems management. Supervised practice experience must be completed in the United States or its territories. Supervisors who obtain their doctoral degree outside the United States and its territories must have their degrees approved by the board as equivalent to the doctoral degree conferred by a United States regionally accredited college or university; and</p>
          <p>(iii) has successfully completed the registration examination for dietitians administered by the commission; or</p>
          <p>(2) has a valid current registration with the commission which gives the applicant the right to use the term "registered dietitian" or "RD."</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.624.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Nutrition.</span></h2>
          <p>The board shall issue a license as a nutritionist to a person who files a completed application, pays all required fees, and certifies and furnishes evidence satisfactory to the board that the applicant:</p>
          <p>(1) meets the following qualifications:</p>
          <p>(i) has received a master's or doctoral degree from an accredited or approved college or university with a major in human nutrition, public health nutrition, clinical nutrition, nutrition education, community nutrition, or food and nutrition; and</p>
          <p>(ii) has completed a documented supervised preprofessional practice experience component in dietetic practice of not less than 900 hours under the supervision of a registered dietitian, a state licensed nutrition professional, or an individual with a doctoral degree conferred by a United States regionally accredited college or university with a major course of study in human nutrition, nutrition education, food and nutrition, dietetics, or food systems management. Supervised practice experience must be completed in the United States or its territories. Supervisors who obtain their doctoral degree outside the United States and its territories must have their degrees validated as equivalent to the doctoral degree conferred by a United States regionally accredited college or university; or</p>
          <p>(2) has received certification as a Certified Nutrition Specialist by the Certification Board for Nutrition Specialists.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.624.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Petition.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The board may issue a license as a nutritionist to a person who submits to the board a petition for individual review, provided the person has received a master's or doctoral degree from an accredited college or university with a major course of study that includes an emphasis in human nutrition and has completed a supervised preprofessional experience component in nutrition practice of not less than 900 hours under the supervision of a registered dietitian, a state licensed health care practitioner, or an individual with a doctoral degree conferred by a United States regionally accredited college or university with a major course of study in human nutrition, nutrition education, food and nutrition, dietetics, or food system management. Supervised practice experience must be completed in the United States or its territories. Supervisors who obtain their degree outside the United States and its territories must have their degrees approved by the board as equivalent to a comparable degree conferred by a United States regionally accredited college or university.</p>
          <p>(b) The board may issue a license as a dietitian or nutritionist to an applicant who has completed a course of study at a foreign college or university, if the applicant:</p>
          <p>(1) submits a petition for individual review;</p>
          <p>(2) successfully completes a course of study approved by the board as equivalent to a baccalaureate or master's degree conferred by a United States regionally accredited college or university; and</p>
          <p>(3) meets the applicable experiential requirements set by the board.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.624.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Renewal.</span></h2>
          <p>Licensees shall renew licenses at the time and in the manner established by the rules of the board.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.624.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Expedited and temporary licensing for former and current members of the military.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Applicants seeking licensure according to this subdivision must be:</p>
          <p>(1) an active duty military member;</p>
          <p>(2) the spouse of an active duty military member; or</p>
          <p>(3) a veteran who has left service in the two years preceding the date of license application, and has confirmation of an honorable or general discharge status.</p>
          <p>(b) A qualified applicant under this subdivision must provide evidence of:</p>
          <p>(1) a current valid license in another state without history of disciplinary action by a regulatory authority in the other state; and</p>
          <p>(2) a current criminal background study without a criminal conviction that is determined by the board to adversely affect the applicant's ability to become licensed.</p>
          <p>(c) A temporary license issued under this subdivision is effective for six months from the initial temporary licensure date.</p>
          <p>(d) During the temporary license period, the individual shall complete the licensed dietitian or nutritionist application for licensure.</p>
          <p>(e) In order to remain licensed after the expiration of the temporary license, an individual must meet the full licensure requirements.</p>
          <p>(f) The fee for the temporary license is $250.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.624.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/613/#laws.0.5.0">1994 c 613 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/159/#laws.0.36.0">2009 c 159 s 36</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/312/#laws.4.11.0">2014 c 312 art 4 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/77/#laws.2.19.0">2015 c 77 art 2 s 19</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.625">
        <h1 class="shn">148.625 APPLICATION.</h1>
        <p>A person desiring a license under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a> shall apply to the board on a form and in the manner the board prescribes. The application must be accompanied by an application fee in an amount determined by the board.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.625.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/613/#laws.0.6.0">1994 c 613 s 6</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.626">
        <h1 class="shn">148.626 CONTINUING EDUCATION REQUIRED.</h1>
        <p>Within three years of the effective date of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a>, renewal of a license is contingent on the applicant meeting uniform continuing education requirements established by the board. Notice of initial or amended continuing education requirements must be sent to all persons licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a> at least 12 months before a person's license renewal is dependent on satisfaction of those requirements. Continuing education requirements must be sent to new applicants with the forms on which they are to apply for licensure.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.626.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/613/#laws.0.7.0">1994 c 613 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.148.627"><b>148.627</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/159/#laws.0.112.0">2009 c 159 s 112</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.628">
        <h1 class="shn">148.628 RECIPROCITY.</h1>
        <p>The board may issue a license to an applicant who is licensed as a dietitian or nutritionist in another state or the District of Columbia, provided that in the judgment of the board the standards for licensure in that state are not less stringent than the requirements set forth in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.628.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/613/#laws.0.9.0">1994 c 613 s 9</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.629">
        <h1 class="shn">148.629 DENIAL, SUSPENSION, OR REVOCATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.629.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Grounds.</span></h2>
          <p>The board may refuse to renew or grant a license to, or may suspend, revoke, or restrict the license of an individual whom the board, after a hearing under the contested case provisions of chapter 14, determines:</p>
          <p>(1) is incompetent to engage in dietetic or nutrition practice, or is found to be engaged in dietetic or nutrition practice in a manner harmful or dangerous to a client or to the public;</p>
          <p>(2) has violated the rules of the board or the statutes the board is empowered to enforce;</p>
          <p>(3) has obtained or attempted to obtain a license or license renewal by bribery or fraudulent representation;</p>
          <p>(4) has knowingly made a false statement on a form required by the board for licensing or license renewal; or</p>
          <p>(5) has sold any dietary supplement product if the sale of that product resulted in financial benefit to the individual.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.629.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Restoring license.</span></h2>
          <p>For reasons it finds sufficient, the board may grant a license previously refused, restore a license that has been revoked, or reduce a period of suspension or restriction of a license.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.629.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Review.</span></h2>
          <p>Suspension, revocation, or restriction of a license must be reviewed by the board at the request of the licensee against whom the disciplinary action was taken.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.629.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/613/#laws.0.10.0">1994 c 613 s 10</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.630">
        <h1 class="shn">148.630 LICENSE REQUIRED.</h1>
        <p>(a) No person may engage in dietetics or nutrition practice unless the person is licensed as a dietitian or nutritionist by the board. No person may use the title "dietitian," "licensed dietitian," "nutritionist," "licensed nutritionist," or any occupational title using the word "dietitian" or "nutritionist" unless so licensed by the board, nor shall any person hold out as a dietitian or nutritionist unless so licensed.</p>
        <p>(b) Notwithstanding any other provision of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a>, a dietitian registered by the commission shall have the right to use the title "registered dietitian" and the designation "RD." Notwithstanding any other provision of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a>, a dietetic technician registered by the Commission on Dietetic Registration shall have the right to use the title "dietetic technician registered" and the designation "DTR."</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.630.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/613/#laws.0.11.0">1994 c 613 s 11</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.631">
        <h1 class="shn">148.631 PENALTY.</h1>
        <p>A person who violates sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a> is guilty of a misdemeanor. If a person other than a licensed dietitian or nutritionist engages in an act or practice constituting an offense under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a>, a district court on application of the board may issue an injunction or other appropriate order restraining the act or practice.</p>
        <p>If the board finds that a licensed dietitian or nutritionist has violated a provision of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a> or rules adopted under them, it may impose a civil penalty not exceeding $10,000 for each separate violation, the amount of the civil penalty to be fixed so as to deprive the dietitian or nutritionist of any economic advantage gained by reason of the violation charged, to discourage similar violations, or to reimburse the board for the cost of the investigation and proceeding, including, but not limited to, fees paid for services provided by the Office of Administrative Hearings, legal and investigational services provided by the Office of the Attorney General, services of court reporters, witnesses, reproduction of records, board members' per diem compensation, board staff time, and expenses incurred by board members and staff.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.631.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/613/#laws.0.12.0">1994 c 613 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/66/#laws.0.4.0">2003 c 66 s 4</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.632">
        <h1 class="shn">148.632 EXEMPTIONS; VOLUNTARY LICENSING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.632.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Persons excepted from the licensing requirement.</span></h2>
          <p>Nothing in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a> prevents or restricts the activities of:</p>
