          <p>(1) any person pursuing a degree in dietetics or nutrition at an accredited college or university who is practicing under the supervision of a licensed dietitian or licensed nutritionist and in accordance with accepted scientific knowledge and standards of practice, provided that the person is designated by a title which clearly indicates the person's status as a student or trainee;</p>
          <p>(2) any person in the process of fulfilling the professional experience requirements in dietetics or nutrition necessary for licensure who is practicing under the supervision of a licensed dietitian or licensed nutritionist and in accordance with accepted scientific knowledge and standards of practice, provided that the person is designated by a title which clearly indicates the person's status as a trainee;</p>
          <p>(3) any person licensed to practice medicine, nursing, optometry, psychology, pharmacy, dentistry, or chiropractic, when nutrition practice is incidental to the practice of the person's profession and the person does not hold out as a dietitian or nutritionist unless so licensed;</p>
          <p>(4) any person, including a registered dietetic technician, dietetic technician, or other paraprofessional working in a program supervised by a licensed dietitian or nutritionist, if the person's activities are within the scope of the person's education and training and in accordance with accepted scientific knowledge and standards of practice in nutrition or dietetics and the person does not hold out as a dietitian or nutritionist unless so licensed;</p>
          <p>(5) any person who provides weight control services, provided the nutrition program has been reviewed by, consultation is available from, and no program change can be initiated without prior approval by an individual licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a>, a dietitian licensed in another state that has licensure requirements considered by the board to be at least as stringent as the requirements for licensure under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a>, or a registered dietitian, and provided that the person does not hold out as a dietitian or nutritionist unless so licensed;</p>
          <p>(6) any home economist with a baccalaureate or graduate degree from an accredited college or university, if the person's activities are within the scope of the person's education and training and in accordance with accepted scientific knowledge and standards of practice and the person does not hold out as a dietitian or nutritionist;</p>
          <p>(7) any person employed by a federal, state, county, or municipal agency, elementary or secondary school, regionally accredited institution of higher education, or nonprofit agency, if the person's activities are within the scope of the person's employment and the person does not hold out as a dietitian or nutritionist unless so licensed;</p>
          <p>(8) any person who furnishes nutrition information on food, food materials, or dietary supplements or engages in the explanation to customers about foods or food products in connection with the marketing and distribution of those products provided that the person does not hold out as a dietitian or nutritionist unless so licensed;</p>
          <p>(9) any person who is recognized in the community as a provider of nutritional advice, including a curandero or medicine man or woman, and who advises people according to or based on traditional practices provided the person does not hold out as a dietitian or nutritionist unless so licensed;</p>
          <p>(10) any animal nutritionist who does not meet the requirements of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a>, provided that the person's activities are limited to the nutritional care of animals. Animal nutritionists may continue to use the title nutritionist so long as they provide nutrition services only to animals;</p>
          <p>(11) any person who provides nutrition services without remuneration to family members; or</p>
          <p>(12) any person involved in dietary or nutritional counseling pursuant to a research study supervised by a Minnesota institution of higher learning or state agency which has been approved by an institutional review board to ensure the informed consent and safety of study participants.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.632.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Voluntary licensing.</span></h2>
          <p>The licensing of persons employed by facilities licensed under chapters 144 and 144A is voluntary. Nothing in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a> prevents or restricts the activities of persons employed by these institutions.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.632.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/613/#laws.0.13.0">1994 c 613 s 13</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.633">
        <h1 class="shn">148.633 DISPOSITION OF FUNDS.</h1>
        <p>Money received by the board under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.621">148.621</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.633">148.633</a> must be credited to the health occupations licensing account within the special revenue fund.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.633.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/613/#laws.0.14.0">1994 c 613 s 14</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.634">
        <h1 class="shn">148.634 PRESCRIPTION PROTOCOL.</h1>
        <p>A licensed dietitian or licensed nutritionist may implement a protocol that does not reference a specific patient and results in a prescription of a legend drug that has been predetermined and delegated by a licensed practitioner as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/151.01">151.01</a>, subdivision 23, when caring for a patient whose condition falls within the protocol and the protocol specifies the circumstances under which the drug is to be prescribed or administered.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.634.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/55/#laws.0.1.0">2013 c 55 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.635">
        <h1 class="shn">148.635 FEE.</h1>
        <p>The fee for verification of licensure is $20. The fee is nonrefundable.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.635.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 70 art 6 s 16</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">OCCUPATIONAL THERAPISTS AND OCCUPATIONAL<br>THERAPY ASSISTANTS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.6401">
        <h1 class="shn">148.6401 SCOPE.</h1>
        <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6401">148.6401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a> apply to persons who are applicants for licensure, who are licensed, who use protected titles, or who represent that they are licensed as occupational therapists or occupational therapy assistants.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.6401.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/361/#laws.0.1.0">2000 c 361 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.11.54.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 11 s 54</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.6402">
        <h1 class="shn">148.6402 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purpose of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6401">148.6401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a>, the following terms have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.11.56.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 11 s 56</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Biennial licensure period.</span></h2>
          <p>"Biennial licensure period" means the two-year period for which licensure is effective.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Board.</span></h2>
          <p>"Board" means the Board of Occupational Therapy Practice established in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Contact hour.</span></h2>
          <p>"Contact hour" means an instructional session of 60 minutes, excluding coffee breaks, registration, meals without a speaker, and social activities.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Credential.</span></h2>
          <p>"Credential" means a license, permit, certification, registration, or other evidence of qualification or authorization to engage in the practice of occupational therapy issued by any authority.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Credentialing examination for occupational therapist.</span></h2>
          <p>"Credentialing examination for occupational therapist" means the examination sponsored by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy for credentialing as an occupational therapist, registered.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Credentialing examination for occupational therapy assistant.</span></h2>
          <p>"Credentialing examination for occupational therapy assistant" means the examination sponsored by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy for credentialing as a certified occupational therapy assistant.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Delegate.</span></h2>
          <p>"Delegate" means to transfer to an occupational therapy assistant the authority to perform selected portions of an occupational therapy evaluation or treatment plan for a specific patient.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.</h2>
          <p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/79/#laws.2.26.0">2020 c 79 art 2 s 26</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.</h2>
          <p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/50/#laws.1.130.0">2019 c 50 art 1 s 130</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.</h2>
          <p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/50/#laws.1.130.0">2019 c 50 art 1 s 130</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Licensed health care professional.</span></h2>
          <p>"Licensed health care professional" means a person licensed in good standing in Minnesota to practice medicine, osteopathic medicine, chiropractic, podiatry, advanced practice registered nursing, or dentistry, or is a person registered as a physician assistant in Minnesota.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Occupational therapist.</span></h2>
          <p>"Occupational therapist" means an individual who meets the qualifications in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6401">148.6401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a> and is licensed by the board.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.15">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.</h2>
          <p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/79/#laws.2.26.0">2020 c 79 art 2 s 26</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.16">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.<span class="headnote">Occupational therapy assistant.</span></h2>
          <p>"Occupational therapy assistant" means an individual who meets the qualifications for an occupational therapy assistant in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6401">148.6401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a> and is licensed by the board.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.16a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16a.<span class="headnote">Occupational therapy practitioner.</span></h2>
          <p>"Occupational therapy practitioner" means any individual licensed as either an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6401">148.6401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.17">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17.</h2>
          <p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/50/#laws.1.130.0">2019 c 50 art 1 s 130</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.18">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 18.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/7/#laws.0.91.0">2001 c 7 s 91</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.19">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 19.<span class="headnote">License or licensed.</span></h2>
          <p>"License" or "licensed" means the act or status of a natural person who meets the requirements of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6401">148.6401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.20">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 20.<span class="headnote">Licensee.</span></h2>
          <p>"Licensee" means a person who meets the requirements of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6401">148.6401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.21">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 21.<span class="headnote">Licensure by equivalency.</span></h2>
          <p>"Licensure by equivalency" means a method of licensure described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6412">148.6412</a> by which an individual who possesses a current credential from the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy may qualify for licensure.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.22">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 22.<span class="headnote">Licensure by reciprocity.</span></h2>
          <p>"Licensure by reciprocity" means a method of licensure described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6415">148.6415</a> by which an individual who possesses a credential from another jurisdiction may qualify for Minnesota licensure.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.22a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 22a.<span class="headnote">Limited license.</span></h2>
          <p>"Limited license" means a license issued according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6425#stat.148.6425.3">148.6425, subdivision 3</a>, paragraph (c), to persons who for two years or more did not apply for a license after meeting the requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6408">148.6408</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6410">148.6410</a> or who allowed their license to lapse for four years or more.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.23">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 23.<span class="headnote">Service competency.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) "Service competency" of an occupational therapy assistant in performing evaluation tasks means the ability of an occupational therapy assistant to obtain the same information as the supervising occupational therapist when evaluating a client's function.</p>
          <p>(b) "Service competency" of an occupational therapy assistant in performing treatment procedures means the ability of an occupational therapy assistant to perform treatment procedures in a manner such that the outcome, documentation, and follow-up are equivalent to that which would have been achieved had the supervising occupational therapist performed the treatment procedure.</p>
          <p>(c) "Service competency" of an occupational therapist means the ability of an occupational therapist to consistently perform an assessment task or intervention procedure with the level of skill recognized as satisfactory within the appropriate acceptable prevailing practice of occupational therapy.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.24">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 24.</h2>
          <p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/50/#laws.1.130.0">2019 c 50 art 1 s 130</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.25">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 25.<span class="headnote">Temporary licensure.</span></h2>
          <p>"Temporary licensure" means a method of licensure described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6418">148.6418</a>, by which an individual who (1) has completed an approved or accredited education program but has not met the examination requirement; or (2) possesses a credential from another jurisdiction or the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy but who has not submitted the documentation required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6420">148.6420</a>, subdivisions 3 and 4, may qualify for Minnesota licensure for a limited time period.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6402.26">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 26.</h2>
          <p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/50/#laws.1.130.0">2019 c 50 art 1 s 130</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.6402.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/361/#laws.0.2.0">2000 c 361 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/7/#laws.0.35.0">2001 c 7 s 35</a>,36; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/279/#laws.1.19.0">2004 c 279 art 1 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/157/#laws.1.8.0">2009 c 157 art 1 s 8</a>,9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/43/#laws.0.28.0">2013 c 43 s 28</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.4.10.0">2014 c 291 art 4 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/119/#laws.0.7.0">2016 c 119 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.11.7.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 11 s 7</a>,54; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/50/#laws.1.46.0">2019 c 50 art 1 s 46</a>,47; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/79/#laws.2.1.0">2020 c 79 art 2 s 1</a>,2</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.6403">
        <h1 class="shn">148.6403 LICENSURE; PROTECTED TITLES AND RESTRICTIONS ON USE; EXEMPT PERSONS; SANCTIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6403.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Unlicensed practice prohibited.</span></h2>
          <p>A person must not engage in the practice of occupational therapy unless the person is licensed as an occupational therapy practitioner in accordance with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6401">148.6401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6403.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Protected titles and restrictions on use.</span></h2>
          <p>Use of the phrase "occupational therapy" or "occupational therapist," or the initials "OT" alone or in combination with any other words or initials to form an occupational title, or to indicate or imply that the person is licensed by the state as an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant, is prohibited unless that person is licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6401">148.6401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6403.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Use of "Minnesota licensed."</span></h2>
          <p>Use of the term "Minnesota licensed" in conjunction with titles protected under this section by any person is prohibited unless that person is licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6401">148.6401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6403.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Persons licensed or certified in other states.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who is licensed in Minnesota and licensed or certified in another state may use the designation "licensed" or "certified" with a protected title only if the state of licensure or certification is clearly indicated.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6403.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Exempt persons.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not apply to:</p>
          <p>(1) a person employed as an occupational therapy practitioner by the government of the United States or any agency of it. However, use of the protected titles under those circumstances is allowed only in connection with performance of official duties for the federal government;</p>
          <p>(2) a student participating in supervised fieldwork or supervised coursework that is necessary to meet the requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6408#stat.148.6408.1">148.6408, subdivision 1</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6410#stat.148.6410.1">148.6410, subdivision 1</a>, if the person is designated by a title which clearly indicates the person's status as a student trainee. Any use of the protected titles under these circumstances is allowed only while the person is performing the duties of the supervised fieldwork or supervised coursework; or</p>
          <p>(3) a person visiting and then leaving the state and performing occupational therapy services while in the state, if the services are performed no more than 30 days in a calendar year as part of a professional activity that is limited in scope and duration and is in association with an occupational therapist licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6401">148.6401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a>, and</p>
          <p>(i) the person is credentialed under the law of another state which has credentialing requirements at least as stringent as the requirements of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6401">148.6401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a>; or</p>
          <p>(ii) the person meets the requirements for certification as an occupational therapist registered (OTR) or a certified occupational therapy assistant (COTA), established by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6403.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Sanctions.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who practices occupational therapy or holds out as an occupational therapy practitioner by or through the use of any title described in subdivision 2 without prior licensure according to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6401">148.6401 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a> is subject to sanctions or action against continuing the activity according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6448">148.6448</a>, chapter 214, or other statutory authority.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6403.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Exemption.</span></h2>
          <p>Nothing in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6401">148.6401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a> shall prohibit the practice of any profession or occupation licensed or registered by the state by any person duly licensed or registered to practice the profession or occupation or to perform any act that falls within the scope of practice of the profession or occupation.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.6403.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/361/#laws.0.3.0">2000 c 361 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/279/#laws.1.20.0">2004 c 279 art 1 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.11.54.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 11 s 54</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/79/#laws.2.3.0">2020 c 79 art 2 s 3</a>-5</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.6404">
        <h1 class="shn">148.6404 SCOPE OF PRACTICE.</h1>
        <p>(a) The practice of occupational therapy means the therapeutic use of everyday activities with individuals or groups for the purpose of enhancing or enabling participation. It is the promotion of health and well-being through the use of occupational therapy services that includes screening, evaluation, intervention, and consultation to develop, recover, and maintain a client's:</p>
        <p>(1) sensory integrative, neuromuscular, motor, emotional, motivational, cognitive, or psychosocial components of performance;</p>
        <p>(2) daily living skills;</p>
        <p>(3) feeding and swallowing skills;</p>
        <p>(4) play and leisure skills;</p>
        <p>(5) educational participation skills;</p>
        <p>(6) functional performance and work participation skills;</p>
        <p>(7) community mobility; and</p>
        <p>(8) health and wellness.</p>
        <p class="in">(b) Occupational therapy services include but are not limited to:</p>
        <p>(1) designing, fabricating, or applying rehabilitative technology, such as selected orthotic and prosthetic devices, and providing training in the functional use of these devices;</p>
        <p>(2) designing, fabricating, or adapting assistive technology and providing training in the functional use of assistive devices;</p>
        <p>(3) adapting environments using assistive technology such as environmental controls, wheelchair modifications, and positioning; and</p>
        <p>(4) employing physical agent modalities in preparation for or as an adjunct to purposeful activity to meet established functional occupational therapy goals.</p>
        <p>(c) Occupational therapy services must be based on nationally established standards of practice.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.6404.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/361/#laws.0.4.0">2000 c 361 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.4.11.0">2014 c 291 art 4 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/79/#laws.2.6.0">2020 c 79 art 2 s 6</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.6405">
        <h1 class="shn">148.6405 LICENSURE APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS: PROCEDURES AND QUALIFICATIONS.</h1>
        <p>(a) An applicant for licensure must comply with the application requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6420">148.6420</a>. To qualify for licensure, an applicant must satisfy one of the requirements in paragraphs (b) to (f) and not be subject to denial of licensure under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6448">148.6448</a>.</p>
        <p>(b) A person who applies for licensure as an occupational therapist and who has not been credentialed by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy or another jurisdiction must meet the requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6408">148.6408</a>.</p>
        <p>(c) A person who applies for licensure as an occupational therapy assistant and who has not been credentialed by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy or another jurisdiction must meet the requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6410">148.6410</a>.</p>
        <p>(d) A person who is certified by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy may apply for licensure by equivalency and must meet the requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6412">148.6412</a>.</p>
        <p>(e) A person who is credentialed in another jurisdiction and who was previously certified by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy may apply for licensure by reciprocity and must meet the requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6415">148.6415</a>.</p>
        <p>(f) A person who applies for temporary licensure must meet the requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6418">148.6418</a>.</p>
        <p>(g) A person who applies for licensure under paragraph (b), (c), or (f) more than two and less than four years after meeting the examination requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6408#stat.148.6408.2">148.6408, subdivision 2,</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6410#stat.148.6410.2">148.6410, subdivision 2, </a>must submit the following:</p>
        <p>(1) a completed and signed application for licensure on forms provided by the board;</p>
        <p>(2) the license application fee required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6445">148.6445</a>;</p>
        <p>(3) if applying for occupational therapist licensure, proof of having met a minimum of 24 contact hours of continuing education in the two years preceding licensure application, or if applying for occupational therapy assistant licensure, proof of having met a minimum of 18 contact hours of continuing education in the two years preceding licensure application;</p>
        <p>(4) verified documentation of successful completion of 160 hours of supervised practice approved by the board under a limited license specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6425#stat.148.6425.3">148.6425, subdivision 3</a>, paragraph (c); and</p>
        <p>(5) additional information as requested by the board to clarify information in the application, including information to determine whether the individual has engaged in conduct warranting disciplinary action under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6448">148.6448</a>. The information must be submitted within 30 calendar days from the date of the board's request.</p>
        <p>(h) A person who applies for licensure under paragraph (b), (c), or (f) four years or more after meeting the examination requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6408">148.6408</a>, subdivision 2, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6410">148.6410</a>, subdivision 2, must:</p>
        <p>(1) meet all the requirements in paragraph (g) except clauses (3) and (4);</p>
        <p>(2) submit documentation of having retaken and achieved a qualifying score on the credentialing examination for occupational therapists or occupational therapy assistants, or of having completed an occupational therapy refresher program that contains both a theoretical and clinical component approved by the board; and</p>
        <p>(3) submit verified documentation of successful completion of 480 hours of supervised practice approved by the board under a limited license specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6425#stat.148.6425.3">148.6425, subdivision 3</a>, paragraph (c). The 480 hours of supervised practice must be completed in six months and may be completed at the applicant's place of work. Only refresher courses completed within one year prior to the date of application qualify for approval.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.6405.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/361/#laws.0.5.0">2000 c 361 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/279/#laws.1.21.0">2004 c 279 art 1 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/157/#laws.1.10.0">2009 c 157 art 1 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/274/#laws.0.4.0">2010 c 274 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.11.8.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 11 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/79/#laws.2.7.0">2020 c 79 art 2 s 7</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.6408">
        <h1 class="shn">148.6408 QUALIFICATIONS FOR OCCUPATIONAL THERAPIST.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6408.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Education required.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An applicant who has received professional education in the United States or its possessions or territories must successfully complete all academic and fieldwork requirements of an educational program for occupational therapists approved or accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education.</p>
          <p>(b) An applicant who has received professional education outside the United States or its possessions or territories must successfully complete all academic and fieldwork requirements of an educational program for occupational therapists approved by a member association of the World Federation of Occupational Therapists.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6408.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Qualifying examination score required.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An applicant must achieve a qualifying score on the credentialing examination for occupational therapist.</p>
          <p>(b) The board shall determine the qualifying score for the credentialing examination for occupational therapist. In determining the qualifying score, the board shall consider the cut score recommended by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy, or other national credentialing organization approved by the board, using the modified Angoff method for determining cut score or another method for determining cut score that is recognized as appropriate and acceptable by industry standards.</p>
          <p>(c) The applicant is responsible for:</p>
          <p>(1) making arrangements to take the credentialing examination for occupational therapist;</p>
          <p>(2) bearing all expenses associated with taking the examination; and</p>
          <p>(3) having the examination scores sent directly to the board from the testing service that administers the examination.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.6408.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/361/#laws.0.6.0">2000 c 361 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.11.9.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 11 s 9</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.6410">
        <h1 class="shn">148.6410 QUALIFICATIONS FOR OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY ASSISTANTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6410.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Education required.</span></h2>
          <p>An applicant must successfully complete all academic and fieldwork requirements of an occupational therapy assistant program approved or accredited by the Accreditation Council for Occupational Therapy Education.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6410.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Qualifying examination score required.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An applicant for licensure must achieve a qualifying score on the credentialing examination for occupational therapy assistants.</p>
          <p>(b) The board shall determine the qualifying score for the credentialing examination for occupational therapy assistants. In determining the qualifying score, the board shall consider the cut score recommended by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy, or other national credentialing organization approved by the board, using the modified Angoff method for determining cut score or another method for determining cut score that is recognized as appropriate and acceptable by industry standards.</p>
          <p>(c) The applicant is responsible for:</p>
          <p>(1) making all arrangements to take the credentialing examination for occupational therapy assistants;</p>
          <p>(2) bearing all expense associated with taking the examination; and</p>
          <p>(3) having the examination scores sent directly to the board from the testing service that administers the examination.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.6410.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/361/#laws.0.7.0">2000 c 361 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.11.10.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 11 s 10</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.6412">
        <h1 class="shn">148.6412 LICENSURE BY EQUIVALENCY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6412.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.</h2>
          <p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/79/#laws.2.26.0">2020 c 79 art 2 s 26</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6412.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Persons certified by National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy.</span></h2>
          <p>The board may license any person certified by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy as an occupational therapist if the board determines the requirements for certification are equivalent to or exceed the requirements for licensure as an occupational therapist under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6408">148.6408</a>. The board may license any person certified by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy as an occupational therapy assistant if the board determines the requirements for certification are equivalent to or exceed the requirements for licensure as an occupational therapy assistant under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6410">148.6410</a>. Nothing in this section limits the board's authority to deny licensure based upon the grounds for discipline in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6401">148.6401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6412.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Application procedures.</span></h2>
          <p>Applicants for licensure by equivalency must provide:</p>
          <p>(1) the application materials as required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6420">148.6420, subdivisions 1, 3, and 4</a>; and</p>
          <p>(2) the fees required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6445">148.6445</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.6412.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/361/#laws.0.8.0">2000 c 361 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.11.11.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 11 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/79/#laws.2.8.0">2020 c 79 art 2 s 8</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.6415">
        <h1 class="shn">148.6415 LICENSURE BY RECIPROCITY.</h1>
        <p>A person who is not certified by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy but who holds a current credential as an occupational therapist in the District of Columbia or a state or territory of the United States whose standards for credentialing are determined by the board to be equivalent to or exceed the requirements for licensure under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6408">148.6408</a> may be eligible for licensure by reciprocity as an occupational therapist. A person who is not certified by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy but who holds a current credential as an occupational therapy assistant in the District of Columbia or a state or territory of the United States whose standards for credentialing are determined by the board to be equivalent to or exceed the requirements for licensure under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6410">148.6410</a> may be eligible for licensure by reciprocity as an occupational therapy assistant. Nothing in this section limits the board's authority to deny licensure based upon the grounds for discipline in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6401">148.6401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a>. An applicant must provide:</p>
        <p>(1) the application materials as required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6420">148.6420, subdivisions 1, 3, and 4</a>;</p>
        <p>(2) the fees required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6445">148.6445</a>;</p>
        <p>(3) a copy of a current and unrestricted credential for the practice of occupational therapy as either an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant;</p>
        <p>(4) a letter from the jurisdiction that issued the credential describing the applicant's qualifications that entitled the applicant to receive the credential; and</p>
        <p>(5) other information necessary to determine whether the credentialing standards of the jurisdiction that issued the credential are equivalent to or exceed the requirements for licensure under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6401">148.6401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6449">148.6449</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.6415.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/361/#laws.0.9.0">2000 c 361 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.11.12.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 11 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/79/#laws.2.9.0">2020 c 79 art 2 s 9</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.6418">
        <h1 class="shn">148.6418 TEMPORARY LICENSURE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6418.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Application.</span></h2>
          <p>The board shall issue temporary licensure as an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant to applicants who are not the subject of a disciplinary action or past disciplinary action, nor disqualified on the basis of items listed in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6448#stat.148.6448.1">148.6448, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6418.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Procedures.</span></h2>
          <p>To be eligible for temporary licensure, an applicant must submit a completed application for temporary licensure on forms provided by the board, the fees required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6445">148.6445</a>, and one of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) evidence of successful completion of the requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6408#stat.148.6408.1">148.6408, subdivision 1</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6410#stat.148.6410.1">148.6410, subdivision 1</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) a copy of a current and unrestricted credential for the practice of occupational therapy as either an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant in another jurisdiction; or</p>
          <p>(3) a copy of a current and unrestricted certificate from the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy stating that the applicant is certified as an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6418.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Additional documentation.</span></h2>
          <p>Persons who are credentialed by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy or another jurisdiction must provide an affidavit with the application for temporary licensure stating that they are not the subject of a pending investigation or disciplinary action and have not been the subject of a disciplinary action in the past.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6418.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Supervision required.</span></h2>
          <p>An applicant who has graduated from an accredited occupational therapy program, as required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6408#stat.148.6408.1">148.6408, subdivision 1</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6410#stat.148.6410.1">148.6410, subdivision 1</a>, and who has not passed the examination required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6408#stat.148.6408.2">148.6408, subdivision 2</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6410#stat.148.6410.2">148.6410, subdivision 2</a>, must practice under the supervision of a licensed occupational therapist. The supervising therapist must, at a minimum, supervise the person working under temporary licensure in the performance of the initial evaluation, determination of the appropriate intervention plan, and periodic review and modification of the intervention plan. The supervising therapist must observe the person working under temporary licensure in order to ensure service competency in carrying out evaluation, intervention planning, and intervention implementation. The frequency of face-to-face collaboration between the person working under temporary licensure and the supervising therapist must be based on the condition of each patient or client, the complexity of intervention and evaluation procedures, and the proficiencies of the person practicing under temporary licensure. Following demonstrated service competency of the applicant, supervision must occur no less than every ten intervention days or every 30 calendar days, whichever occurs first. The occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant working under temporary licensure must provide verification of supervision on the application form provided by the board.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6418.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Qualifying examination requirement; expiration and renewability.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A person issued a temporary license pursuant to subdivision 2, clause (1), must demonstrate to the board within the temporary licensure period successful completion of the qualifying examination requirement under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6408#stat.148.6408.2">148.6408, subdivision 2</a>, or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6410#stat.148.6410.2">148.6410, subdivision 2</a>. A temporary license holder who fails the qualifying examination for a second time shall have their temporary license revoked effective upon notification to the temporary license holder of the examination score. It is the temporary license holder's obligation to submit to the board their qualifying examination scores and to refrain from practice if their temporary license is revoked. Failure to do so subjects the temporary license holder to disciplinary action pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6448#stat.148.6448.1">148.6448, subdivision 1</a>, clause (5).</p>
          <p>(b) A temporary license expires six months from the date of issuance or on the date the board grants or denies licensure, whichever occurs first.</p>
          <p>(c) A temporary license is not renewable.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.6418.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/361/#laws.0.10.0">2000 c 361 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/228/#laws.0.1.0">2002 c 228 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/0/274/#laws.0.5.0">2010 c 274 s 5</a>,6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.11.13.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 11 s 13</a>-16; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/79/#laws.2.10.0">2020 c 79 art 2 s 10</a>,11</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.6420">
        <h1 class="shn">148.6420 APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6420.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Applications for licensure.</span></h2>
          <p>An applicant for licensure must:</p>
          <p>(1) submit a completed application for licensure on forms provided by the board and must supply the information requested on the application, including:</p>
          <p>(i) the applicant's name, business address and business telephone number, business setting, primary email address, and daytime telephone number;</p>
          <p>(ii) the name and location of the occupational therapy program the applicant completed;</p>
          <p>(iii) a description of the applicant's education and training, including a list of degrees received from educational institutions;</p>
          <p>(iv) the applicant's work history for the six years preceding the application;</p>
          <p>(v) a list of all credentials currently and previously held in Minnesota and other jurisdictions;</p>
          <p>(vi) a description of any jurisdiction's refusal to credential the applicant;</p>
          <p>(vii) a description of all professional disciplinary actions initiated against the applicant in any jurisdiction;</p>
          <p>(viii) information on any physical or mental condition or substance use disorder that impairs the person's ability to engage in the practice of occupational therapy with reasonable judgment or safety;</p>
          <p>(ix) a description of any misdemeanor or felony conviction that relates to honesty or to the practice of occupational therapy; and</p>
          <p>(x) a description of any state or federal court order, including a conciliation court judgment or a disciplinary order, related to the individual's occupational therapy practice;</p>
          <p>(2) submit with the application all fees required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6445">148.6445</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) sign a statement that the information in the application is true and correct to the best of the applicant's knowledge and belief;</p>
          <p>(4) sign a waiver authorizing the board to obtain access to the applicant's records in this or any other state in which the applicant holds or previously held a credential for the practice of an occupation, has completed an accredited occupational therapy education program, or engaged in the practice of occupational therapy;</p>
          <p>(5) submit additional information as requested by the board; and</p>
          <p>(6) submit the additional information required for licensure by equivalency, licensure by reciprocity, and temporary licensure as specified in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6408">148.6408</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6418">148.6418</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6420.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Persons applying for licensure under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6408">148.6408</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6410">148.6410</a>. </span></h2>
          <p>Persons applying for licensure under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6408">148.6408</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6410">148.6410</a> must submit the materials required in subdivision 1 and the following:</p>
          <p>(1) a certificate of successful completion of the requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6408#stat.148.6408.1">148.6408, subdivision 1</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6410#stat.148.6410.1">148.6410, subdivision 1</a>; and</p>
          <p>(2) the applicant's test results from the examining agency, as evidence that the applicant received a qualifying score on a credentialing examination meeting the requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6408#stat.148.6408.2">148.6408, subdivision 2</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6410#stat.148.6410.2">148.6410, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6420.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Applicants certified by National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy.</span></h2>
          <p>An applicant who is certified by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy must provide the materials required in subdivision 1 and the following:</p>
          <p>(1) verified documentation from the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy stating that the applicant is certified as an occupational therapist, registered or certified occupational therapy assistant, the date certification was granted, and the applicant's certification number. The document must also include a statement regarding disciplinary actions. The applicant is responsible for obtaining this documentation by sending a form provided by the board to the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy; and</p>
          <p>(2) a waiver authorizing the board to obtain access to the applicant's records maintained by the National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6420.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Applicants credentialed in another jurisdiction.</span></h2>
          <p>In addition to providing the materials required in subdivision 1, an applicant credentialed in another jurisdiction must request that the appropriate government body in each jurisdiction in which the applicant holds or held an occupational therapy credential provide documentation to the board that verifies the applicant's credentials. Except as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6418">148.6418</a>, a license must not be issued until the board receives verification of each of the applicant's credentials. Each verification must include the applicant's name and date of birth, credential number and date of issuance, a statement regarding investigations pending and disciplinary actions taken or pending against the applicant, current status of the credential, and the terms under which the credential was issued.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6420.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Action on applications for licensure.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The board shall approve, approve with conditions, or deny licensure. The board shall act on an application for licensure according to paragraphs (b) to (d).</p>
          <p>(b) The board shall determine if the applicant meets the requirements for licensure. The board may investigate information provided by an applicant to determine whether the information is accurate and complete.</p>
          <p>(c) The board shall notify an applicant of action taken on the application and, if licensure is denied or approved with conditions, the grounds for the board's determination.</p>
          <p>(d) An applicant denied licensure or granted licensure with conditions may make a written request to the board, within 30 days of the date of the board's determination, for reconsideration of the board's determination. Individuals requesting reconsideration may submit information which the applicant wants considered in the reconsideration. After reconsideration of the board's determination to deny licensure or grant licensure with conditions, the board shall determine whether the original determination should be affirmed or modified. An applicant is allowed no more than one request in any one biennial licensure period for reconsideration of the board's determination to deny licensure or approve licensure with conditions.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.6420.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/361/#laws.0.11.0">2000 c 361 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/7/#laws.0.37.0">2001 c 7 s 37</a>,38; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.11.17.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 11 s 17</a>-19; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/50/#laws.1.48.0">2019 c 50 art 1 s 48</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/79/#laws.2.12.0">2020 c 79 art 2 s 12</a>-14; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/98/#laws.4.51.0">2022 c 98 art 4 s 51</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.6423">
        <h1 class="shn">148.6423 LICENSURE RENEWAL.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6423.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Renewal requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>To be eligible for licensure renewal, a licensee must:</p>
          <p>(1) submit a completed and signed application for licensure renewal;</p>
          <p>(2) submit the renewal fee required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6445">148.6445</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) submit proof of having met the continuing education requirement of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6443">148.6443</a>; and</p>
          <p>(4) submit additional information as requested by the board to clarify information presented in the renewal application. The information must be submitted within 30 calendar days of the board's request.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6423.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Renewal deadline.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as provided in paragraph (c), licenses must be renewed every two years. Licensees must comply with the following procedures in paragraphs (b) to (e).</p>
          <p>(b) Each license must state an expiration date. An application for licensure renewal must be received by the board at least 30 calendar days before the expiration date.</p>
          <p>(c) If the board changes the renewal schedule and the expiration date is less than two years, the fee and the continuing education contact hours to be reported at the next renewal must be prorated.</p>
          <p>(d) An application for licensure renewal not received within the time required under paragraph (b), but received on or before the expiration date, must be accompanied by a late fee in addition to the renewal fee specified by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6445">148.6445</a>.</p>
          <p>(e) Licensure renewals received after the expiration date must comply with the requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6425">148.6425</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6423.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Licensure renewal notice.</span></h2>
          <p>At least 60 days before the expiration date in subdivision 2, the board must send or transmit a renewal notice to the licensee. The notice must include information about accessing the license renewal and fee schedule. The licensee's failure to receive notice does not relieve the licensee of the obligation to meet the renewal deadline and other requirements for licensure renewal.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6423.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">License renewal cycle conversion.</span></h2>
          <p>The license renewal cycle for occupational therapy licensees is converted to a two-year cycle where renewal is due on the last day of the licensee's month of birth. Conversion pursuant to this section begins January 1, 2021. This section governs license renewal procedures for licensees who were licensed before December 31, 2020. The conversion renewal cycle is the renewal cycle following the first license renewal after January 1, 2020. The conversion license period is the license period for the conversion renewal cycle. The conversion license period is between 13 and 24 months and ends on the last day of the licensee's month of birth in either 2022 or 2023, as described in subdivision 5.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6423.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Conversion of license renewal cycle for current licensees.</span></h2>
          <p>For a licensee whose license is current as of December 31, 2020, the licensee's conversion license period begins on January 1, 2021, and ends on the last day of the licensee's month of birth in 2023, except that for licensees whose month of birth is January, February, March, April, May, or June, the licensee's renewal cycle ends on the last day of the licensee's month of birth in 2022.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6423.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Conversion of license renewal cycle for noncurrent licensees.</span></h2>
          <p>This subdivision applies to a licensee who was licensed before December 31, 2020, but whose license is not current as of December 31, 2020. When the licensee first renews the license after January 1, 2021, the conversion renewal cycle begins on the date the licensee applies for renewal and ends on the last day of the licensee's month of birth in the next year, except that if the last day of the licensee's month of birth is less than six months after the date the licensee applies for renewal, then the renewal period ends on the last day of the licensee's month of birth two years after the date of renewal.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6423.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Subsequent renewal cycles.</span></h2>
          <p>After the licensee's conversion renewal cycle under subdivision 5 or 6, subsequent renewal cycles are biennial and begin on the first day of the month following the licensee's birth month.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6423.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Conversion period and fees.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A licensee who holds a license issued before January 1, 2021, and who renews that license pursuant to subdivision 5 or 6, must pay a renewal fee as required in this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(b) A licensee must be charged the biennial license fee listed in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6445">148.6445</a> for the conversion license period.</p>
          <p>(c) For a licensee whose conversion license period is 13 to 24 months, the first biennial license fee charged after the conversion license period must be adjusted to credit the excess fee payment made during the conversion license period. The credit is calculated by:</p>
          <p>(1) subtracting the number of months of the licensee's conversion license period from 24; and</p>
          <p>(2) multiplying the result of clause (1) by 1/24 of the biennial fee rounded up to the next dollar.</p>
          <p>(d) For a licensee whose conversion license period is 24 months, the first biennial license fee charged after the conversion license period must not be adjusted.</p>
          <p>(e) For the second and all subsequent license renewals made after the conversion license period, the licensee's biennial license fee is as listed in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6445">148.6445</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6423.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Expiration.</span></h2>
          <p>Subdivisions 4, 5, 7, and 8 expire December 31, 2023.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.6423.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/361/#laws.0.12.0">2000 c 361 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.11.20.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 11 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/79/#laws.2.15.0">2020 c 79 art 2 s 15</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.6425">
        <h1 class="shn">148.6425 RENEWAL OF LICENSURE; AFTER EXPIRATION DATE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6425.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Removal of name from list.</span></h2>
          <p>The names of licensees who do not comply with the licensure renewal requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6423">148.6423</a> on or before the expiration date shall be removed from the list of individuals authorized to practice occupational therapy and to use the protected titles in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6403">148.6403</a>. The licensees must comply with the requirements of this section in order to regain licensed status.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6425.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Licensure renewal after licensure expiration date.</span></h2>
          <p>A licensee whose application for licensure renewal is received after the licensure expiration date must submit the following:</p>
          <p>(1) a completed and signed application for licensure following lapse in licensed status;</p>
          <p>(2) the renewal fee and the late fee required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6445">148.6445</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) proof of having met the continuing education requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6443#stat.148.6443.1">148.6443, subdivision 1</a>; and</p>
          <p>(4) additional information as requested by the board to clarify information in the application, including information to determine whether the licensee has engaged in conduct warranting disciplinary action as set forth in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6448">148.6448</a>. The information must be submitted within 30 calendar days from the date of the board's request.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6425.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Licensure renewal four years or more after licensure expiration date.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An individual who requests licensure renewal four years or more after the licensure expiration date must submit the following:</p>
          <p>(1) a completed and signed application for licensure on forms provided by the board;</p>
          <p>(2) the renewal fee and the late fee required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6445">148.6445</a> if renewal application is based on paragraph (b), clause (1), (2), or (3), or the renewal fee required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6445">148.6445</a> if renewal application is based on paragraph (b), clause (4);</p>
          <p>(3) proof of having met the continuing education requirement in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6443#stat.148.6443.1">148.6443, subdivision 1</a>, except the continuing education must be obtained in the two years immediately preceding application renewal; and</p>
          <p>(4) at the time of the next licensure renewal, proof of having met the continuing education requirement, which shall be prorated based on the number of months licensed during the two-year licensure period.</p>
          <p>(b) In addition to the requirements in paragraph (a), the applicant must submit proof of one of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) verified documentation of successful completion of 160 hours of supervised practice approved by the board as described in paragraph (c);</p>
          <p>(2) verified documentation of having achieved a qualifying score on the credentialing examination for occupational therapists or the credentialing examination for occupational therapy assistants administered within the past year;</p>
          <p>(3) documentation of having completed a combination of occupational therapy courses or an occupational therapy refresher program that contains both a theoretical and clinical component approved by the board. Only courses completed within one year preceding the date of the application or one year after the date of the application qualify for approval; or</p>
          <p>(4) evidence that the applicant holds a current and unrestricted credential for the practice of occupational therapy in another jurisdiction and that the applicant's credential from that jurisdiction has been held in good standing during the period of lapse.</p>
          <p>(c) To participate in a supervised practice as described in paragraph (b), clause (1), the applicant shall obtain limited licensure. To apply for limited licensure, the applicant shall submit the completed limited licensure application, fees, and agreement for supervision of an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant practicing under limited licensure signed by the supervising therapist and the applicant. The supervising occupational therapist shall state the proposed level of supervision on the supervision agreement form provided by the board. The supervising therapist shall determine the frequency and manner of supervision based on the condition of the patient or client, the complexity of the procedure, and the proficiencies of the supervised occupational therapist. At a minimum, a supervising occupational therapist shall be on the premises at all times that the person practicing under limited licensure is working; be in the room ten percent of the hours worked each week by the person practicing under limited licensure; and provide daily face-to-face collaboration for the purpose of observing service competency of the occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant, discussing treatment procedures and each client's response to treatment, and reviewing and modifying, as necessary, each treatment plan. The supervising therapist shall document the supervision provided. The occupational therapist participating in a supervised practice is responsible for obtaining the supervision required under this paragraph and must comply with the board's requirements for supervision during the entire 160 hours of supervised practice. The supervised practice must be completed in two months and may be completed at the applicant's place of work.</p>
          <p>(d) In addition to the requirements in paragraphs (a) and (b), the applicant must submit additional information as requested by the board to clarify information in the application, including information to determine whether the applicant has engaged in conduct warranting disciplinary action as set forth in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6448">148.6448</a>. The information must be submitted within 30 days after the board's request.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.6425.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/361/#laws.0.13.0">2000 c 361 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/7/#laws.0.39.0">2001 c 7 s 39</a>,40; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/118/#laws.0.2.0">2003 c 118 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/189/#laws.0.14.0">2008 c 189 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.11.21.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 11 s 21</a>,22; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/79/#laws.2.16.0">2020 c 79 art 2 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.6428">
        <h1 class="shn">148.6428 CHANGE OF CONTACT INFORMATION OR EMPLOYMENT.</h1>
        <p>A licensee who changes a name, primary email address, address, employment, business address, or business telephone number must inform the board of the change of name, primary email address, address, employment, business address, or business telephone number within 30 calendar days from the effective date of the change. A change in name must be accompanied by a copy of a marriage certificate or court order. All notices or other correspondence served on a licensee by the board at the licensee's contact information on file with the board must be considered as having been received by the licensee.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.6428.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/361/#laws.0.14.0">2000 c 361 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/279/#laws.1.22.0">2004 c 279 art 1 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/189/#laws.0.15.0">2008 c 189 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.11.23.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 11 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/79/#laws.2.17.0">2020 c 79 art 2 s 17</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.6430">
        <h1 class="shn">148.6430 DELEGATION OF DUTIES; ASSIGNMENT OF TASKS.</h1>
        <p>The occupational therapist is responsible for all duties delegated to the occupational therapy assistant or tasks assigned to direct service personnel. The occupational therapist may delegate to an occupational therapy assistant those portions of a client's evaluation, reevaluation, and intervention that, according to prevailing national practice standards, can be performed by an occupational therapy assistant. The occupational therapist may not delegate portions of an evaluation or reevaluation of a person whose condition is changing rapidly.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.6430.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/361/#laws.0.15.0">2000 c 361 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.4.12.0">2014 c 291 art 4 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/79/#laws.2.18.0">2020 c 79 art 2 s 18</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.6432">
        <h1 class="shn">148.6432 SUPERVISION OF OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY ASSISTANTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6432.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Applicability.</span></h2>
          <p>If the professional standards identified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6430">148.6430</a> permit an occupational therapist to delegate an evaluation, reevaluation, or treatment procedure, the occupational therapist must provide supervision consistent with this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6432.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Evaluations.</span></h2>
          <p>The occupational therapist shall determine the frequency of evaluations and reevaluations for each client. The occupational therapy assistant shall inform the occupational therapist of the need for more frequent reevaluation if indicated by the client's condition or response to treatment. Before delegating a portion of a client's evaluation pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.6430">148.6430</a>, the occupational therapist shall ensure the service competency of the occupational therapy assistant in performing the evaluation procedure and shall provide supervision consistent with the condition of the patient or client and the complexity of the evaluation procedure.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.6432.3">
