      <div class="section" id="stat.148.965">
        <h1 class="shn">148.965 TEST SECURITY.</h1>
        <p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.292">144.292</a>, subdivisions 2 and 5, a provider shall not be required to provide copies of psychological tests, test materials, or scoring keys to any individual who has completed a test, or to an individual not qualified to administer, score, and interpret the test, if the provider reasonably determines that access would compromise the objectivity, fairness, or integrity of the testing process for the individual or others. If the provider makes this determination, the provider shall, at the discretion of the individual who has completed the test, release the information either to another provider who is qualified to administer, score, and interpret the test or instead furnish a summary of the test results to the individual or to a third party designated by the individual.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.965.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/58/#laws.0.1.0">1999 c 58 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.10.15.0">2007 c 147 art 10 s 15</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.148.97"><b>148.97</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/424/#laws.0.24.0">1996 c 424 s 24</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.975">
        <h1 class="shn">148.975 DUTY TO WARN; LIMITATION ON LIABILITY; VIOLENT BEHAVIOR OF PATIENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.975.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The definitions in this subdivision apply to this section.</p>
          <p>(b) "Other person" means an immediate family member or someone who personally knows the client and has reason to believe the client is capable of and will carry out the serious, specific threat of harm to a specific, clearly identified or identifiable victim.</p>
          <p>(c) "Reasonable efforts" means communicating the serious, specific threat to the potential victim and if unable to make contact with the potential victim, communicating the serious, specific threat to the law enforcement agency closest to the potential victim or the client.</p>
          <p>(d) For purposes of this section, "licensee" includes practicum psychology students, predoctoral psychology interns, and individuals who have earned a doctoral degree in psychology and are in the process of completing their postdoctoral supervised psychological employment in order to qualify for licensure.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.975.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Duty to warn.</span></h2>
          <p>The duty to predict, warn of, or take reasonable precautions to provide protection from, violent behavior arises only when a client or other person has communicated to the licensee a specific, serious threat of physical violence against a specific, clearly identified or identifiable potential victim. If a duty to warn arises, the duty is discharged by the licensee if reasonable efforts, as defined in subdivision 1, paragraph (c), are made to communicate the threat.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.975.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Liability standard.</span></h2>
          <p>If no duty to warn exists under subdivision 2, then no monetary liability and no cause of action may arise against a licensee for failure to predict, warn of, or take reasonable precautions to provide protection from, a client's violent behavior.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.975.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Disclosure of confidences.</span></h2>
          <p>Good faith compliance with the duty to warn shall not constitute a breach of confidence and shall not result in monetary liability or a cause of action against the licensee.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.975.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Continuity of care.</span></h2>
          <p>Nothing in subdivision 2 shall be construed to authorize a licensee to terminate treatment of a client as a direct result of a client's violent behavior or threat of physical violence unless the client is referred to another practitioner or appropriate health care facility.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.975.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Exception.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not apply to a threat to commit suicide or other threats by a client to harm the client, or to a threat by a client who is adjudicated mentally ill and dangerous under chapter 253B.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.975.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Optional disclosure.</span></h2>
          <p>Nothing in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.975">148.975</a> shall be construed to prohibit a licensee from disclosing confidences to third parties in a good faith effort to warn against or take precautions against a client's violent behavior or threat to commit suicide for which a duty to warn does not arise.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.975.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Limitation on liability.</span></h2>
          <p>No monetary liability and no cause of action, or disciplinary action by the board may arise against a licensee for disclosure of confidences to third parties, for failure to disclose confidences to third parties, or for erroneous disclosure of confidences to third parties in a good faith effort to warn against or take precautions against a client's violent behavior or threat of suicide for which a duty to warn does not arise.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.975.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/380/#laws.0.1.0">1986 c 380 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/424/#laws.0.21.0">1996 c 424 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/163/#laws.3.2.0">2016 c 163 art 3 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.148.976"><b>148.976</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/254/#laws.1.48.0">1998 c 254 art 1 s 48</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.98">
        <h1 class="shn">148.98 RULES OF CONDUCT.</h1>
        <p>The board shall adopt rules of conduct to govern an applicant's or licensee's practices or behavior. The board shall publish the rules in the State Register and file the rules with the secretary of state at least 30 days prior to the effective date of the rules. The rules of conduct shall include, but are not limited to, the principles in paragraphs (a) to (c).</p>
        <p>(a) Applicants or licensees shall recognize the boundaries of their competence and the limitations of their techniques and shall not offer services or use techniques that fail to meet usual and customary professional standards.</p>
        <p>(b) An applicant or licensee who engages in practice shall assist clients in obtaining professional help for all important aspects of the client's problems that fall outside the boundaries of the applicant's or licensee's competence.</p>
        <p>(c) Applicants or licensees shall not claim either directly or by implication professional qualifications that differ from their actual qualifications, nor shall they misrepresent their affiliations with any institution, organization, or individual, nor lead others to assume affiliations that do not exist.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.98.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/685/#laws.0.11.0">1973 c 685 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/222/#laws.0.72.0">1976 c 222 s 72</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/255/#laws.0.16.0">1991 c 255 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/206/#laws.0.19.0">1993 c 206 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/424/#laws.0.22.0">1996 c 424 s 22</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.981">
        <h1 class="shn">148.981 FEES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.981.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Licensing fees.</span></h2>
          <p>The nonrefundable fees for licensure shall be established by the board, not to exceed the following amounts:</p>
          <p>(1) application for admission to national standardized examination, $150;</p>
          <p>(2) application for professional responsibility examination, $150;</p>
          <p>(3) application for licensure as a licensed psychologist, $500;</p>
          <p>(4) renewal of license for a licensed psychologist, $500;</p>
          <p>(5) late renewal of license for a licensed psychologist, $250;</p>
          <p>(6) application for converting from master's to doctoral level licensure, $150;</p>
          <p>(7) application for guest licensure, $150;</p>
          <p>(8) certificate replacement fee, $25;</p>
          <p>(9) mailing and duplication fee, $5;</p>
          <p>(10) statute and rule book fee, $10;</p>
          <p>(11) verification fee, $20; and</p>
          <p>(12) fee for optional preapproval of postdoctoral supervision, $50.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.981.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Continuing education sponsor fee.</span></h2>
          <p>A sponsor applying for approval of a continuing education activity pursuant to Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/7200.3830">7200.3830</a>, subpart 2, shall submit with the application a fee to be established by the board, not to exceed $80 for each activity.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.981.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.10.17.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 10 s 17</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr_by_subd" id="stat.148.99">
        <h1>148.99 </h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.99.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/222/#laws.0.209.0">1976 c 222 s 209</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.99.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Expired]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CERTIFIED DOULAS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.995">
        <h1 class="shn">148.995 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.995.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Applicability.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The definitions in this section apply to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.995">148.995</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.997">148.997</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.995.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Certified doula.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">"Certified doula" means an individual who has received a certification to perform doula services from the International Childbirth Education Association, the Doulas of North America (DONA), the Association of Labor Assistants and Childbirth Educators (ALACE), Birthworks, the Childbirth and Postpartum Professional Association (CAPPA), Childbirth International, the International Center for Traditional Childbearing, Commonsense Childbirth, Inc., Modern Doula Education (MDE), or an organization designated by the commissioner under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9965">148.9965</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.995.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">"Commissioner" means the commissioner of health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.995.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Doula services.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">"Doula services" means continuous emotional and physical support throughout labor and birth, and intermittently during the prenatal and postpartum periods.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.995.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.9.27.0">2007 c 147 art 9 s 27</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/159/#laws.0.38.0">2009 c 159 s 38</a>,39; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.4.23.0">2014 c 291 art 4 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/7/#laws.4.3.0">1Sp2021 c 7 art 4 s 3</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.996">
        <h1 class="shn">148.996 REGISTRY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.996.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Establishment.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The commissioner of health shall maintain a registry of certified doulas who have met the requirements listed in subdivision 2.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.996.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Qualifications.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The commissioner shall include on the registry any individual who:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) submits an application on a form provided by the commissioner. The form must include the applicant's name, address, and contact information;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) submits evidence of maintaining a current certification from one of the organizations listed in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.995#stat.148.995.2">148.995, subdivision 2</a>, or from an organization designated by the commissioner under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9965">148.9965</a>; and</p>
          <p class="in">(3) pays the fees required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.997">148.997</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.996.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Criminal background check.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The commissioner shall conduct a criminal background check by reviewing the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension's website. If the review indicates that an applicant has been engaged in criminal behavior, the commissioner shall indicate this on the registry and provide a link to the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension's website.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.996.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Renewal.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Inclusion on the registry maintained by the commissioner is valid for three years, provided the doula meets the requirement in subdivision 2, clause (2), during the entire period. At the end of the three-year period, the certified doula may submit a new application to remain on the doula registry by meeting the requirements described in subdivision 2.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.996.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Public access.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The commissioner shall provide a link to the registry on the Department of Health's website.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.996.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Removal from registry.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If the commissioner determines that a doula included on the registry does not meet the requirement in subdivision 2, clause (2), the commissioner shall notify the affected doula that the doula no longer meets the requirement in subdivision 2, clause (2), specify steps the doula must take to maintain inclusion on the registry, and specify the effect of failing to take such steps. The commissioner must provide this notice by first class mail to the address on file with the commissioner for the affected doula.</p>
          <p>(b) Following the provision of notice under paragraph (a), the commissioner shall remove from the registry any doula who no longer meets the requirement in subdivision 2, clause (2), and who does not take the steps specified by the commissioner to maintain inclusion on the registry.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.996.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.9.28.0">2007 c 147 art 9 s 28</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.4.24.0">2014 c 291 art 4 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/7/#laws.4.4.0">1Sp2021 c 7 art 4 s 4</a>-6</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.9965">
        <h1 class="shn">148.9965 DESIGNATION OF DOULA CERTIFICATION ORGANIZATIONS BY COMMISSIONER.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9965.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Review and designation by commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall periodically review the doula certification organizations listed in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.995">148.995, subdivision </a>2, or designated by the commissioner under this section. The commissioner may: (1) designate additional organizations from which individuals, if maintaining current doula certification from such an organization, are eligible for inclusion on the registry of certified doulas; and (2) remove the designation of a doula certification organization previously designated by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9965.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Designation.</span></h2>
          <p>A doula certification organization seeking designation under this section shall provide the commissioner with evidence that the organization satisfies designation criteria established by the commissioner. If the commissioner designates a doula certification organization under this section, the commissioner shall provide notice of the designation by publication in the State Register and on the Department of Health website for the registry of certified doulas and shall specify the date after which a certification by the organization authorizes a doula certified by the organization to be included on the registry.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9965.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Removal of designation.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner may remove the designation of a doula certification organization previously designated by the commissioner under this section upon a determination by the commissioner that the organization does not meet the commissioner's criteria for designation. If the commissioner removes a designation, the commissioner shall provide notice of the removal by publication in the State Register and shall specify the date after which a certification by the organization no longer authorizes a doula certified by the organization to be included on the registry.</p>
          <p>(b) Following removal of a designation, the Department of Health website for the registry of certified doulas shall be modified to reflect the removal.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.9965.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/7/#laws.4.7.0">1Sp2021 c 7 art 4 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.997">
        <h1 class="shn">148.997 FEES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.997.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Fees.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) The application fee is $185.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) The criminal background check fee is $15.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.997.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Nonrefundable fees.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The fees in this section are nonrefundable.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.997.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Deposit.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Fees received under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.995">148.995</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.997">148.997</a> shall be deposited in the state government special revenue fund.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.997.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.9.29.0">2007 c 147 art 9 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.10.121.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 10 s 121</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">BEHAVIOR ANALYSTS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.9981">
        <h1 class="shn">148.9981 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9981.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9981">148.9981</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9995">148.9995</a>, the terms in this section have the meanings given.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9981.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Accredited school or educational program.</span></h2>
          <p>"Accredited school or educational program" means a school, university, college, or other postsecondary education program that, at the time the student completes the program, is accredited by a regional accrediting association whose standards are substantially equivalent to those of the North Central Association of Colleges and Postsecondary Education Institutions or an accrediting association that evaluates schools of behavior analysis, psychology, or education for inclusion of the education, practicum, and core function standards.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9981.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Advisory council.</span></h2>
          <p>"Advisory council" means the Behavior Analyst Advisory Council established in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9994">148.9994</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9981.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Board.</span></h2>
          <p>"Board" means the Board of Psychology established in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.90">148.90</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9981.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Certifying entity.</span></h2>
          <p>"Certifying entity" means the Behavior Analyst Certification Board, Inc., or a successor organization or other organization approved by the board in consultation with the advisory council.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9981.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Client.</span></h2>
          <p>"Client" means an individual who is the recipient of behavior analysis services. Client also means "patient" as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291#stat.144.291.2">144.291, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (g).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9981.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Licensed behavior analyst.</span></h2>
          <p>"Licensed behavior analyst" or "behavior analyst" means an individual who holds a valid license issued under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9981">148.9981</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9995">148.9995 </a>to engage in the practice of applied behavior analysis.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9981.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Licensee.</span></h2>
          <p>"Licensee" means an individual who holds a valid license issued under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9981">148.9981</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9995">148.9995</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9981.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Practice of applied behavior analysis.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) "Practice of applied behavior analysis" means the design, implementation, and evaluation of social, instructional, and environmental modifications to produce socially significant improvements in human behavior. The practice of applied behavior analysis includes the empirical identification of functional relations between behavior and environmental factors, known as functional behavioral assessment and analysis. Applied behavior analysis interventions are based on scientific research, direct and indirect observation, and measurement of behavior and environment and utilize contextual factors, motivating operations, antecedent stimuli, positive reinforcement, and other procedures to help individuals develop new behaviors, increase or decrease existing behaviors, and emit behaviors under specific social, instructional, and environmental conditions.</p>
          <p>(b) The practice of applied behavior analysis does not include the diagnosis of psychiatric or mental health disorders, psychological testing, neuropsychology, psychotherapy, cognitive therapy, sex therapy, hypnotherapy, psychoanalysis, or psychological counseling.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.9981.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.19.1.0">2024 c 127 art 19 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.9982">
        <h1 class="shn">148.9982 DUTIES OF THE BOARD OF PSYCHOLOGY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9982.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">General.</span></h2>
          <p>The board, in consultation with the advisory council, must:</p>
          <p>(1) adopt and enforce standards for licensure, licensure renewal, and the regulation of behavior analysts;</p>
          <p>(2) issue licenses to qualified individuals under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9981">148.9981</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9995">148.9995</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) carry out disciplinary actions against licensed behavior analysts;</p>
          <p>(4) educate the public about the existence and content of the regulations for behavior analyst licensing to enable consumers to file complaints against licensees who may have violated laws or rules the board is empowered to enforce; and</p>
          <p>(5) collect license fees for behavior analysts as specified under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9995">148.9995</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9982.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Rulemaking.</span></h2>
          <p>The board, in consultation with the advisory council, may adopt rules necessary to carry out the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9981">148.9981</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9995">148.9995</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.9982.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.19.2.0">2024 c 127 art 19 s 2</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.9983">
        <h1 class="shn">148.9983 REQUIREMENTS FOR LICENSURE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9983.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">General.</span></h2>
          <p>An individual seeking licensure as a behavior analyst must complete and submit a written application on forms provided by the board together with the appropriate fee as specified under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9995">148.9995</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9983.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Requirements for licensure.</span></h2>
          <p>An applicant for licensure as a behavior analyst must submit evidence satisfactory to the board that the applicant:</p>
          <p>(1) has a current and active national certification as a board-certified behavior analyst issued by the certifying entity; or</p>
          <p>(2) has completed the equivalent requirements for certification by the certifying entity, including satisfactorily passing a psychometrically valid examination administered by a nationally accredited credentialing organization.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9983.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Background investigation.</span></h2>
          <p>The applicant must complete a background check pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.075">214.075</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.9983.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.19.3.0">2024 c 127 art 19 s 3</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.9984">
        <h1 class="shn">148.9984 LICENSE RENEWAL REQUIREMENTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9984.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Biennial renewal.</span></h2>
          <p>A license must be renewed every two years.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9984.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">License renewal notice.</span></h2>
          <p>At least 60 calendar days before the renewal deadline date, the board must mail a renewal notice to the licensee's last known address on file with the board. The notice must include instructions for accessing an online application for license renewal, the renewal deadline, and notice of fees required for renewal. The licensee's failure to receive notice does not relieve the licensee of the obligation to meet the renewal deadline and other requirements for license renewal.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9984.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Renewal requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) To renew a license, a licensee must submit to the board:</p>
          <p>(1) a completed and signed application for license renewal;</p>
          <p>(2) the license renewal fee as specified under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9995">148.9995</a>; and</p>
          <p>(3) evidence satisfactory to the board that the licensee holds a current and active national certification as a behavior analyst from the certifying entity or otherwise meets renewal requirements as established by the board, in consultation with the advisory council.</p>
          <p>(b) The application for license renewal and fee must be postmarked or received by the board by the end of the day on which the license expires or the following business day if the expiration date falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or holiday. A renewal application that is not completed and signed, or that is not accompanied by the correct fee, is void and must be returned to the licensee.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9984.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Pending renewal.</span></h2>
          <p>If a licensee's application for license renewal is postmarked or received by the board by the end of the business day on the expiration date of the license or the following business day if the expiration date falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or holiday, the licensee may continue to practice after the expiration date while the application for license renewal is pending with the board.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9984.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Late renewal fee.</span></h2>
          <p>If the application for license renewal is postmarked or received after the expiration date of the license or the following business day if the expiration date falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or holiday, the licensee must pay a biennial renewal late fee as specified by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9995">148.9995</a>, in addition to the renewal fee, before the licensee's application for license renewal will be considered by the board.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.9984.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.19.4.0">2024 c 127 art 19 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.9985">
        <h1 class="shn">148.9985 EXPIRED LICENSE.</h1>
        <p>(a) Within 30 days after the renewal date, a licensee who has not renewed their license must be notified by letter, sent to the last known address of the licensee in the board's file, that the renewal is overdue and that failure to pay the current fee and current biennial renewal late fee within 60 days after the renewal date will result in termination of the license.</p>
        <p>(b) The board must terminate the license of a licensee whose license renewal is at least 60 days overdue and to whom notification has been sent as provided in paragraph (a). Failure of a licensee to receive notification is not grounds for later challenge of the termination. The former licensee must be notified of the termination by letter within seven days after board action, in the same manner as provided in paragraph (a).</p>
        <p>(c) Notwithstanding paragraph (b), the board retains jurisdiction over a former licensee for complaints received after termination of a license regarding conduct that occurred during licensure.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.9985.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.19.5.0">2024 c 127 art 19 s 5</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.9986">
        <h1 class="shn">148.9986 PROHIBITED PRACTICE OR USE OF TITLES; PENALTY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9986.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Practice.</span></h2>
          <p>Effective January 1, 2025, an individual must not engage in the practice of applied behavior analysis unless the individual is licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9981">148.9981</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9995">148.9995</a> as a behavior analyst or is exempt under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9987">148.9987</a>. A psychologist licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.88">148.88</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.981">148.981</a> who practices behavior analysis is not required to obtain a license as a behavior analyst under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9981">148.9981</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9995">148.9995</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9986.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Use of titles.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An individual must not use a title incorporating the words "licensed behavior analyst," or "behavior analyst," or use any other title or description stating or implying that they are licensed or otherwise qualified to practice applied behavior analysis, unless that person holds a valid license under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9981">148.9981</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9995">148.9995</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) Notwithstanding paragraph (a), a licensed psychologist who practices applied behavior analysis within the psychologist's scope of practice may use the title "behavior analyst," but must not use the title "licensed behavior analyst" unless the licensed psychologist holds a valid license as a behavior analyst issued under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9981">148.9981</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9995">148.9995</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9986.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>An individual who violates this section is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.9986.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.19.6.0">2024 c 127 art 19 s 6</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.9987">
        <h1 class="shn">148.9987 EXCEPTIONS TO LICENSE REQUIREMENT.</h1>
        <p>(a) Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9981">148.9981</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9995">148.9995</a> must not be construed to prohibit or restrict:</p>
        <p>(1) the practice of an individual who is licensed to practice psychology in the state or an individual who is providing psychological services under the supervision of a licensed psychologist in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.925">148.925</a>;</p>
        <p>(2) the practice of any other profession or occupation licensed, certified, or registered by the state by an individual duly licensed, certified, or registered to practice the profession or occupation or to perform any act that falls within the scope of practice of the profession or occupation;</p>
        <p>(3) an individual who is employed by a school district from providing behavior analysis services as part of the individual's employment with the school district, so long as the individual does not provide behavior analysis services to any person or entity other than as an employee of the school district or accept remuneration for the provision of behavior analysis services outside of the individual's employment with the school district;</p>
        <p>(4) an employee of a program licensed under chapter 245D from providing the services described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245D.091#stat.245D.091.1">245D.091, subdivision 1</a>;</p>
        <p>(5) teaching behavior analysis or conducting behavior analysis research if the teaching or research does not involve the direct delivery of behavior analysis services;</p>
        <p>(6) providing behavior analysis services by an unlicensed supervisee or trainee under the authority and direction of a licensed behavior analyst and in compliance with the licensure and supervision standards required by law or rule;</p>
        <p>(7) a family member or guardian of the recipient of behavior analysis services from performing behavior analysis services under the authority and direction of a licensed behavior analyst; or</p>
        <p>(8) students or interns enrolled in an accredited school or educational program, or participating in a behavior analysis practicum, from engaging in the practice of applied behavior analysis while supervised by a licensed behavior analyst or instructor of an accredited school or educational program. These individuals must be designated as a behavior analyst student or intern.</p>
        <p>(b) Notwithstanding paragraph (a), a licensed psychologist may supervise an unlicensed supervisee, trainee, student, or intern who is engaged in the practice of behavior analysis if the supervision is authorized under the Minnesota Psychology Practice Act.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.9987.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.19.7.0">2024 c 127 art 19 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.9988">
        <h1 class="shn">148.9988 NONTRANSFERABILITY OF LICENSES.</h1>
        <p>A behavior analyst license is not transferable.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.9988.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.19.8.0">2024 c 127 art 19 s 8</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.9989">
        <h1 class="shn">148.9989 DUTY TO MAINTAIN CURRENT INFORMATION.</h1>
        <p>All licensees and applicants for licensure must notify the board within 30 days of the occurrence of:</p>
        <p>(1) a change of name, address, place of employment, or home or business telephone number; or</p>
        <p>(2) a change in any other application information.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.9989.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.19.9.0">2024 c 127 art 19 s 9</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.999">
        <h1 class="shn">148.999 DISCIPLINE; REPORTING.</h1>
        <p>For purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9981">148.9981</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9995">148.9995</a>, behavior analysts are subject to the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.941">148.941</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.952">148.952</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.965">148.965</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.98">148.98</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.999.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.19.10.0">2024 c 127 art 19 s 10</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.9991">
        <h1 class="shn">148.9991 COMPETENT PROVISION OF SERVICES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9991.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Limits on practice.</span></h2>
          <p>Behavior analysts must limit practice to the client populations and services for which the behavior analysts have competence or for which the behavior analysts are developing competence.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9991.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Developing competence.</span></h2>
          <p>When a behavior analyst is developing competence in a service, method, or procedure, or is developing competence to treat a specific client population, the behavior analyst must obtain professional education, training, continuing education, consultation, supervision or experience, or a combination thereof, necessary to demonstrate competence.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9991.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Limitations.</span></h2>
          <p>A behavior analyst must recognize the limitations to the scope of practice of applied behavior analysis. When the needs of a client appear to be outside the behavior analyst's scope of practice, the behavior analyst must inform the client that there may be other professional, technical, community, and administrative resources available to the client. A behavior analyst must assist with identifying resources when it is in the best interest of a client to be provided with alternative or complementary services.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9991.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Burden of proof.</span></h2>
          <p>Whenever a complaint is submitted to the board involving a violation of this section, the burden of proof is on the behavior analyst to demonstrate that the elements of competence have been reasonably met.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.9991.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.19.11.0">2024 c 127 art 19 s 11</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.9992">
        <h1 class="shn">148.9992 DUTY TO WARN; LIMITATION ON LIABILITY; VIOLENT BEHAVIOR OF PATIENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9992.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For the purposes of this section, the terms in this subdivision have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Other person" means an immediate family member or someone who personally knows the client and has reason to believe the client is capable of and will carry out a serious, specific threat of harm to a specific, clearly identified or identifiable victim.</p>
          <p>(c) "Reasonable efforts" means communicating a serious, specific threat to the potential victim and, if unable to make contact with the potential victim, communicating the serious, specific threat to the law enforcement agency closest to the potential victim or the client.</p>
          <p>(d) "Licensee" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9981">148.9981</a> and includes behavior analysis students, interns, and unlicensed supervisees who are participating in a behavior analysis practicum or enrolled in an accredited school or educational program.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9992.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Duty to warn.</span></h2>
          <p>The duty to predict, warn of, or take reasonable precautions to provide protection from violent behavior arises only when a client or other person has communicated to the licensee a specific, serious threat of physical violence against a specific, clearly identified or identifiable potential victim. If a duty to warn arises, the duty is discharged by the licensee if reasonable efforts are made to communicate the threat.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9992.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Liability standard.</span></h2>
          <p>If no duty to warn exists under subdivision 2, then no monetary liability and no cause of action may arise against a licensee for failure to predict, warn of, or take reasonable precautions to provide protection from a client's violent behavior.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9992.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Disclosure of confidences.</span></h2>
          <p>Good faith compliance with the duty to warn must not constitute a breach of confidence and must not result in monetary liability or a cause of action against the licensee.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9992.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Continuity of care.</span></h2>
          <p>Subdivision 2 must not be construed to authorize a licensee to terminate treatment of a client as a direct result of a client's violent behavior or threat of physical violence unless the client is referred to another practitioner or appropriate health care facility.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9992.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Exception.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not apply to a threat to commit suicide or other threats by a client to harm the client, or to a threat by a client who is adjudicated as a person who has a mental illness and is dangerous to the public under chapter 253B.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9992.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Optional disclosure.</span></h2>
          <p>This section must not be construed to prohibit a licensee from disclosing confidences to third parties in a good faith effort to warn or take precautions against a client's violent behavior or threat to commit suicide for which a duty to warn does not arise.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9992.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Limitation on liability.</span></h2>
          <p>No monetary liability and no cause of action or disciplinary action by the board may arise against a licensee for disclosure of confidences to third parties, for failure to disclose confidences to third parties, or for erroneous disclosure of confidences to third parties in a good faith effort to warn against or take precautions against a client's violent behavior or threat of suicide for which a duty to warn does not arise.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.9992.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.19.12.0">2024 c 127 art 19 s 12</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.9993">
        <h1 class="shn">148.9993 INFORMED CONSENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9993.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Obtaining informed consent for services.</span></h2>
          <p>A behavior analyst must obtain informed consent from the client or the client's legal guardian before initiating services. The informed consent must be in writing, signed by the client, and include, at a minimum, the following:</p>
          <p>(1) consent for the behavior analyst to engage in activities that directly affect the client;</p>
          <p>(2) the goals, purposes, and procedures of the proposed services;</p>
          <p>(3) the factors that may impact the duration of the proposed services;</p>
          <p>(4) the applicable fee schedule for the proposed services;</p>
          <p>(5) the significant risks and benefits of the proposed services;</p>
          <p>(6) the behavior analyst's limits under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9991">148.9991</a>, including, if applicable, information that the behavior analyst is developing competence in the proposed service, method, or procedure, and alternatives to the proposed service, if any; and</p>
          <p>(7) the behavior analyst's responsibilities if the client terminates the service.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9993.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Updating informed consent.</span></h2>
          <p>If there is a substantial change in the nature or purpose of a service, the behavior analyst must obtain a new informed consent from the client.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9993.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Emergency or crisis services.</span></h2>
          <p>Informed consent is not required when a behavior analyst is providing emergency or crisis services. If services continue after the emergency or crisis has abated, informed consent must be obtained.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.9993.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.19.13.0">2024 c 127 art 19 s 13</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.9994">
        <h1 class="shn">148.9994 BEHAVIOR ANALYST ADVISORY COUNCIL.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9994.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Membership.</span></h2>
          <p>The Behavior Analyst Advisory Council is created and composed of five members appointed by the board. The advisory council consists of:</p>
          <p>(1) one public member as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.02">214.02</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) three members who are licensed behavior analysts; and</p>
          <p>(3) one member who is a licensed psychologist and, to the extent practicable, who practices applied behavior analysis.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9994.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Administration.</span></h2>
          <p>The advisory council is established and administered under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/15.059">15.059</a>, except that the advisory council does not expire.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9994.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Duties.</span></h2>
          <p>The advisory council must:</p>
          <p>(1) advise the board regarding standards for behavior analysts;</p>
          <p>(2) assist with the distribution of information regarding behavior analyst standards;</p>
          <p>(3) advise the board on enforcement of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9981">148.9981</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.9995">148.9995</a>;</p>
          <p>(4) review license applications and license renewal applications and make recommendations to the board;</p>
          <p>(5) review complaints and complaint investigation reports and make recommendations to the board on whether disciplinary action should be taken and, if applicable, what type;</p>
          <p>(6) advise the board regarding evaluation and treatment protocols; and</p>
          <p>(7) perform other duties authorized for advisory councils under chapter <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214">214</a> as directed by the board to ensure effective oversight of behavior analysts.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.9994.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.19.14.0">2024 c 127 art 19 s 14</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.148.9995">
        <h1 class="shn">148.9995 FEES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9995.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Fees.</span></h2>
          <p>All applicants and licensees must pay fees as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) application fee, $225;</p>
          <p>(2) license renewal fee, $225;</p>
          <p>(3) inactive license renewal fee, $125;</p>
          <p>(4) biennial renewal late fee, $100;</p>
          <p>(5) inactive license renewal late fee, $100; and</p>
          <p>(6) supervisor application processing fee, $225.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9995.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Nonrefundable fees.</span></h2>
          <p>All fees in this section are nonrefundable.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.148.9995.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Deposit of fees.</span></h2>
          <p>Fees collected by the board under this section must be deposited in the state government special revenue fund.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.148.9995.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.19.15.0">2024 c 127 art 19 s 15</a>
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
